8:1: Al-Bukhari said: Ibn Abbas said: The spoils of war are the spoils of war. Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim told us, Saeed bin Sulaiman told us, Hisham told us, Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Surat Al-Anfal. He said: It was revealed at Badr. As for what he related on the authority of Ibn Abbas, it was also narrated by Ali bin Abi Talhah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The spoils of war are the spoils of war. They were exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and no one else had a share of them. And this is what Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ata, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ata Al-Khurasani, Muqatil bin Hayyan, Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam, and more than one said, that they are the spoils of war. Al-Kalbi said, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: The spoils of war are the spoils of war. Labid said about it: Fearing our Lord is the best voluntary act, and God willing, I will be patient and hasten. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Malik ibn Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: I heard a man asking Ibn Abbas about the spoils of war, and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The horse is from the spoils of war and the spoils of war are from the spoils of war. Then he returned to his question and Ibn Abbas said that too. Then the man said: What are the spoils of war that God said in His Book? Al-Qasim said: He kept asking him until he almost made him embarrassed. Then Ibn Abbas said: Do you know what is like this, like Subaygh who was struck by Umar ibn Al-Khattab? And Abd Al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: Ibn Abbas said: When Umar ibn Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, was asked about something, he would say: I neither command you nor forbid you. Then Ibn Abbas said: By God, God did not send His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, except as a forbidding, commanding, permitting and forbidding. Al-Qasim said: A man was sent to Ibn Abbas and he asked him about the spoils of war. Ibn Abbas said: A man would give away another man’s horse and weapon as spoils of war. The man repeated the same thing to him, then he repeated it to him until he angered him. Ibn Abbas said: Do you know what is like this? It is like Subaygh, whom Umar ibn al-Khattab beat until blood flowed down his heels or feet. The man said: As for you, God has avenged Umar from you. This is a sound chain of transmission to Ibn Abbas, that he interpreted the spoils of war as what the imam gives away to some people from spoils or the like after dividing the original spoils of war, which is what many jurists understand from the word spoils of war. And God knows best. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: They asked the Messenger of God (peace be upon him) about the fifth after the four of the fifths, so the verse They ask you about the spoils of war was revealed. Ibn Mas’ud and Masruq said: There is no voluntary charity on the day of battle, rather the voluntary charity is before the ranks meet. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on their authority. Ibn al-Mubarak and others said on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah regarding the verse They ask you about the spoils of war he said they ask you about what the polytheists have strayed from to the Muslims other than in combat, from an animal or a male or female slave or goods, so it is voluntary charity for the Prophet (peace be upon him) to do with as he wishes. This necessitates that he interpreted the spoils of war as the booty, which is what is taken from the infidels without fighting. Ibn Jarir said: Others said: They are the spoils of war by raiding parties. Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Ali bin Salih bin Hayy told us, he said it reached me in the words of God the Almighty: They ask you about the spoils of war he said the raiding parties, and the meaning of this is what the Imam gives as a voluntary charity to some of the raiding parties in addition to their division with the rest of the army. Al-Sha’bi stated this, and Ibn Jarir chose that it was an addition to the oath. This is supported by what was reported regarding the reason for the revelation of the verse, which is what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, Abu Ishaq al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ubayd God al-Thaqafi, on the authority of Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: When the day of Badr came and my brother Umair was killed, I killed Sa’id ibn al-’As and took his sword, and he was called Dhu al-Katifah. I brought it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Go and throw it in the fist. He said: So I returned with what only God knows about me, who killed my brother and took my spoils. He said: I had not gone far until Surat al-Anfal was revealed, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Go and take your spoils. Imam Ahmad also said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Asim bin Abi Al-Najoud, on the authority of Mus`ab bin Sa`d, on the authority of Sa`d bin Malik, who said: I said, O Messenger of God, God has cured me today of the polytheists, so give me this sword. He said, This sword is neither for you nor for me, put it down. So I put it down, then I went back and said, Perhaps this sword will be given to someone who will not suffer as I have suffered. Then a man called me from behind me and said, I said, ‘Has God revealed something about me?’ He said, You asked me for the sword, but it was not mine, and it has been given to me, so it is yours. He said, “Then God revealed this verse, ‘They ask you about the spoils of war. Say, “The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.”’” It was narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, and Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. This is how Abu Dawud At-Tayalisi narrated it. Shu’bah told us, Samak bin Harb told us, he heard Mus’ab bin Sa’d narrating on the authority of Sa’d, he said: It was revealed about four verses. I obtained a sword on the day of Badr, so I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Give it to me as a gift. He said: Put it down from where you took it, twice, then I went back to him and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Put it down from where you took it. Then this verse was revealed: They ask you about the spoils of war, the verse and the rest of the hadith, about the revelation of: And We have enjoined upon man, to be good to his parents, and the words of God Almighty: Intoxicants and gambling, and the verse of the will. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih on the authority of Shu’bah, and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Abdullah bin Abi Bakr told me on the authority of some of Banu Sa’idah, he said: I heard Abu Asid Malik bin Rabi’ah say: I obtained the sword of Ibn A’idh on the day of Badr, and the sword was called Al-Marzban, so when he ordered… The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked the people to return what they had in their hands of voluntary charity. I brought it and threw it in the voluntary charity. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not refuse anything that anyone asked for. Al-Arqam bin Abi Al-Arqam Al-Makhzumi saw him, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked him and he gave it to him. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another source. Another reason for the revelation of the verse Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: I asked Ubadah about the spoils of war, and he said: We were the companions of Badr. It was revealed when we disagreed about the voluntary spoils of war and our morals deteriorated, so God took it from our hands and gave it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muslims. On the authority of Buwa’a, he said on the authority of Equally. Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Muawiyah bin Omar told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin al-Harith bin Abdullah bin Ayyash bin Abi Rabia, on the authority of Sulayman bin Musa, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Umamah, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I witnessed Badr with him. The people met, and God, the Most High, defeated the enemy. A group set out in their tracks, defeating and killing them, and a group approached the army, seizing and gathering it, and a group surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so that the enemy would not be taken by surprise. When night fell, the people returned to each other. Those who had gathered the spoils said: We have taken them, so no one has a share in them. Those who went out in pursuit of the enemy said: You are not more deserving of them than we are. We prevented the enemy from reaching them and defeated them. Those who surrounded the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We feared that the enemy would take him by surprise, so we occupied ourselves with him. Then the verse was revealed: “They ask you about the spoils. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and amend your affairs.” Between you, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided it among the Muslims. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raided the land of the enemy, he gave a quarter as a gift, and when he returned, he gave a third as a gift. He disliked spoils of war. Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan al-Thawri from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, with a similar wording. Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a good hadith. Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith. Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is sound according to the conditions of Muslim, but they did not include it. Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, and the wording is his. Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim narrated it from various chains of transmission on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever does such and such will have such and such. The young men of the people rushed to do so, while the elders remained under the banners. When the spoils came, they came seeking what had been given to them, and the elders said: Do not monopolize us, for we would have been a support for you. If you were to flee, you would have come to us. They disputed, so God Almighty revealed: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say, ‘The spoils belong to God and the Messenger. So fear God and set things right between you and obey God and His Messenger, if you are believers.’” Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-Kalbi on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever kills a person will have such and such, and whoever takes a prisoner will have such and such. Abu Al-Yusr came with two prisoners and said: O Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, you promised us. Saad bin Ubadah stood up and said: O Messenger of God, if you had given these, nothing would have remained for your companions. It was not a lack of reward that prevented us from doing this, nor was it cowardice in the face of the enemy. Rather, we stood up in this position to protect you, fearing that they might come from behind you. They quarrelled and the Qur’an was revealed: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.” He said: And the Qur’an was revealed: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God. to the end of the verse. Imam Abu Ubaidullah Al-Qasim bin Salam, may God have mercy on him, said in the Book of Legal Money and Explanation of Its Directions and Disbursements: As for the spoils of war, they are the spoils and all the gains that the Muslims obtained from the money of the people of war. The first spoils of war were for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty says: “They ask you about the spoils of war. Say: The spoils belong to God and the Messenger.” So he divided them on the day of Badr according to what God showed him, without dividing them into fifths as we mentioned in the hadith of Saad. Then it was revealed after That is the verse of the fifth, so the first was abrogated. I said: This is how Ali bin Abi Talha narrated it from Ibn Abbas, and Mujahid, Ikrimah and As-Suddi said the same. Ibn Zayd said: It is not abrogated, rather it is decisive. Abu Ubaid said: And there are traces of that. The origin of the spoils of war is the sum of the spoils of war, except that the fifth of it is specific to its people according to what was revealed in the Book and the Sunnah. The meaning of the spoils of war in the speech of the Arabs is every good deed done by an agent as a favor, without it being obligatory upon him. So that is the voluntary gift that God made permissible for the believers from the wealth of their enemy. Rather, it is something that God made specific to them out of His generosity towards them after the spoils of war were forbidden to the nations before them, so God made it permissible for this nation. This is the origin of the voluntary gift. I said: The evidence for this is what is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been given five things that were not given to anyone before me - and he mentioned the hadith until he said - and the spoils of war were made permissible for me, but were not made permissible for anyone before me.” He mentioned the entire hadith, then Abu Ubaid said: This is why he called what the Imam gave to the fighters a voluntary gift, which is his preference of some of the army over others with something other than their arrows, he does that to them according to the extent of their ability to suffice for Islam and to harm the enemy, and in the voluntary gift that the Imam gives, there are four Sunnahs, each of which has a place other than the place of the other one of them in the voluntary gift, there is no fifth in it, and that is the plunder, and the second is the voluntary gift that comes from the spoils after taking out the fifth, which is that the Imam directs the raiding parties in the land of war, so they bring back the spoils, so the raiding party gets a quarter or a third of what they bring after the fifth, and the third in the voluntary gift from the fifth itself, which is that the entire spoils are seized, then divided into fifths, and when the fifth is in the hands of the Imam, he gives it as a voluntary gift according to what he sees fit. and the fourth in the voluntary gift in the total spoils before any of it is divided into fifths, which is that he gives to the guides, the shepherds of the livestock, and the drivers of the livestock. And in all of that there is a difference. Al-Rabi’ said: Al-Shafi’i said: The spoils of war are that nothing is taken from the head of the spoils before the fifth other than the booty. Abu Ubaid said: The second aspect of the voluntary war is something that they increase other than what was theirs, and that is from the fifth of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for he has a fifth of the fifth of every spoil, so the Imam should strive hard, and if the enemy is numerous and their strength is strong and the number of Muslims facing him is few, he should give a voluntary war from it in accordance with the Sunnah of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and if that is not the case, he should not give a voluntary war. The third aspect of the voluntary war is if the Imam sends out a detachment or an army and says to them before the encounter, whoever takes anything, it is his, after the fifth, it is theirs according to what the Imam stipulated, because they fought on that basis and were satisfied with it. His words end. And what preceded from his words, which is his saying: The spoils of Badr were not given a fifth, is considered. The hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib, regarding the two sides that he obtained from the fifth on the day of Badr, is refuted by it, and I have explained that in the Book of the Seerah in a clear explanation, and praise and thanks be to God. And the Almighty’s saying: So fear God and amend that which is between you means fear God in your affairs and amend that which is between you and do not wrong one another and do not quarrel and do not quarrel, for what God has given you of guidance and knowledge is better than what you quarrel about. And obey God and His Messenger meaning in His division among you according to what God wants, for He only divides it as God has commanded Him of justice and fairness. Ibn Abbas said: This is an exhortation from God and His Messenger to fear God and amend that which is between you, and Mujahid said the same. Al-Suddi said: So fear God and amend that which is between you meaning do not quarrel. Let us mention here a hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Ahmad bin Ali bin Al-Muthanna Al-Mawsili, may God have mercy on him, in his Musnad. He said: Mujahid bin Musa told us, Abdullah bin Bakr told us, Ibad bin Shaiba Al-Habti told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: While the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, we saw him laughing until his front teeth were visible. Umar said: What made you laugh, O Messenger of God, may my father and mother be sacrificed for you? He said: Two men from my nation knelt before the Lord of Glory, Blessed and Exalted be He. One of them said: O Lord, take my grievance from my brother. God Almighty said: Give your brother his grievance. He said: O Lord, nothing remains of my good deeds. He said: O Lord, let him bear some of my burdens. He said: The eyes of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, overflowed with tears, and then he said: “That is a great day, a day when people will need someone to bear their burdens. God, the Most High, said to the seeker: ‘Raise your eyes and look at the gardens.’ He raised his head and said: ‘O Lord, I see cities of silver and palaces of gold crowned with pearls. Which prophet is this? Which friend is this? Which martyr is this?’ He said: ‘This is for the one who gave its price.’ He said: ‘O Lord, and who owns its price?’ He said: ‘You own it.’ He said: ‘What, O Lord?’ He said: ‘Do you pardon your brother?’ He said: ‘O Lord, I have pardoned him.’ God, the Most High, said: ‘Take your brother by the hand and enter Paradise.’” Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: So fear God and reconcile your differences, for God, the Most High, will reconcile the believers on the Day of Resurrection.
8:2: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: The hypocrites do not have any remembrance of God in their hearts when performing His obligations. They do not believe in any of God's verses, nor do they trust in God, nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat on their wealth. So God the Most High informed us that they are not believers, then God described the believers and said, The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, so they performed His obligations, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, meaning it increases their belief, and upon their Lord they rely, meaning they do not hope for anyone other than Him. Mujahid said, And their hearts were terrified, meaning they were frightened and afraid. As-Suddi and others said the same. This is the description of the true believer, who, when God is mentioned, his heart is fearful, meaning he fears Him, so he does what He commands and abandons what He forbids, like the saying of God the Almighty: “And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except God - and do not persist in what they have done while they know.” And like the saying of God the Almighty: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination, then Paradise will be the refuge. For this reason, Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: I heard As-Suddi say regarding the saying of God the Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: He is the man who wants to wrong or he said he is about to commit a sin, so it is said to him: Fear God, and his heart becomes fearful. Ath-Thawri also said on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab on the authority of Umm Ad-Darda’ regarding the saying of God the Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: Fear in the heart is like the burning of a palm branch. Do you not find it trembling? He said: Yes. She said: If you find that, then supplicate to God at that time, for supplication removes that. His statement, And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, is like His statement, And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ But as for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice. Al-Bukhari and other imams have used this verse and similar verses as evidence for the increase of faith and its distinction in the hearts, as is the doctrine of the majority of the nation. In fact, more than one imam has reported consensus on it, such as Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Ubaid, as we have explained in detail at the beginning of the commentary on Al-Bukhari. Praise and thanks be to God. And upon their Lord they rely means they do not hope for anyone other than Him, and they do not intend anyone other than Him, and they do not seek refuge except in His presence, and they do not seek their needs except from Him, and they do not desire anyone other than Him, and they know that whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be, and that He is the One who controls the kingdom, He alone has no partner and no one can question His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. For this reason, Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Trusting in God is the sum of faith. And His statement, Those who establish prayer and spend from what We have provided for them, God the Almighty draws attention to their deeds after mentioning their belief, and these deeds include all types of good, which is establishing prayer, which is the right of God the Almighty. Qatada said: Establishing prayer means maintaining its times, performing ablution, bowing, and prostrating. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Establishing it means maintaining its times, performing ablution properly, completing its bowing and prostrating, reciting the Qur’an in it, the testimony of faith, and sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), this is establishing it. Spending from what God has provided for them includes paying zakat and all other rights of the servants, whether obligatory or recommended. All of creation is God’s dependents, so the most beloved of them to God is the one who is most beneficial to His creation. Qatada said about His statement, and from what We have provided for them they spend, “So spend from what God has provided for you, for this wealth is a loan and a trust with you, O son of Adam, and you are about to part with it.” And His statement, Those are the true believers, meaning those who are described by these qualities are the true believers. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid Al-Sakaski, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Al-Jahm, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Malik Al-Ansari, that he passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: How are you this morning, O Harith? He said: I have become a true believer. He said: Pay attention to what you say, for everything has a reality, so what is the reality of your faith? He said: “I have turned away from the world, so I have stayed up all night and been thirsty during the day, and it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord appearing, and it is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise visiting one another in it, and it is as if I am looking at the people of Hell crushing themselves in it.” He said: O Harith, you have known, so adhere to it, three times. Amr bin Murrah said about God’s statement, Those are the true believers, that the Qur’an was revealed in the Arabic language, like you say, So-and-so is a true master, and There are masters among the people. So-and-so is truly a merchant, and there are merchants among the people. So-and-so is truly a poet, and there are poets among the people. His statement, For them are degrees with their Lord, means homes, stations, and degrees in Paradise, as God the Almighty said, They are degrees with God, and God is Seeing of what they do. “And forgiveness,” meaning He forgives them their sins and appreciates their good deeds. Ad-Dahhak said about His statement, For them are degrees with their Lord, that the people of Paradise are above one another, so the one who is above will see his superiority over the one who is below him, and the one who is below him will not see that anyone is superior to him. For this reason, it was reported in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The people of ‘Illiyyin will be seen by those below them just as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky. They said, O Messenger of God, those are the homes of the prophets, and no one else will attain them. He said, Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are men who believed in God and believed in the Messengers. In another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah from the hadith of Abu Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abi Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will see the people of the highest ranks as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky, and Abu Bakr and Umar are among them and are blessed.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Establishing it means maintaining its times, performing ablution properly, completing its bowing and prostrating, reciting the Qur’an in it, the testimony of faith, and sending blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), this is establishing it. Spending from what God has provided for them includes paying zakat and all other rights of the servants, whether obligatory or recommended. All of creation is God’s dependents, so the most beloved of them to God is the one who is most beneficial to His creation. Qatada said about His statement, and from what We have provided for them they spend, “So spend from what God has provided for you, for this wealth is a loan and a trust with you, O son of Adam, and you are about to part with it.” And His statement, Those are the true believers, meaning those who are described by these qualities are the true believers. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami told us, Abu Kurayb told us, Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Yazid Al-Sakaski, on the authority of Saeed bin Abi Hilal, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abi Al-Jahm, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Malik Al-Ansari, that he passed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said to him: How are you this morning, O Harith? He said: I have become a true believer. He said: Pay attention to what you say, for everything has a reality, so what is the reality of your faith? He said: “I have turned away from the world, so I have stayed up all night and been thirsty during the day, and it is as if I am looking at the Throne of my Lord appearing, and it is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise visiting one another in it, and it is as if I am looking at the people of Hell crushing themselves in it.” He said: O Harith, you have known, so adhere to it, three times. Amr bin Murrah said about God’s statement, Those are the true believers, that the Qur’an was revealed in the Arabic language, like you say, So-and-so is a true master, and There are masters among the people. So-and-so is truly a merchant, and there are merchants among the people. So-and-so is truly a poet, and there are poets among the people. His statement, For them are degrees with their Lord, means homes, stations, and degrees in Paradise, as God the Almighty said, They are degrees with God, and God is Seeing of what they do. “And forgiveness,” meaning He forgives them their sins and appreciates their good deeds. Ad-Dahhak said about His statement, For them are degrees with their Lord, that the people of Paradise are above one another, so the one who is above will see his superiority over the one who is below him, and the one who is below him will not see that anyone is superior to him. For this reason, it was reported in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, The people of ‘Illiyyin will be seen by those below them just as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky. They said, O Messenger of God, those are the homes of the prophets, and no one else will attain them. He said, Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are men who believed in God and believed in the Messengers. In another hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad and the people of Sunnah from the hadith of Abu Atiyah on the authority of Ibn Abi Saeed, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will see the people of the highest ranks as you see a distant star in the horizon of the sky, and Abu Bakr and Umar are among them and are blessed.
8:4: Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement, The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: The hypocrites do not have any remembrance of God in their hearts when performing His obligations. They do not believe in any of God's verses, nor do they trust in God, nor do they pray when they are absent, nor do they pay the zakat on their wealth. So God the Most High informed us that they are not believers, then God described the believers and said, The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful, so they performed His obligations, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, meaning it increases their belief, and upon their Lord they rely, meaning they do not hope for anyone other than Him. Mujahid said, And their hearts were terrified, meaning they were frightened and afraid. As-Suddi and others said the same. This is the description of the true believer, who, when God is mentioned, his heart is fearful, meaning he fears Him, so he does what He commands and abandons what He forbids, like the saying of God the Almighty: “And those who, when they have committed an immorality or wronged themselves, remember God and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except God - and do not persist in what they have done while they know.” And like the saying of God the Almighty: But as for he who feared the position of his Lord and prevented the soul from [unlawful] inclination, then Paradise will be the refuge. For this reason, Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: I heard As-Suddi say regarding the saying of God the Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: He is the man who wants to wrong or he said he is about to commit a sin, so it is said to him: Fear God, and his heart becomes fearful. Ath-Thawri also said on the authority of Abdullah bin Uthman bin Khathim on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab on the authority of Umm Ad-Darda’ regarding the saying of God the Almighty: The believers are only those who, when God is mentioned, their hearts become fearful. He said: Fear in the heart is like the burning of a palm branch. Do you not find it trembling? He said: Yes. She said: If you find that, then supplicate to God at that time, for supplication removes that. His statement, And when His verses are recited to them, it increases their faith, is like His statement, And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ But as for those who believe, it increases them in faith, and they rejoice. Al-Bukhari and other imams have used this verse and similar verses as evidence for the increase of faith and its distinction in the hearts, as is the doctrine of the majority of the nation. In fact, more than one imam has reported consensus on it, such as Al-Shafi’i, Ahmad ibn Hanbal, and Abu Ubaid, as we have explained in detail at the beginning of the commentary on Al-Bukhari. Praise and thanks be to God. And upon their Lord they rely means they do not hope for anyone other than Him, and they do not intend anyone other than Him, and they do not seek refuge except in His presence, and they do not seek their needs except from Him, and they do not desire anyone other than Him, and they know that whatever He wills will be, and whatever He does not will will not be, and that He is the One who controls the kingdom, He alone has no partner and no one can question His judgment, and He is swift in reckoning. For this reason, Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: Trusting in God is the sum of faith. 8:5: Imam Abu Jaafar al-Tabari said: The commentators differed about the reason for bringing this kaf in His statement, As your Lord brought you out, some of them said that it was likened to the righteousness of the believers, their fear of their Lord, their reconciliation between them, and their obedience to God and His Messenger. Then it was narrated from Ikrimah something similar to this, and the meaning of this is that God Almighty says, just as when you differed over the spoils and quarrelled over them, God took them from you and made them His portion, and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, divided them justly and equally, so this was the complete interest for you. Likewise, when you hated to go out to the enemies to fight those with power, and they were the mobilization who went out to support their religion and protect their caravan, so the consequence of your hatred of fighting was that He decreed for you and brought you and your enemy together without an appointment, with guidance and direction, victory and conquest, as God Almighty said: "Fighting is prescribed for you while it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you, and perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you. And God is Knowing and Knowing." He knows, and you do not know. Ibn Jarir said: And others said that the meaning of this is just as your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, against the will of a group of believers, so they are averse to fighting, so they argue with you about it after it became clear to them. Then it was narrated from Mujahid something similar that he said just as your Lord brought you out, he said, likewise they argue with you about the truth. Al-Suddi said: God revealed about his going out to Badr and their arguing with him, so He said, just as your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, and a group of the believers were averse, to the polytheists’ request, arguing with you about the truth after it became clear. And some of them said, “They ask you about the spoils of war, arguing with you about the spoils of war, just as they argued with you on the day of Badr, so they said, ‘You brought us out for the caravan and you did not teach us fighting, so we could prepare for it.’” I said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only left Medina in pursuit of Abu Sufyan’s caravan, which he had heard was coming from Syria and containing abundant wealth for the Quraysh. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mobilized the Muslims who were light among them, so he went out with three hundred and a few men, and sought the coast from the road to Badr. Abu Sufyan learned of the Messenger of God’s, may God bless him and grant him peace, departure in pursuit of him, so he sent Damdam bin Amr as a warner to the people of Mecca, so they set out with nearly a thousand masked men, between nine hundred and a thousand. Abu Sufyan headed the caravan to the right of the seashore, so it escaped, and the mobilization came, so they arrived at the water of Badr. God gathered the Muslims and the infidels without an appointment, for God Almighty wants to raise the word of the Muslims and grant them victory over their enemy and to differentiate between truth and falsehood, as will be explained. The purpose is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard the report of the mobilization, God revealed to him that he should prepare one of the two groups, either the caravan or the mobilization. Many Muslims desired the caravan because it was a gain without fighting, as God Almighty said: And you wish that you should have nothing but power, but God wants that you should have nothing but power. He establishes the truth with His words and cuts off the roots of the disbelievers. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said in his interpretation: Sulayman bin Ahmad al-Tabarani told us, Bakr bin Sahl told us, Abdullah bin Yusuf told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Habib, on the authority of Aslam Abu Imran, who told him that he heard Abu Ayyub al-Ansari say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said while we were in Medina: “I have been informed that the caravan of Abu Sufyan is coming. Would you like us to go out before this caravan, perhaps God will grant us booty?” We said: Yes. So he went out and we went out. When we had traveled for a day or two, he said to us: What do you think about fighting the people, for they have been informed of your departure? We said: No, by God, we do not have the strength to fight the enemy, but we wanted the caravan. Then he said: What do you think about fighting the people? So we said the same thing, and Al-Miqdad bin Amr said: Then we will not say to you, O Messenger of God, as the people of Moses said to Moses: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” He said: We, the Ansar, wished that if we said as Al-Miqdad said, it would be more beloved to us than having a great deal of wealth. He said: So God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace: Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with the truth, although a party of the believers were averse. He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Lahi’ah in a similar manner. Ibn Mardawayh also narrated from the hadith of Muhammad bin Amr bin Alqamah bin Abi Waqqas Al-Laythi, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Badr, and when he was at Ar-Rawha’, he addressed the people and said: What do you think? Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, we have been informed that they are in such and such a place. He said: Then he addressed the people and said: What do you think? Umar said the same as Abu Bakr, then he addressed the people and said: What do you think? Sa’d bin Mu’adh said: O Messenger of God, do you mean us?” By the One Who honored you and sent down the Book to you, I have never walked it, nor do I have any knowledge of it. If you go until you reach Bark al-Ghamad in Dhi Yaman, we will go with you, and we will not be like those who said to Moses, “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting right here.” Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. Perhaps you have gone out for a matter and God has revealed something else to you. So look at what God has revealed to you and go for it. Separate the ropes of whomever you wish, cut the ropes of whomever you wish, oppose whomever you wish, make peace with whomever you wish, and take from our wealth whatever you wish. So the Qur’an was revealed based on the words of Sa’d, Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, although a party of the believers were averse. Al-A’wfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, when he consulted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about meeting the enemy, and Sa’d ibn Ubadah said to him what he said, and that was on the day of Badr, he commanded the people to prepare for battle and commanded them to use force. The people of faith disliked that, so God revealed, Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, although a party of the believers were averse. They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on. Mujahid said, They argue with you about the truth means in fighting. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, They argue with you about the truth means hatred for meeting the polytheists, and denial of the march of Quraysh when they mentioned it to them. Al-Suddi said, They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear means after it has become clear to them that you will only do what God has commanded you to do. Ibn Jarir said, and others said that he meant the polytheists. Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God the Almighty, They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on, these polytheists said, they argued with him about the truth as if they were being driven to death when they were called to Islam while they were looking on. He said, This is not a description of the others; this is a description that has been introduced for the people of disbelief. Then Ibn Jarir said, There is no meaning to what he said, because what preceded his saying, “They argue with you about the truth is report about the people of faith, and what follows it is report about them.” The correct statement is that of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Ishaq: that it is a report from the believers. This which Ibn Jarir supported is the truth and is what the context of the speech indicates, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Bakir and Abd al-Razzaq told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he finished with Badr: Go with the caravan, there is nothing beyond it. Al-Abbas bin Abd al-Muttalib called out to him. Abd al-Razzaq said while he was a prisoner in his chains: He is not suitable for you. He said: Why? He said: Because God, the Almighty, promised you only one of the two groups, and God has given you what He promised you with a good chain of transmission and has not included it. The meaning of His, the Almighty, saying: And you would like that the one without power should be yours means that they would like the group that has no limits, no strength, and no fighting to be theirs, which is the caravan. And God wants to establish the truth with His words means that He wants to unite you with the group that has power and fighting, so that He may make you victorious over them and support you against them, and make His religion prevail and raise the word of Islam and make it victorious over religions. He is the most knowledgeable about the consequences of things, and He is the One who manages you with His good management, even if the servants like the opposite of that in what appears to them, like His, the Almighty’s, saying: “Fighting has been prescribed for you, although it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you. And perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas. Each of them narrated to me some of this hadith, and it came together. Their hadith in what I have cited from the hadith of Badr, they said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of Abu Sufyan coming from Syria, he summoned the Muslims to them and said: ‘This is the caravan of Quraysh with their wealth in it, so go out to it, perhaps God will grant you some of it.’ So the people volunteered, some of them lightly and some of them were heavy, because they did not think that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would encounter war. Abu Sufyan had been mobilized when he approached the Hijaz, spying on the report and asking whomever he met of the caravans, fearing for the people’s situation, until he received report from some of the caravans that Muhammad had mobilized his companions for you and your caravan. So he was cautious and hired Damdam bin Amr al-Ghifari and sent him to the people of Mecca and ordered him to go to Quraysh and summon them to their wealth and inform them that Muhammad had attacked it with his companions. So Damdam bin Amr went out quickly to Mecca, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions until he reached a valley called Dhafran, and he went out from it until he was in some of it, and the report came to him from Quraysh about their march to prevent it.” He reproached them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people and told them about the Quraysh. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, and he did well. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, and he did well. Then Al-Miqdad bin Amr stood up and said: O Messenger of God, go to what God has commanded you to do, for we are with you. By God, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Moses: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting here.” Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. By the One Who sent you with the truth, if you were to march with us to Bark Al-Ghamad, meaning the city of Abyssinia, we would fight with you until you reach it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke well of him and prayed for good for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Advise me, O people, for he only means the Ansar, for they were the number of people, and that is because when they pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, they said: O Messenger of God, we are innocent of your reins until you reach our home. When you reach us, then you are in our reins, and we will protect you as we protect our sons and women. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afraid that the Ansar would not see it upon them to support him except against those who attacked him in Medina from his enemy, and that they were not required to march with them to an enemy from their country. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, he said to him: Saad bin Muadh: By God, it seems that you want us, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: We have believed in you and we believe you and we testify that what you have brought is the truth and we have given you our pledges and covenants to hear and obey. So go, O Messenger of God, as God has commanded you. By He Who sent you with the truth, if you were to parade us across this sea and cross it, we would cross it with you. Not a single man of us would stay behind and we would not mind if you were to meet our enemy tomorrow. We are patient in war and truthful when we meet. Perhaps God will show you from us something that will please your eyes. So go with us with God’s blessing. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with what Saad said and was encouraged by it. Then he said: Go with God’s blessing and be glad, for God has promised me one of the two groups. By God, it seems that I am now looking at the place where the people will fall. Al-Awfi narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas. Al-Suddi, Qatadah, Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf and Khalaf said the same. We have summarized their statements, contenting ourselves with the context of Muhammad bin Ishaq.

Al-A’wfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, when he consulted the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, about meeting the enemy, and Sa’d ibn Ubadah said to him what he said, and that was on the day of Badr, he commanded the people to prepare for battle and commanded them to use force. The people of faith disliked that, so God revealed, Just as your Lord brought you out from your home with truth, although a party of the believers were averse. They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on. Mujahid said, They argue with you about the truth means in fighting. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, They argue with you about the truth means hatred for meeting the polytheists, and denial of the march of Quraysh when they mentioned it to them. Al-Suddi said, They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear means after it has become clear to them that you will only do what God has commanded you to do. Ibn Jarir said, and others said that he meant the polytheists. Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God the Almighty, They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear as if they were being driven to death while they are looking on, these polytheists said, they argued with him about the truth as if they were being driven to death when they were called to Islam while they were looking on. He said, This is not a description of the others; this is a description that has been introduced for the people of disbelief. Then Ibn Jarir said, There is no meaning to what he said, because what preceded his saying, “They argue with you about the truth is report about the people of faith, and what follows it is report about them.” The correct statement is that of Ibn Abbas and Ibn Ishaq: that it is a report from the believers. This which Ibn Jarir supported is the truth and is what the context of the speech indicates, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad, may God have mercy on him, said: Yahya bin Bakir and Abd al-Razzaq told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he finished with Badr: Go with the caravan, there is nothing beyond it. Al-Abbas bin Abd al-Muttalib called out to him. Abd al-Razzaq said while he was a prisoner in his chains: He is not suitable for you. He said: Why? He said: Because God, the Almighty, promised you only one of the two groups, and God has given you what He promised you with a good chain of transmission and has not included it. The meaning of His, the Almighty, saying: And you would like that the one without power should be yours means that they would like the group that has no limits, no strength, and no fighting to be theirs, which is the caravan. And God wants to establish the truth with His words means that He wants to unite you with the group that has power and fighting, so that He may make you victorious over them and support you against them, and make His religion prevail and raise the word of Islam and make it victorious over religions. He is the most knowledgeable about the consequences of things, and He is the One who manages you with His good management, even if the servants like the opposite of that in what appears to them, like His, the Almighty’s, saying: “Fighting has been prescribed for you, although it is hateful to you. But perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you. And perhaps you love a thing and it is bad for you.” Muhammad ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Zuhri, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatadah, Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr, and Yazid ibn Ruman narrated to me, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and others of our scholars, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Abbas. Each of them narrated to me some of this hadith, and it came together. Their hadith in what I have cited from the hadith of Badr, they said: “When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, heard of Abu Sufyan coming from Syria, he summoned the Muslims to them and said: ‘This is the caravan of Quraysh with their wealth in it, so go out to it, perhaps God will grant you some of it.’ So the people volunteered, some of them lightly and some of them were heavy, because they did not think that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would encounter war. Abu Sufyan had been mobilized when he approached the Hijaz, spying on the report and asking whomever he met of the caravans, fearing for the people’s situation, until he received report from some of the caravans that Muhammad had mobilized his companions for you and your caravan. So he was cautious and hired Damdam bin Amr al-Ghifari and sent him to the people of Mecca and ordered him to go to Quraysh and summon them to their wealth and inform them that Muhammad had attacked it with his companions. So Damdam bin Amr went out quickly to Mecca, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions until he reached a valley called Dhafran, and he went out from it until he was in some of it, and the report came to him from Quraysh about their march to prevent it.” He reproached them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people and told them about the Quraysh. Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, and he did well. Then Umar, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, and he did well. Then Al-Miqdad bin Amr stood up and said: O Messenger of God, go to what God has commanded you to do, for we are with you. By God, we will not say to you as the Children of Israel said to Moses: “Go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are sitting here.” Rather, go, you and your Lord, and fight. We are with you, fighting. By the One Who sent you with the truth, if you were to march with us to Bark Al-Ghamad, meaning the city of Abyssinia, we would fight with you until you reach it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spoke well of him and prayed for good for him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Advise me, O people, for he only means the Ansar, for they were the number of people, and that is because when they pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, they said: O Messenger of God, we are innocent of your reins until you reach our home. When you reach us, then you are in our reins, and we will protect you as we protect our sons and women. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was afraid that the Ansar would not see it upon them to support him except against those who attacked him in Medina from his enemy, and that they were not required to march with them to an enemy from their country. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said that, he said to him: Saad bin Muadh: By God, it seems that you want us, O Messenger of God? He said: Yes. He said: We have believed in you and we believe you and we testify that what you have brought is the truth and we have given you our pledges and covenants to hear and obey. So go, O Messenger of God, as God has commanded you. By He Who sent you with the truth, if you were to parade us across this sea and cross it, we would cross it with you. Not a single man of us would stay behind and we would not mind if you were to meet our enemy tomorrow. We are patient in war and truthful when we meet. Perhaps God will show you from us something that will please your eyes. So go with us with God’s blessing. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with what Saad said and was encouraged by it. Then he said: Go with God’s blessing and be glad, for God has promised me one of the two groups. By God, it seems that I am now looking at the place where the people will fall. Al-Awfi narrated something similar to this from Ibn Abbas. Al-Suddi, Qatadah, Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam and more than one of the scholars of the Salaf and Khalaf said the same. We have summarized their statements, contenting ourselves with the context of Muhammad bin Ishaq.
8:9: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Nuh Qurad told us, Ikrimah bin Ammar told us, Samak Al-Hanafi Abu Zamil told us, Ibn Abbas told me, Omar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, told me: When the day of Badr came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, looked at his companions, who were more than three hundred, and he looked at the polytheists, and he saw that they were a thousand or more. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, faced the qiblah, wearing his cloak and lower garment, then he said, “O God, fulfill for me what You promised me. O God, if You destroy this group of the people of Islam, You will never be worshipped on earth again.” He continued to seek help from his Lord and supplicate to Him until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came to him, took his cloak, put it back on, embraced him from behind, and said, O Prophet of God, it is enough for you to implore your Lord, for He will fulfill for you what He promised you. Then God Almighty revealed, “When you sought help from your Lord, and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another. ’” When that day came, they met, and God defeated the polytheists, and they were killed. Seventy of them were taken prisoner, and seventy of them were taken prisoner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali. Abu Bakr said: O Messenger of God, these are our cousins, our clan, and our brothers. I think that you should take ransom from them, so that what we have taken from them will be a strength for us against the infidels. Perhaps God will guide them and they will be a support for us. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think, O son of Al-Khattab? I said: I do not think what Abu Bakr thinks, but I think that you should give me control over so-and-so, a relative of Umar, so that I may strike off his neck, and give Ali control over Uqayl so that he may strike off his neck, and give Hamza control over so-and-so, his brother, so that he may strike off his neck, until God knows that there is no truce in our hearts for the polytheists. These are their leaders, their leaders, and their chiefs. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, liked what Abu Bakr said, but he did not like what I said, and he took ransom from them. The next day, Umar said: I went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, and they were crying. I said: What makes you and your friend cry? If I find something to cry, I will cry, and if I do not find something to cry, I will pretend to cry because of your crying. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, To the one who offered me your companions to take ransom, your punishment was offered to me closer than this tree. This is a tree close to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. God Almighty revealed, “It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has made slaughter in the land. You desire the goods of this world, but God desires the Hereafter. And God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took. So eat of what you have taken as lawful and good.” So the spoils were made lawful for them. Then, on the day of Uhud of the following year, they were punished for what they had done on the day of Badr, by taking ransoms. Seventy of them were killed, and the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, fled from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his front teeth were broken, and the egg on his head was smashed, and blood flowed down his face. Then God revealed, Or when a disaster struck you, although you had inflicted twice as much, did you say, ‘From where is this?’ Say, ‘It is from yourselves.’ Indeed, God is over all things competent. by taking ransoms. Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Ammar, and Ali ibn al-Madini and al-Tirmidhi authenticated it. They said that it is only known from the hadith of Ikrimah ibn Ammar al-Yamani. Thus, Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that this noble verse, When you sought help from your Lord, was in the supplication of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Yazid ibn Yathi’, al-Suddi, and Ibn Jurayj said the same. Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash said on the authority of Abu Hasin on the authority of Abu Salih, who said: When the day of Badr came, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to implore his Lord with the most intense entreaty, supplicating. Then Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him came to him and said: O Messenger of God, some of your supplication, by God, God will fulfill for you what He promised you. Al-Bukhari said in the Book of Military Expeditions, Chapter on the saying of God the Most High: “When you called upon your Lord and He answered you, ‘I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one another.’ And God made it not but good tidings and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. And victory is not but from God. Indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. When He covered you with drowsiness as a security from Him and sent down upon you from the sky water to purify you thereby and remove from you the defilement of Satan and to strengthen your hearts and plant firmly thereby your feet. When your Lord inspired to the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [them] above the necks and strike from them every fingertip.’ That is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger - indeed, God is severe in penalty.” Abu Na’im narrated to us, Isra’il narrated to us, on the authority of Mukhariq, on the authority of Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: I heard Ibn Mas’ud say: I witnessed a scene from al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, which would have been more beloved to me to be his companion than to take something else. He came to the Prophet (may God bless him and grant him peace) while he was supplicating. On the polytheists, he said: We do not say as the people of Moses said: Go, you and your Lord, and fight. Rather, we will fight on your right and on your left, in front of you and behind you. I saw the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, his face and his secret shining, meaning his words. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Hawshab told me, Abd al-Wahhab told us, Khalid al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr, “O God, I ask You to fulfill Your covenant and promise. O God, if You will, You will not be worshipped.” Abu Bakr took his hand and said, That is enough for You. He went out saying, The army will be defeated and they will turn their backs. An-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Bandar on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab on the authority of Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi. God Almighty’s statement, With a thousand angels in succession, means that some of them will follow one another, as Harun ibn Antara said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in succession, in succession. It is possible that what is meant by in succession for you means to help you, as al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in succession, meaning reinforcement, as you say to a man, increase him so-and-so. And this is what Mujahid, Ibn Kathir al-Qari, and Ibn Zayd said, in succession, “stretched.” Abu Kudaynah said on the authority of Qabus on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, stretched you with a thousand angels in succession, meaning that behind every angel there is an angel. In a narration with this chain of transmission, mardafin two angels was said by some of them one after the other, and so said Abu Dhibyan, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Yaqub ibn Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Imran told me, Al-Zumai’i told us, Abu Al-Huwayrith told us, Muhammad Jubayr told us, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Gabriel descended with a thousand angels on the right flank of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr was in it, and Michael descended with a thousand angels on the left flank of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was on the left flank. This requires, if its chain of transmission is sound, that the alif is followed by its like, and for this reason some of them read mardafin with a fat-ha on the dal, and God knows best. The well-known narration is what Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And God supported His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with a thousand angels. Gabriel was with five hundred angels on his side, and Michael was with five hundred on his side. Imam Abu Ja`far bin Jarir and Muslim narrated from the hadith of `Ikrimah bin `Ammar on the authority of Abu Zamil Samak bin Walid al-Hanafi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of `Umar, the previous hadith. Then Abu Zamil said: Ibn Abbas told me: While a Muslim man was pursuing a polytheist in front of him, he heard a whip strike above him and the voice of a knight saying, Go forward, Haizum. When he looked at the polytheist in front of him, he fell down and lay down. He said: So he looked at him and saw that his face had been smashed and split like a whip strike, and it all turned green. Then the Ansari came and told that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: You have spoken the truth. It was from the support of the third heaven. So they killed seventy that day and took seventy captive. Al-Bukhari said: Chapter: The angels’ witnesses to Badr. Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Muadh bin Rafa’ah bin Rafi’ al-Zarqi, on the authority of his father, and his father was one of the people of Badr. He said, Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, Who do you consider the people of Badr among you? He said, Among the best of the Muslims, or something similar. He said, And so are those angels who witnessed Badr. Al-Bukhari was the only one to narrate it, and Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabir from the hadith of Rafi' bin Khadij, which is a mistake. The correct narration is that of Al-Bukhari, and God knows best. In the two Sahihs, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar when he consulted him about killing Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah: "He witnessed Badr, and what do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." And the Almighty said: And God did not make it except as good tidings 3:10, meaning that God did not make sending the angels and informing you of them except as good tidings, and that your hearts might be reassured thereby 3:10. Otherwise, God is able to grant you victory over your enemies and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. Victory comes only from God, meaning without that. That is why He said: And victory comes only from God, as God, the Almighty, said: "So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure [their] bonds. Then either [take] a favor afterwards or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens. That is. And if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And as for those who are killed in the way of God - never will He let their deeds perish." * He will guide them and set their affairs right * And admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them. And the Most High said: “And these days We alternate among the people so that God may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs - and God does not love the wrongdoers - * And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.” This is the ruling of God’s law regarding jihad against the disbelievers at the hands of the believers for its sake. And the Most High used to punish the previous nations that denied the prophets with the calamities that befell those nations that denied the prophets, just as He destroyed the people of Noah with the flood, and the first ‘Aad with the hornet, and the Thamud with the blast, and the people of Lot with the sinking and the overturning and the stones of baked clay, and the people of Shu’aib with the Day of the Shadow. So when God the Most High sent Moses and destroyed his enemy Pharaoh and his people by drowning them in the sea, then He sent down the Torah to Moses, He made it lawful to fight the disbelievers in it, and the ruling continued in the rest of the laws after him on that basis, as the Most High said: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations as insight. And the killing of the disbelievers by the believers is a greater humiliation for the disbelievers, and more healing for the hearts of the believers, as the Most High said: For the believers of this nation, Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the hearts of a believing people. That is why the killing of the leaders of Quraysh by the hands of their enemies who looked at them with eyes of contempt was more painful for them and more healing for the hearts of the party of faith. The killing of Abu Jahl in the battlefield and the heat of battle was more humiliating for him than his death in his bed by a calamity or thunderbolt or something similar, just as Abu Lahab, may God curse him, died from a lentil, such that none of his relatives approached him. Rather, they washed him with water, throwing him from a distance, and they stoned him until they buried him. That is why God the Almighty said, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, meaning that He has might, and for His Messenger and for the believers in them in this world and the Hereafter, like His saying, Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. “Wise” in what He has prescribed of fighting the infidels while being able to destroy and annihilate them by His power and strength, glory be to Him, the Most High.
