Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Ishaq told us, Yaqub ibn Muhammad Al-Zuhri told us, Abdul Aziz ibn Imran told me, Al-Zumai’i told us, Abu Al-Huwayrith told us, Muhammad Jubayr told us, Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Gabriel descended with a thousand angels on the right flank of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr was in it, and Michael descended with a thousand angels on the left flank of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I was on the left flank. This requires, if its chain of transmission is sound, that the alif is followed by its like, and for this reason some of them read mardafin with a fat-ha on the dal, and God knows best. The well-known narration is what Ali bin Abi Talha narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: And God supported His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with a thousand angels. Gabriel was with five hundred angels on his side, and Michael was with five hundred on his side. Imam Abu Ja`far bin Jarir and Muslim narrated from the hadith of `Ikrimah bin `Ammar on the authority of Abu Zamil Samak bin Walid al-Hanafi on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of `Umar, the previous hadith. Then Abu Zamil said: Ibn Abbas told me: While a Muslim man was pursuing a polytheist in front of him, he heard a whip strike above him and the voice of a knight saying, Go forward, Haizum. When he looked at the polytheist in front of him, he fell down and lay down. He said: So he looked at him and saw that his face had been smashed and split like a whip strike, and it all turned green. Then the Ansari came and told that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: You have spoken the truth. It was from the support of the third heaven. So they killed seventy that day and took seventy captive. Al-Bukhari said: Chapter: The angels’ witnesses to Badr. Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Muadh bin Rafa’ah bin Rafi’ al-Zarqi, on the authority of his father, and his father was one of the people of Badr. He said, Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, Who do you consider the people of Badr among you? He said, Among the best of the Muslims, or something similar. He said, And so are those angels who witnessed Badr. Al-Bukhari was the only one to narrate it, and Al-Tabarani narrated it in Al-Mu'jam Al-Kabir from the hadith of Rafi' bin Khadij, which is a mistake. The correct narration is that of Al-Bukhari, and God knows best. In the two Sahihs, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Umar when he consulted him about killing Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah: "He witnessed Badr, and what do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." And the Almighty said: And God did not make it except as good tidings 3:10, meaning that God did not make sending the angels and informing you of them except as good tidings, and that your hearts might be reassured thereby 3:10. Otherwise, God is able to grant you victory over your enemies and that your hearts might be reassured thereby. Victory comes only from God, meaning without that. That is why He said: And victory comes only from God, as God, the Almighty, said: "So when you meet those who disbelieve, strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure [their] bonds. Then either [take] a favor afterwards or ransom them until the war lays down its burdens. That is. And if God had willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them, but that He may test some of you by means of others. And as for those who are killed in the way of God - never will He let their deeds perish." * He will guide them and set their affairs right * And admit them into Paradise, which He has made known to them. And the Most High said: “And these days We alternate among the people so that God may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs - and God does not love the wrongdoers - * And that God may purify those who believe and destroy the disbelievers.” This is the ruling of God’s law regarding jihad against the disbelievers at the hands of the believers for its sake. And the Most High used to punish the previous nations that denied the prophets with the calamities that befell those nations that denied the prophets, just as He destroyed the people of Noah with the flood, and the first ‘Aad with the hornet, and the Thamud with the blast, and the people of Lot with the sinking and the overturning and the stones of baked clay, and the people of Shu’aib with the Day of the Shadow. So when God the Most High sent Moses and destroyed his enemy Pharaoh and his people by drowning them in the sea, then He sent down the Torah to Moses, He made it lawful to fight the disbelievers in it, and the ruling continued in the rest of the laws after him on that basis, as the Most High said: And We gave Moses the Scripture after We destroyed the former generations as insight. And the killing of the disbelievers by the believers is a greater humiliation for the disbelievers, and more healing for the hearts of the believers, as the Most High said: For the believers of this nation, Fight them; God will punish them by your hands and disgrace them and give you victory over them and heal the hearts of a believing people. That is why the killing of the leaders of Quraysh by the hands of their enemies who looked at them with eyes of contempt was more painful for them and more healing for the hearts of the party of faith. The killing of Abu Jahl in the battlefield and the heat of battle was more humiliating for him than his death in his bed by a calamity or thunderbolt or something similar, just as Abu Lahab, may God curse him, died from a lentil, such that none of his relatives approached him. Rather, they washed him with water, throwing him from a distance, and they stoned him until they buried him. That is why God the Almighty said, Indeed, God is Exalted in Might, meaning that He has might, and for His Messenger and for the believers in them in this world and the Hereafter, like His saying, Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believe during the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand. “Wise” in what He has prescribed of fighting the infidels while being able to destroy and annihilate them by His power and strength, glory be to Him, the Most High.
8:11: God the Almighty reminds them of what He bestowed upon them by sending them sleep as a security from their fear that they had from the great number of their enemy and the small number of them. And this is what God the Almighty did to them on the day of Uhud, as He the Almighty said: Then, after the distress, He sent down upon you security - a drowsiness that overcame a party of you and a party whose souls were concerned Al-Akhbar 2:13. Abu Talha said: I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud, and the sword fell from my hand repeatedly, falling and I would catch it, and falling and I would catch it. I saw them swaying while they were under the shield. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Zuhair told us, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha bin Mudrib, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: There was no knight among us on the day of Badr except Al-Miqdad, and I saw us and there was none among us except sleeping, except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying under a tree and crying until morning. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Asim on the authority of Abu Razin on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Drowsiness in battle is a security from God, and in prayer it is from Satan. Qatada said: Drowsiness is in the head, and sleep is in the heart. I said: As for drowsiness, it afflicted them on the day of Uhud and the matter of that is very well known. As for the noble verse, it is in the context of the story of Badr, and it indicates that that also happened, as if that would happen to the believers at the height of battle so that their hearts would be secure and reassured by God’s victory. This is from God’s grace, mercy and blessings upon them, as God Almighty said: “For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” For this reason it came in the Sahih that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the hut with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the day of Badr, and they were supplicating, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell asleep and then he woke up smiling and said: “Be glad, O Abu Bakr. This is Gabriel on his teeth, covered in dust.” Then he went out from the door of the hut while reciting the words of God Almighty: The hosts will be routed and they will turn their backs. And His saying, And He sends down upon you water from the sky, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended when he marched to Badr and the polytheists had between them and the water a small sand dune, and the Muslims were afflicted with severe weakness and Satan cast rage into their hearts, whispering among them, You claim that you are the allies of God Almighty and that His Messenger is among you, and the polytheists have overcome you at the water, and you are praying in a state of ritual impurity. So God rained down heavy rain upon them, so the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and God removed from them the impurity of Satan, and the sand stood firm when the rain fell upon it, and people and animals walked on it, so they marched to the people, and God supported His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with a thousand angels, so Gabriel was with five hundred angels, and Michael was with five hundred angels. And likewise Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When the polytheists of Quraysh went out to support the caravan and fight on its behalf, they camped at the water on the day of Badr and defeated the believers there. The believers were afflicted with thirst, so they began to pray while in a state of ritual impurity and in a state of minor ritual impurity until it became a burden on their hearts. Then God sent down water from the sky until the valley overflowed. The believers drank, filled their water skins, gave water to their riders, and washed themselves after ritual impurity. God made that a means of purification and made their feet firm. This is because there was sand between them and the people, so God sent rain on it and struck it until it became hard and their feet were firm on it. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Ash-Sha’bi, Az-Zuhri, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam that they were afflicted with thirst on the day of Badr. It is well known that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) marched to Badr, he camped at the lowest water there, that is, the first water he found. Then Al-Habbab bin Al-Mundhir approached him and said, “O Messenger of God, is this the place where you have camped? This is the place where God has camped for you, so we should not go beyond it. Or is it a place where you have camped for war and plotting?” He said: Rather, it is a place where I have come for war and plotting. He said: "O Messenger of God, this is not a place, but let us go until we camp at the nearest water source near the people and we will fill up the heart behind it, and we will draw water from the basins so that we will have water and they will not have water." So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on and did likewise. In the Battles of the Umayyads, it is narrated that when Al-Hubab said that, an angel came down from the sky and Gabriel was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. That angel said: O Muhammad, your Lord sends you his greetings and tells you that the opinion is what Al-Hubab bin Al-Mundhir indicated. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel, peace be upon him, and said: Do you know this? So he looked at him and said: "I do not know all the angels. He is an angel and not a devil." The best of this is what Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, the author of Al-Maghāzī, may God have mercy on him, narrated: Yazid bin Ruman told me on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, who said: God sent the sky and the valley was flat, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions were struck by what made the earth sticky for them, but it did not prevent them from moving on, and it struck the Quraysh by what they were not able to travel with him. Mujahid said: God sent rain upon them before drowsiness, so the rain extinguished the dust and the earth was covered with it, and their souls were comforted and their feet were firm. Ibn Jarir said: Harun bin Ishaq told us, Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Israel told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Haritha, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were struck by a heavy downpour of rain at night, meaning the night in the morning of which the Battle of Badr took place, so we set out under the trees and the rocks to seek shade from the rain, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the night and urged people to fight. And His saying, To purify you thereby means from minor or major impurity, which is the purification of the outward appearance, and to remove from you the defilement of Satan, meaning from any evil whisperings or thoughts, which is the purification of the inward appearance, as God Almighty said about the people of Paradise, Upon them will be green garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver, which is the adornment of the outward appearance, and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink, meaning purifying from any rancor, envy, or hatred, which is the adornment and purity of the inward appearance, and to strengthen your hearts, meaning with patience and boldness in confronting the enemies, which is the courage of the inward appearance, and to make firm thereby your feet, which is the courage of the outward appearance, and God knows best. And His saying, When your Lord inspired the angels, ‘I am with you, so strengthen those who believe.’ This is a hidden blessing that God Almighty revealed to them so that they would thank Him for it, and that is that He, the Most High, the Most Holy, the Most Blessed, and the Most Glorious, inspired the angels whom He sent down to support His Prophet, His religion, and His party of believers, inspiring them between Him and them to strengthen those who believe. Ibn Ishaq said: And support them. Another said: Fight with them. It was said: They increased their numbers. It was said that this was because the king would come to a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: I heard these people, meaning the polytheists, saying: By God, if they attack us, we will be defeated. So the Muslims would tell each other about that, and their souls would be strengthened. Ibn Jarir narrated it, and this is its wording verbatim. His statement, I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve, means: Be steadfast, you believers, and strengthen your souls against your enemies. By my command to you, I will cast terror, humiliation, and disgrace upon those who disobey my command and deny my messenger. Then strike above the necks and strike from them every fingertip, meaning strike the crowns and split them, and cut off the necks and cut off the limbs, which are their hands and feet. The commentators differed about the meaning of above the necks. It was said that it means strike the heads, said by Ikrimah. It was said that it means on the necks, which are the necks, said by Ad-Dahhak and Atiyah Al-Awfi. This meaning is supported by the fact that God Almighty guided the believers to this in His statement, Then when… You will meet those who disbelieved, so strike their necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter on them, then secure their bonds.” And Wakee’ said on the authority of Al-Mas’udi on the authority of Al-Qasim, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was not sent to punish with the punishment of God, I was only sent to strike necks and secure their bonds. Ibn Jarir chose that it may refer to striking necks and splitting heads. I said: In the Battles of Al-Umawi, it is mentioned that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would pass among the dead on the day of Badr and say: Split heads. Abu Bakr would say: From men who were dear to us, but they were disobedient and unjust The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would begin with the beginning of the verse and would ask Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, to recite the end of it because he was not good at reciting poetry, as God Almighty said: And We did not teach him poetry, nor is it befitting for it. Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: On the day of Badr, the people would recognize those killed by the angels from those they had killed by a strike above the necks and on the fingers like a mark of fire that had been burned. And his saying, And strike from them every fingertip, Ibn Jarir said: Its meaning is, strike from your enemy, O believers, every extremity and joint of the ends of their hands and feet, and the finger is the plural of fingernail, as the poet said: I wish I had cut off a finger and found him awake and alert in the house. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And strike off from them every fingertip, meaning by finger the extremities. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Jarir said the same. As-Suddi said that fingertip is the extremities, and it is also said that every joint. Ikrimah, Atiyah Al-Awfi and Ad-Dahhak said in another narration that every joint. Al-Awza’i said in the words of God the Almighty, And strike off from them every fingertip, that is, strike off the face and the eye and shoot at it with a meteor of fire. When you capture it, all of that will be forbidden to you. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He mentioned the story of Badr until he said: Abu Jahl said, Do not kill them, but seize them until you know what they did of attacking your religion and turning away from Al-Lat and Al-Uzza. So God revealed to the angels, “Indeed, I am with you, so strengthen those who believe. I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve. So strike above the necks and strike off from them every fingertip,” the verse. Abu Jahl, may God curse him, was killed with sixty-nine men, and Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt was taken prisoner and killed patiently, and that was seventy, meaning dead. For this reason God the Almighty said, That is because they opposed God. And His Messenger” meaning they opposed them and went in one direction, and abandoned the law and belief in it and following it in another direction. It is also taken from splitting the stick, which is dividing it into two parts. And whoever opposes God and His Messenger, then indeed, God is severe in penalty. meaning He is the seeker and the victorious of whoever opposes Him and opposes Him. Nothing escapes Him and nothing can withstand His anger. Blessed and Most High, there is no god or lord but Him. That is it, so taste it, and indeed, for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire. This is addressed to the disbelievers, meaning taste this punishment and chastisement in this world, and know also that for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter.

8:13: God the Almighty reminds them of what He bestowed upon them by sending them sleep as a security from their fear that they had from the great number of their enemy and the small number of them. And this is what God the Almighty did to them on the day of Uhud, as He the Almighty said: Then, after the distress, He sent down upon you security - a drowsiness that overcame a party of you and a party whose souls were concerned Al-Akhbar 2:13. Abu Talha said: I was among those who were overcome by drowsiness on the day of Uhud, and the sword fell from my hand repeatedly, falling and I would catch it, and falling and I would catch it. I saw them swaying while they were under the shield. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Zuhair told us, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha bin Mudrib, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: There was no knight among us on the day of Badr except Al-Miqdad, and I saw us and there was none among us except sleeping, except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, praying under a tree and crying until morning. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Asim on the authority of Abu Razin on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, that he said: Drowsiness in battle is a security from God, and in prayer it is from Satan. Qatada said: Drowsiness is in the head, and sleep is in the heart. I said: As for drowsiness, it afflicted them on the day of Uhud and the matter of that is very well known. As for the noble verse, it is in the context of the story of Badr, and it indicates that that also happened, as if that would happen to the believers at the height of battle so that their hearts would be secure and reassured by God’s victory. This is from God’s grace, mercy and blessings upon them, as God Almighty said: “For indeed, with hardship [will be] ease. Indeed, with hardship [will be] ease.” For this reason it came in the Sahih that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in the hut with Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, on the day of Badr, and they were supplicating, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell asleep and then he woke up smiling and said: “Be glad, O Abu Bakr. This is Gabriel on his teeth, covered in dust.” Then he went out from the door of the hut while reciting the words of God Almighty: The hosts will be routed and they will turn their backs. And His saying, And He sends down upon you water from the sky, Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, descended when he marched to Badr and the polytheists had between them and the water a small sand dune, and the Muslims were afflicted with severe weakness and Satan cast rage into their hearts, whispering among them, You claim that you are the allies of God Almighty and that His Messenger is among you, and the polytheists have overcome you at the water, and you are praying in a state of ritual impurity. So God rained down heavy rain upon them, so the Muslims drank and purified themselves, and God removed from them the impurity of Satan, and the sand stood firm when the rain fell upon it, and people and animals walked on it, so they marched to the people, and God supported His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers with a thousand angels, so Gabriel was with five hundred angels, and Michael was with five hundred angels. And likewise Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: When the polytheists of Quraysh went out to support the caravan and fight on its behalf, they camped at the water on the day of Badr and defeated the believers there. The believers were afflicted with thirst, so they began to pray while in a state of ritual impurity and in a state of minor ritual impurity until it became a burden on their hearts. Then God sent down water from the sky until the valley overflowed. The believers drank, filled their water skins, gave water to their riders, and washed themselves after ritual impurity. God made that a means of purification and made their feet firm. This is because there was sand between them and the people, so God sent rain on it and struck it until it became hard and their feet were firm on it. Something similar to this was narrated on the authority of Qatada, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi. It was narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Ash-Sha’bi, Az-Zuhri, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam that they were afflicted with thirst on the day of Badr. It is well known that when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) marched to Badr, he camped at the lowest water there, that is, the first water he found. Then Al-Habbab bin Al-Mundhir approached him and said, “O Messenger of God, is this the place where you have camped? This is the place where God has camped for you, so we should not go beyond it. Or is it a place where you have camped for war and plotting?” He said: Rather, it is a place where I have come for war and plotting. He said: "O Messenger of God, this is not a place, but let us go until we camp at the nearest water source near the people and we will fill up the heart behind it, and we will draw water from the basins so that we will have water and they will not have water." So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went on and did likewise. In the Battles of the Umayyads, it is narrated that when Al-Hubab said that, an angel came down from the sky and Gabriel was sitting with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. That angel said: O Muhammad, your Lord sends you his greetings and tells you that the opinion is what Al-Hubab bin Al-Mundhir indicated. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to Gabriel, peace be upon him, and said: Do you know this? So he looked at him and said: "I do not know all the angels. He is an angel and not a devil." Mujahid said: God sent rain upon them before drowsiness, so the rain extinguished the dust and the earth was covered with it, and their souls were comforted and their feet were firm. Ibn Jarir said: Harun bin Ishaq told us, Mus`ab bin Al-Muqaddam told us, Israel told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Haritha, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: We were struck by a heavy downpour of rain at night, meaning the night in the morning of which the Battle of Badr took place, so we set out under the trees and the rocks to seek shade from the rain, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the night and urged people to fight. It was said that this was because the king would come to a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: I heard these people, meaning the polytheists, saying: By God, if they attack us, we will be defeated. By my command to you, I will cast terror, humiliation, and disgrace upon those who disobey my command and deny my messenger. It was said that it means on the necks, which are the necks, said by Ad-Dahhak and Atiyah Al-Awfi. 8:15: God Almighty says, threatening those who do that with the Fire for fleeing from the battlefield: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieve advancing meaning, you approach them and come close to them, do not turn your backs to them meaning, flee and leave your companions. And whoever turns his back to them that day, except one who turns aside for the sake of fighting meaning, he flees in front of his comrades as a plot to show him that he fears him, so he follows him and then attacks him and kills him, then there is no harm in that. Saeed bin Jubayr and Al-Suddi stated this explicitly. Ad-Dahhak said that he should advance ahead of his companions to see a surprise from the enemy and strike it, or withdraw to a group meaning, he fled from here to another group of Muslims, helping them and they helping him, so that is permissible for him, even if he was in a secret mission and fled to his commander or the greatest imam, he is included in this concession. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan told us, Zuhair told us, Yazid bin Abi Ziyad told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Abi Laila, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: I was in one of the raids of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people surrounded him, and I was among those surrounded. We said: What should we do, since we have fled from the battle and have been afflicted with wrath? Then we said: Why don’t we enter Madinah? So we spent the night, then we said: Why don’t we present ourselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? If we can repent, then we will go. So we came to him before the morning prayer, and he came out and said: Who are these people? We said: We are the ones who fled. He said: No, you are the troublemakers. I am your group and I am the group of the Muslims. So we came to him and kissed his hand. And thus Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of transmission on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good. We do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Abi Ziyad. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad with it, and he added at the end of it: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited this verse: Or withdrawing to a group. The people of knowledge said that the meaning of his saying the grocers is the ones who give gifts. And likewise, Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said about Abu Ubaid when he was killed on the bridge in the land of Persia due to the large army from the direction of the Magians. Umar said: If he had withdrawn to me, I would have been a group for him. This is how Muhammad bin Sirin narrated it on the authority of Umar. And in the narration of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi on the authority of Umar, he said: When Abu Ubaid was killed, Umar said: O people, I am your group. And Mujahid said: Umar said: I am the group of every Muslim. And Abd Al-Malik bin Umair said on the authority of Umar: O people, do not be deceived by this verse, for it was on the day of Badr, and I am a group for every Muslim. And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hassan bin Abdullah Al-Masry told us, Khallad bin Sulayman Al-Hadrami told us, Nafi’ told us that he asked Ibn Umar: I said: We are a people who do not… Shall we stand firm when fighting our enemy, and we do not know who is in the group, our leader or our army? He said: The group is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. I said: God says: When you meet those who disbelieve advancing (al-Baqarah 2:14), He said: This verse was revealed on the day of Badr, not before or after it. Ad-Dahhak said about His statement: or withdrawing to a group: withdrawing to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. Likewise, the one who flees today to his leader or his companions. But if the flight is not for any of these reasons, then it is forbidden and a major sin, because of what was narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Avoid the seven destructive sins. It was said: O Messenger of God, what are they? He said: “Associating partners with God, sorcery, killing a soul which God has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the wealth of an orphan, turning away on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, unaware, believing women of adultery.” And there are evidences from other sources, and for this reason God Almighty said: He has incurred meaning he has returned with wrath from God, and his refuge meaning his destination and return on the Day of Appointment is Hell, and an evil destination. Imam Ahmad said: Zakariya bin Adi told us, Abdullah bin Omar Al-Raqi told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Abi Anisa, Jabalah bin Suhaim told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muthanna Al-Abdi, I heard Al-Sadosi, meaning Ibn Al-Khasasiyah, who is Bashir bin Ma’bad, say: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge allegiance to him, and he stipulated that I testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that I establish prayer, and pay zakat, and perform the Hajj of Islam, and fast the month of Ramadan, and strive in the way of God. I said: O Messenger of God, as for two things, by God I cannot bear them: Jihad, for they claim that whoever turns his back has incurred the wrath of God, so I fear that if I am present at that, my soul will be humbled and I will hate death, and charity, for by God I have nothing but spoils and ten camels, which are the messengers of my family and their load. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, withdrew his hand and said: There is no Jihad and no charity, so how will you enter Paradise then? I said, O Messenger of God, I will pledge allegiance to you, so I pledged allegiance to him on all of them. This is a strange hadith from this aspect, and they did not include it in the six books. Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hamza told us: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim Abu al-Nadr told us: Yazid ibn Rabi’ah told us: Abu al-Ash’ath told us on the authority of Thawban, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There are three things with which no action is of any benefit: associating partners with God, disobeying one’s parents, and fleeing from battle.” This is also a very strange hadith. We do not know it except from this source. I said: It is not known from Zayd, the freed slave of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, other than him. It was said that what is meant by this verse is the people of Badr in particular. And God knows best.

Saeed bin Jubayr and Al-Suddi stated this explicitly. Ad-Dahhak said that he should advance ahead of his companions to see a surprise from the enemy and strike it, or withdraw to a group meaning, he fled from here to another group of Muslims, helping them and they helping him, so that is permissible for him, even if he was in a secret mission and fled to his commander or the greatest imam, he is included in this concession. So we spent the night, then we said: Why don’t we present ourselves to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? If we can repent, then we will go. So we came to him before the morning prayer, and he came out and said: Who are these people? We said: We are the ones who fled. He said: No, you are the troublemakers. 8:17: God the Almighty shows that He is the Creator of the actions of His servants and that He is the One to be praised for all the good they do because He is the One who guided them to that and helped them to do it. That is why He said: So you did not kill them, but it was God who killed them. That is, it was not by your power and strength that you killed your enemies despite their large numbers and your small numbers. Rather, it is He who gave you victory over them, as He said: And God had already given you victory at Badr when you were weak. And the Almighty said: "God had already given you victory on many occasions and on the day of Hunayn when your great number pleased you, but it did not avail you at all, and the earth, vast as it is, became strait for you; then you turned back, fleeing." God the Almighty knows that victory does not depend on the large number or the confusion of nation and number, but rather victory comes from Him the Almighty as He the Almighty said: How often has a small company overcome a large one by God's permission? And God is with the patient. Then the Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, also regarding the handful of dirt that he threw at the faces of the unbelievers on the day of Badr when he came out of the hut after his supplication, entreaty and submission, and he threw it at them and said: May your faces be disfigured. Then he ordered his companions to give the attackers their due, so they did, and God delivered those pebbles to the eyes of the polytheists, and there was not one of them who was not affected by it, which distracted him from his state. For this reason the Almighty said: And you did not throw when you threw, but it was God who threw, meaning it was He who delivered that to them and subdued them with it, not you. Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his hands, meaning on the day of Badr, and said: O Lord, if you destroy this group, you will never be worshipped on earth again. Gabriel said to him, Take a handful of dirt and throw it in their faces. So he took a handful of dirt and threw it in their faces. There was not one of the polytheists who did not get dirt in his eyes, nostrils, and mouth from that handful, so they turned back. Al-Suddi said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ali, may God be pleased with him, on the day of Badr, Give me pebbles from the earth. So he gave him pebbles covered with dirt, and he threw them in the faces of the people. There was not a single polytheist who did not get dirt in his eyes. Then the believers followed them, killing them and taking them captive. God revealed: “You did not kill them, but God killed them. You did not throw when you threw, but God threw.” Abu Ma’shar al-Madani said on the authority of Muhammad bin Qais and Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, they said: When the people drew near to one another, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of dirt and threw it in the faces of the people. He said: May your faces be disfigured, and it entered into the eyes of all of them, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to kill them and take them captive, and their defeat was due to the arrow of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God revealed: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. And Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. He said this on the day of Badr. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took three pebbles and threw one pebble on the right flank of the people, a pebble on the left flank of the people, and a pebble in the middle of them, and he said: May your faces be disfigured, and they were defeated. It has been narrated in this story on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and more than one of the imams that it was revealed regarding the arrow of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr, even though he had also done that on the day of Hunayn. Abu Ja`far ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, Ya`qub ibn Muhammad told us, Abd al-`Aziz ibn `Imran told us, Musa ibn Ya`qub ibn `Abdullah ibn Zama`ah told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn `Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah on the authority of Hakim bin Hizam said: When the day of Badr came, we heard a sound falling from the sky as if it was the sound of a pebble falling into a basin, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, threw that throw and we were defeated. This is strange from this aspect, and here are two other very strange sayings one of them Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Auf al-Ta’i told me, Abu al-Mughira told us, Safwan bin Amr told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr told us that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Ibn Abi al-Haqiq in Khaybar called for a bow, and a long bow was brought to him and he said, Bring me another bow. So they brought him a Kabd’ bow, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, shot at the fortress, and the arrow came crashing down until it killed Ibn Abi al-Haqiq while he was in his bed, so God Almighty revealed: And you did not throw when you threw, but God threw. This is strange, and its chain of transmission is good to Abd al-Rahman bin Jubayr bin Nufayr, and perhaps he was confused or he meant that the verse includes all of this, otherwise the context of the verse in Surat al-Anfal is in the story of Badr, and this is something that is not hidden from the Imams. Knowledge and God knows best. The second Ibn Jarir also narrated, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Zuhri that they said: It was revealed regarding the spear thrown by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud by Abi bin Khalaf while he was with his slave girl, and it scratched his collarbone, so he kept falling off his horse repeatedly until his death came after days in which he suffered painful torment connected to the torment of the intermediate realm connected to the torment of the Hereafter. This statement from these two Imams is also very strange, and perhaps they meant that the verse includes him in its generality, not that it was revealed about him specifically, as mentioned above, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement, And that He may test the believers with a good test, meaning that He may make the believers know His favor upon them by making them victorious over their enemy despite their large number and small number, so that they may know His right thereby and be grateful for His favor. Ibn Jarir also interpreted it in this way. In the hadith, And every good test He has tested us with, and his statement, Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning He hears supplications and knows who deserves victory and triumph. His statement, That is so, and that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers, this is another good tiding, along with what has come of victory, that He informed them, the Most High, that He will weaken the plot of the disbelievers in what is to come, in the smallness of their matter, and that they and everything they have are in ruin and destruction. Praise and thanks be to God.

The second Ibn Jarir also narrated, and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak with a sound chain of transmission on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Al-Zuhri that they said: It was revealed regarding the spear thrown by the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Uhud by Abi bin Khalaf while he was with his slave girl, and it scratched his collarbone, so he kept falling off his horse repeatedly until his death came after days in which he suffered painful torment connected to the torment of the intermediate realm connected to the torment of the Hereafter. This statement from these two Imams is also very strange, and perhaps they meant that the verse includes him in its generality, not that it was revealed about him specifically, as mentioned above, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding his statement, And that He may test the believers with a good test, meaning that He may make the believers know His favor upon them by making them victorious over their enemy despite their large number and small number, so that they may know His right thereby and be grateful for His favor. Ibn Jarir also interpreted it in this way. In the hadith, And every good test He has tested us with, and his statement, Indeed, God is All-Hearing, All-Knowing, meaning He hears supplications and knows who deserves victory and triumph. His statement, That is so, and that God weakens the plot of the disbelievers, this is another good tiding, along with what has come of victory, that He informed them, the Most High, that He will weaken the plot of the disbelievers in what is to come, in the smallness of their matter, and that they and everything they have are in ruin and destruction. Praise and thanks be to God.
8:19: God the Almighty says to the infidels: "If you seek victory" meaning if you seek help and ask God for help and to make a decision between you and your believing enemies, then what you asked for has come to you, as Muhammad ibn Ishaq and others said on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Abdullah ibn Tha'labah ibn Su'air that Abu Jahl said on the day of Badr: O God, which of us has severed the ties of kinship and brought us what we do not know, then destroy him this morning. And that was a request from him, so the verse was revealed: "If you seek victory, then victory has come to you" until the end of the verse. And Imam Ahmad said: Yazid, meaning Ibn Harun, told us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, Al-Zuhri told me on the authority of Abdullah ibn Tha'labah that Abu Jahl said when the people met: O God, we have severed the ties of kinship and brought us what we do not know, so destroy him this morning. So he was the one who opened it, and Al-Nasa’i included it in his interpretation from the hadith of Salih bin Kaysan from Al-Zuhri with it, and Al-Hakim also included it in his Mustadrak from the path of Al-Zuhri with it and said it is authentic according to the conditions of the two sheikhs, but they did not include it, and something similar to this was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Yazid bin Ruman and more than one, and Al-Suddi said that when the polytheists left Mecca for Badr, they took hold of the curtains of the Kaaba and sought victory from God and said: O God, support the highest of the two armies and the most honorable of the two groups and the best of the two tribes, so God said: If you seek victory, victory has come to you, meaning I have supported what you said, and he is Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said that the Almighty said, informing about them: And when they said, ‘O God, if this is the truth from You’ the verse, and His saying: And if you desist means from what you are doing of disbelief in God and denial of His Messenger, then it is better for you meaning in this world and the hereafter, and the Almighty’s saying: And if you return, We will return is like His saying: And if you return, We will return meaning if you return to what you were doing of disbelief and misguidance, We will return to you with a similar incident. Al-Suddi said: And if you return means to the opening, We will return meaning to the victory for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his victory and his triumph over his enemies, and the first is stronger, And your faction will not avail you at all, even if it were large meaning even if you gathered from the crowds whatever you could possibly gather, for whoever God is with cannot be defeated, And that God is with the believers and they are the party of the Prophet and the chosen side.
8:20: The Almighty commands His believing servants to obey Him and His Messenger and warns them against disobeying Him and imitating the disbelievers who are stubborn towards Him. For this reason He said, And do not turn away from Him, meaning abandon His obedience and compliance with His commands and abandon His prohibitions, and do not be like those who say, ‘We hear,’ while they do not hear. It was said that what is meant are the polytheists, and Ibn Jarir chose this. Ibn Ishaq said that they are the hypocrites, for they pretend that they have heard and responded, but they are not. Then the Almighty informed that this type of human beings is the worst of creation and creation, so He said, Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of God are the deaf, meaning from hearing the truth, the dumb, from understanding it. For this reason He said, those who do not reason. These are the worst of creation, because every living creature other than them is obedient to God in what He created it for, and these were created for worship, so they disbelieved. For this reason He likened them to livestock in His statement, And the example of those who disbelieve is like that of one who shouts to that which hears nothing but calls and cries, the verse. He said in The other verse: “Those are like livestock, nay, they are more astray. It is those who are the heedless.” It was said that what is meant by those mentioned are a group of Banu Abd al-Dar from Quraysh. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said that they are the hypocrites. I said: There is no contradiction between the polytheists and the hypocrites in this, because each of them is deprived of correct understanding and the intention to do good deeds. Then the Almighty informed that they have no correct understanding and no correct intention, if we assume that they have understanding, so He said: And if God had known any good in them, He would have made them hear. That is, He would have made them understand, and the meaning of the speech is that there is no good in them, so He did not make them understand, because He knows that and if He had made them hear, that is, He made them understand, they would have turned away from that intentionally and stubbornly after understanding it, and they are turning away from it.

8:24: Al-Bukhari said: Respond respond to that which gives you life to that which improves you. Ishaq told me, Ruh told us, Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abd al-Rahman, who said: I heard Hafs bin Asim narrating on the authority of Abu Sa'id bin al-Mu'alla, may God be pleased with him, who said: I was praying when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by me and called me, but I did not come to him until I had prayed, then I came to him and he said: "What prevented you from coming to me? Did not God say: 'O you who believe, respond to God and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life' - then he said: I will teach you the greatest Surah in the Qur'an before I go out." So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to go out and I mentioned it to him. Mu'adh said: Shu'bah told us, on the authority of Khubaib bin Abd al-Rahman, Hafs bin Asim heard Abu Sa'id, a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saying this and saying: Al-Hamdulillah Rabb al-'Alamin is the seven oft-repeated verses. This is its wording verbatim. We have already discussed this hadith by mentioning its chains of transmission at the beginning of the interpretation of al-Fatihah. Mujahid said about His statement, When He gives you life, he said, For the truth. Qatada said, When He gives you life, he said, This is the Qur’an in which there is salvation, survival, and life. Al-Suddi said, When He gives you life, so in Islam, it is their revival after their death in disbelief. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, O you who have believed, respond to God and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life, meaning to the war by which God, the Most High, honored you after humiliation, strengthened you after weakness, and protected you from your enemy after their subjugation of you. God the Almighty said: And know that God intervenes between a person and his heart, Ibn Abbas said: He intervenes between the believer and disbelief, and between the disbeliever and faith. Al-Hakim narrated it in his Mustadrak with a chain of transmission ending with him, and he said: It is authentic, but they did not include it. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from another chain of transmission ending with the Prophet, but it is not authentic due to the weakness of its chain of transmission. The chain of transmission ending with him is more authentic. This is what Mujahid, Sa’id, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Abu Salih, Atiyah, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and As-Suddi said. In a narration from Mujahid regarding his statement: He intervenes between a person and his heart, meaning until he leaves him without reason. As-Suddi said: He intervenes between a person and his heart, so he cannot believe or disbelieve except with His permission. Qatadah said: It is like His statement: And We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. There are hadiths from the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) that are appropriate for this verse. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us from Al-A’mash from Abu Sufyan from Anas ibn Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) used to say frequently: O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. He said: So we said, O Messenger of God, we believe in you and what you have brought, so do you fear for us? He said: Yes, for the hearts are between two fingers of God’s fingers, and He turns them. And thus it was narrated by Al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Al-Qadar in his Jami’ on the authority of Hannad bin Al-Sarri on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah Muhammad bin Hazim Al-Dharee’ on the authority of Al-A’mash, whose name is Sulayman bin Mihran, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, whose name is Talhah bin Nafi’, on the authority of Anas, then he said: It is good. And thus it was narrated on the authority of more than one person on the authority of Al-A’mash, and some of them narrated it on his authority on the authority of Abu Sufyan on the authority of Jabir on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. And the hadith of Abu Sufyan on the authority of Anas is more authentic. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said in his Musnad: Abd bin Hamid told us, Abd al-Malik bin Amr told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abi Laila, on the authority of Bilal, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate, O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. This is a hadith with a good chain of transmission, except that it contains an interruption. However, it meets the conditions of the people of Sunnah, and they did not include it. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I heard Ibn Jabir say: Busr bin Abdullah Al-Hadrami told me that he heard Abu Idris Al-Khawlani say: I heard Al-Nawwas bin Sam’an Al-Kalabi, may God be pleased with him, say: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There is no heart but that it is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Gracious, Lord of the worlds. If He wills to make it straight, He makes it straight, and if He wills to deviate, He deviates it.” And he used to say: O Changer of hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. He said: And the scale is in the hand of the Most Gracious, He lowers it and raises it. And this is how Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid bin Jabir, and he mentioned something similar. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Hammad bin Zaid told us, on the authority of Al-Mu’alla bin Ziyad, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that Aisha said: The supplications that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to make were: O Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. She said: So I said, O Messenger of God, you often make this supplication. He said: “The heart of man is between two of God’s fingers. If He wills, He makes it deviate, and if He wills, He makes it steadfast.” Another Hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us: Abdul Hamid told us: Shahr told me: I heard Umm Salamah narrating that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to frequently say in his supplication: O God, Changer of the hearts, make my heart firm upon Your religion. She said: I said: O Messenger of God, are hearts really changing? He said: “Yes, God has not created any human being from the children of Adam except that his heart is between two fingers of God, the Almighty and Majestic. If He wills, He makes it firm, and if He wills, He makes it deviate. So we ask God, our Lord, not to make our hearts deviate after He has guided us, and we ask Him to bestow upon us mercy from Him, for He is the Bestower.” She said: I said: O Messenger of God, will you not teach me a supplication that I can say for myself? He said: “Yes, say: O God, Lord of the Prophet Muhammad, forgive me my sin, remove the anger in my heart, and save me from the misleading trials as long as You keep me alive.” Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Haywah told us, Abu Hani’ told me that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Habli that he heard Abdullah ibn Amr that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The hearts of the children of Adam are between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, like a single heart, He directs them as He wills. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, the Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience. Muslim alone transmitted it from al-Bukhari, and he narrated it with al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Haywah ibn Shuraih al-Misri with it.
8:25: God Almighty warns His believing servants of a trial, that is, a test and a trial that will befall the wrongdoer and others. It is not limited to those who commit sins or those who have committed the sin, but rather it will befall them both as long as it is not repelled and removed, as Imam Ahmad said: Abu Saeed, a client of Banu Hashim, told us, Shaddad bin Saeed told us, Ghailan bin Jarir told us, on the authority of Mutraf, who said: We said to Al-Zubayr: O Abu Abdullah, what brought you? You neglected the Caliph who was killed, and then you came seeking his blood? Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him, said: We read during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Abu Bakr, Umar, and Uthman, may God be pleased with them, And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those who have wronged among you, and we did not think that we were its people until it happened to us where it happened. Al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Mutraf from Al-Zubayr and he said: We do not know Mutraf who narrated from Al-Zubayr other than this hadith. Al-Nasa’i narrated from the hadith of Jarir ibn Hazim from Al-Hasan from Al-Zubayr something similar to this. Ibn Jarir narrated: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Mubarak ibn Fadala told us from Al-Hasan who said: Al-Zubayr said: It frightened us with it, meaning the words of God Almighty: And fear a trial which will not strike exclusively those who have wronged among you, and we were with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we did not think that we were singled out for it in particular. Hamid narrated it likewise from Al-Hasan from Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with him. Dawud ibn Abi Hind said from Al-Hasan regarding this verse: He said: It was revealed about Ali, Uthman, Talhah, and Al-Zubayr, may God be pleased with them. Sufyan Al-Thawri said from Al-Salt ibn Dinar from Uqbah ibn Sahban, I heard Al-Zubayr said: I read this verse for a long time and I did not see that we were among its people. So we are the ones meant by it: “And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively. And know that God is severe in penalty.” It has been narrated from more than one source on the authority of Al-Zubayr ibn Al-Awwam. Al-Suddi said: It was revealed specifically about the people of Badr, and it struck them on the Day of the Camel, so they fought. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the words of God the Almighty: And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, meaning the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically. And he said in his narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the interpretation of this verse: God commanded the believers not to acknowledge evil among them, lest God punish them all. This is a very good interpretation. For this reason, Mujahid said in his statement, And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively, that it is also for you. And so said Ad-Dahhak, Yazid bin Abi Habib, and more than one. And Ibn Masoud said: There is not one of you who is not encompassed by a trial. God Almighty says: Your wealth and your children are but a trial. So whoever among you seeks refuge, let him seek refuge with God from the misleading trials. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. And the statement that this warning includes the Companions and others, even though the address is with them, is correct. And it is indicated by the hadiths that were mentioned in the most specific of what is mentioned here, what Imam Ahmad narrated where he said: Ahmad bin Al-Hajjaj told us, Abdullah, meaning Ibn Al-Mubarak, told us, Saif bin Abi Sulayman informed us, I heard Adi bin Adi Al-Kindi say, a client of ours told me that he heard my grandfather, meaning Adi bin Umairah, say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: God Almighty does not punish the general public for the actions of the elite until… They see evil among them and they are able to denounce it, but they do not denounce it. If they do that, God will punish the elite and the common people.” There is an accused man in it, and they did not include him in the six books, not even one of them, and God knows best. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman al-Hashimi told us, Ismail told us, meaning Ibn Ja`far, Amr Ibn Abi `Umar told me, on the authority of `Abdullah Ibn `Abd al-Rahman al-Ashhal, on the authority of Hudhayfah Ibn al-Yamani, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, you must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, or God will soon send upon you a punishment from Him, and then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you.” And he narrated it on the authority of Abu Sa`id on the authority of Ismail Ibn Ja`far, who said: Or God will send upon you a people, and then you will call upon Him and He will not respond to you. Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Numayr told us: Razeen Habib al-Juhani told us: Abu al-Raqqad told me: I went out with my master and I was handed over to Hudhayfah while he was saying: If a man spoke a word during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would become a hypocrite, and I would hear it from one of you four times in one place: You must enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and encourage one another to do good, or God will destroy you all with a punishment, or He will appoint the worst of you over you, then the best of you will call out but their supplication will not be answered. Another hadith Imam Ahmad also said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to me on the authority of Zakariya, on the authority of Amer, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard Al-Nu’man bin Bashir, may God be pleased with him, delivering a sermon, saying: And he pointed with his fingers to his ears, saying: The example of one who upholds the limits of God, one who transgresses them, and one who flatters them is like the example of people who boarded a ship. Some of them reached its lower part, its roughest part, and its worst part, and some of them reached its upper part. When those on the lower part wanted to draw water, they had to pass by those on top of them and harm them. They said: If we make a hole in our share and draw water from it without harming those on top of us, then if they leave them to their own devices, they will all perish, but if they take them by the hand, they will all be saved. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it, not Muslim. It was narrated in Al-Sharikah wa Al-Shahadat, and Al-Tirmidhi in Al-Fitan from other chains of transmission on the authority of Sulayman bin Mihran Al-A’mash on the authority of Amer bin Shurahil Al-Sha’bi on his authority. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hussain told us, Khalaf bin Khalifa told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Al-Ma’rur bin Suwaid, on the authority of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When sins appear among my nation, God will afflict them with a punishment from Him. I said: O Messenger of God, are there not righteous people among them? He said: Yes. She said: So what will those people do? He said: What afflicts the people afflicts them, then they will attain forgiveness from God and His pleasure. Another hadith Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Mundhir bin Jarir, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no people who commit sins and among them is a man more honorable and more powerful than them, and he does not change him except that God will afflict them with punishment or the punishment will befall them.” Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of Musaddad, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on his authority. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Abu Ishaq narrating on the authority of `Ubaydullah ibn Jarir, on the authority of his father, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There are no people among whom sins are committed who are more honorable and more numerous than those who commit them and then do not change them, except that God will punish them all. Then he also narrated it on the authority of Waki`, on the authority of Isra`il, and on the authority of `Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Aswad, on the authority of Sharik and Yunus, all on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi`i, on his authority. Ibn Majah included it on the authority of `Ali ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Waki`, on his authority. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, Jami` ibn Abi Rashid told us, on the authority of Mundhir, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his wife, on the authority of `Aishah, conveying it to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, When evil appears on earth, God sends down His punishment upon the people of the earth. I said: And among them are the people of obedience to God? He said: Yes, then they will be brought to the mercy of God.
8:26: God Almighty reminds His believing servants of His blessings upon them and His kindness to them, as they were few, so He made them many, and weak and afraid, so He strengthened them and aided them, and poor and dependent, so He provided them with good things and thanked them, so they obeyed Him and complied with everything He commanded them. This was the state of the believers when they were in Mecca, few, hidden, persecuted, fearing that people from all over the lands of God would snatch them away, polytheists, Zoroastrians, and Romans, all of whom were enemies to them because of their small number and lack of strength. This was their way until God gave them permission to migrate to Medina, so He sheltered them there and provided for them its people, who sheltered and supported them on the day of Badr and other days. They helped each other with their money and sacrificed their lives in obedience to God and His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Qatada bin Di’amah Al-Sadosi, may God have mercy on him, said regarding the words of God Almighty: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, he said: This tribe of Arabs was the most humiliated of people, the most miserable in life, the hungriest in stomachs, the most naked in skins, and the most clearly astray. Whoever lived among them lived miserably, and whoever died among them was thrown into the Fire, being eaten but not eaten. By God, we do not know of a tribe from the people of the earth at that time who were worse off than them until God brought Islam and established it in the lands and expanded By it, He provided them with sustenance and made them kings over the necks of the people. By Islam, God gave what you saw, so thank God for His blessings, for your Lord is a benefactor who loves thanks, and the thankful will have more from God.
8:27: Abd al-Razzaq ibn Abi Qatada and al-Zuhri said: It was revealed about Abu Lubabah ibn Abd al-Mundhir when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent him to Banu Qurayzah to accept the ruling of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They consulted him about that, and he advised them to do that, and he pointed with his hand to his throat, meaning that it was slaughter. Then Abu Lubabah realized and saw that he had betrayed God and His Messenger, so he swore that he would not taste anything until he died or God repented of him. He went to the mosque of Medina and tied himself to a pillar of it, and he remained like that for nine days until he was falling unconscious from the effort until God revealed his repentance to His Messenger. Then the people came to give him the good report of God’s repentance, and they wanted to release him from the pillar, but he swore that no one would release him from it except the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his hand, so he released him, and he said: O Messenger of God, I vowed that I would give away from my wealth in charity, so he said: A third of it is sufficient for you to give in charity. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Abdul Aziz told us, Yunus bin Al-Harith Al-Ta’ifi told us, Muhammad bin Ubaid God bin Awn Al-Thaqafi told us, on the authority of Al-Mughira bin Shu’ba, who said: This verse was revealed regarding the killing of Uthman, may God be pleased with him: O you who have believed, do not betray God and the Messenger the verse. Ibn Jarir also said: Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf told us, Shababah bin Suwar told us, Muhammad bin Al-Muharram told us, he said: I met Ata bin Abi Rabah, so he told me, he said: Jabir bin Abdullah told me that Abu Sufyan left Mecca, so Gabriel came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Sufyan is in such and such a place, so go out to him and conceal it, so a man from the hypocrites wrote to him, Muhammad wants you, so be careful, so God Almighty revealed: Do not betray God and the Messenger, nor betray your trusts, the verse, this is a very strange hadith, and its chain of transmission and context are questionable, and in the two Sahihs there is the story of Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, that he wrote to the Quraysh informing them of the Messenger of God’s intention to them in the year of the conquest, so God informed His Messenger of that, so he sent after the letter and retrieved it and brought Hatib, so he confessed to what he had done, and in it Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up and said: O Messenger of God, should I not strike his neck, for he has betrayed. God, His Messenger, and the believers? He said: "Leave him, for he witnessed Badr. How do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you." I said: The correct view is that the verse is general, and if it is true that it was revealed for a specific reason, then the majority of scholars take the generality of the wording and not the specificity of the reason. Treachery includes minor and major sins, both necessary and transitive. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And betray your trusts. The trust is the deeds that God has entrusted to His servants, meaning the obligatory duties. He says: Do not betray do not break them. And he said in another narration: Do not betray God and the Messenger, meaning by abandoning His Sunnah and committing a sin against Him. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr told me on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr regarding this verse, meaning: Do not show him the truth that will please him, then contradict him in secret to something else, for that will destroy your trusts and betray yourselves. Al-Suddi said: If they betrayed God and the Messenger, then they have betrayed their trusts. He also said: They used to hear hadith from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and then spread it until it reached the polytheists. `Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: He forbade you from betraying God and the Messenger as the hypocrites did. His statement, And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial, means a test and examination from Him for you, as He gave them to you to know whether you would thank Him for them and obey Him in them or be busy with them instead of Him and compensate Him for them, as God the Almighty said: Your wealth and your children are but a trial, and God has with Him a great reward. And He said: And We test you with evil and with good as a trial. God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of God. And whoever does that - then it is those who are the losers.” God the Almighty said: O you who have believed, indeed, among your wives and your children are enemies to you, so beware of them. And His statement: And that God has with Him a great reward means that His reward, His gifts, and His gardens are better for you than wealth and children, because there may be enemies among them, and most of them will not benefit you at all. God the Almighty is the Disposer and Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and He has a great reward on the Day of Resurrection. In the hadith, God Almighty says: O son of Adam, seek Me and you will find Me. If you find Me, you will find everything, and if you lose Me, you will lose everything. I am dearer to you than everything. In the Sahih, it is narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “There are three things in whomsoever they are found, he will find the sweetness of faith: he who loves God and His Messenger more than anything else, he who loves a person and loves him only for God’s sake, and he who would rather be thrown into the Fire than return to disbelief after God has saved him from it.” Rather, the love of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, takes precedence over children, wealth, and souls, as it is proven in the Sahih that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, none of you will believe until I am dearer to him than his own self, his family, his wealth, and all of mankind.
