8:29: Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hayyan and others said, Furqan means a way out. Mujahid added, In this world and the hereafter. In a narration from Ibn Abbas, Furqan means salvation, and in a narration from him, victory. Muhammad bin Ishaq said, Furqan means a separation between truth and falsehood. This interpretation from Ibn Ishaq is more general than what was mentioned above and it entails all of that. For whoever fears God by doing what He commands and abandons what He forbids will be guided to know truth from falsehood, and that will be the reason for his victory, salvation, and way out from worldly affairs and his happiness on the Day of Resurrection, and the expiation of his sins, which is their erasure, and their forgiveness, which is their concealment from people, and a reason for attaining God's abundant reward, as God the Almighty says: "O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy and provide for you a light by which you will walk and forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful."
8:30: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah said: Lithabatuk means to bind you. Ata' and Ibn Zayd said: Lithabatuk. Al-Suddi said: Ithbaat means to imprison and chain you. This includes what these and those said, and it is the sum of the sayings. It is the most common action of those who want to harm others. Sunayd said on the authority of Hajjaj on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Ata' said: I heard Ubayd ibn Umair say: When they conspired against the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to imprison him, kill him or expel him, his uncle Abu Talib said to him: Do you know what they conspired against you? He said: They want to bewitch me, or kill me, or expel me. He said: Who told you this? He said: My Lord. He said: Yes, your Lord is your Lord. Treat Him well. He said: I treat him well, rather he treats me well. Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Masry, known as Al-Waswasi, told me, Abdul Hamid bin Abi Dawud told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, on the authority of Al-Muttalib bin Abi Wada’ah, that Abu Talib said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: What do your people plot against you? He said: They want to bewitch me, or kill me, or expel me. He said: Who told you this? He said: My Lord. He said: Yes, your Lord is a good Lord, so treat Him well. He said: I treat Him well, rather he treats me well. He said: Then the verse was revealed: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you or kill you or expel you 10:13. The mention of Abu Talib in this is very strange, indeed it is reprehensible, because this verse is Medinan, then this story and the gathering of the Quraysh on this conspiracy and consultation on confirmation or denial or killing was only on the night of the migration, and that was about three years after the death of Abu Talib when they were able to do it and dared to do it because of the death of his uncle Abu Talib who used to protect him and support him and take care of his burdens, and the evidence for the correctness of what we said is what Imam Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar, the author of Al-Maghazi, narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Kalbi told me on the authority of Bazan, the freed slave of Umm Hani’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas that a group of the Quraysh from the nobles of each tribe gathered to enter the House of Assembly, and Satan intercepted them in the form of a venerable old man, and when they saw him they said to him who are you? He said an old man from the people of Najd, I heard that you gathered and I wanted to attend to you and you will not be deprived of my opinion and advice. They said: Yes, enter. So he entered with them and said: Look into the matter of this man, by God he is about to attack you in your matter with his command. One of them said: Imprison him in chains and then await the vicissitudes of fate until he perishes as the poets before him, Zuhair and An-Nabigha, perished. He is just like one of them. Then the enemy of God, the Najdi sheikh, cried out and said: By God, this is not your opinion. By God, his Lord will bring him out of his prison to his companions, and they will soon attack him and seize him from your hands and prevent him from you. I do not feel safe that they will expel you from your country. They said: The sheikh has spoken the truth, so look into something else. One of them said: Take him out from among you and you will be relieved of him, for if he goes out, what he has done will not harm you. Where will he fall if his harm is absent from you and you are relieved and his matter is not with you? The Najdi sheikh said: By God, this is not your opinion. Have you not seen the sweetness of his speech and the fluency of his tongue? And what you hear of his speech captures hearts? By God, if you do that, then the Arabs will gather around him and come to you until he expels you from your country and kills your nobles. They said, By God, he is telling the truth, so look for a different opinion. Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, By God, I will advise you with an opinion that I have not seen before, I do not see anything else. They said, What is it? He said, You should take from each tribe a young, well-built, strong boy, then give each boy a sharp sword, then strike him with one blow, and when they kill him his blood will be distributed among all the tribes. I do not think that this tribe of Banu Hashim will be able to fight the entire Quraysh. If they see that, they will accept reason and we will be relieved and his harm will be cut off from us. The Najdi sheikh said, By God, this is the opinion, the statement is what the young man said, I do not see anything else. They said, So they dispersed on that and they agreed on it. Then Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ordered him not to spend the night in the bed in which he used to sleep, and informed him of the plot of the people, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not spend the night in his house that night, and God gave him permission to go out, and God revealed to him after his arrival in Medina Al-Anfal, mentioning His blessings upon him and His trials with him: And when those who disbelieved plotted against you to confine you or kill you or expel you - and they plotted, and God plotted - and God is the best of plotters. And He revealed regarding their saying that they were waiting for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate until he perished as the poets who came before him had perished: Or do they say, ‘He is a poet; we are waiting for him to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate?’ So that day was called the Day of the Crowd because of the opinion they had agreed upon. Al-Suddi narrated something similar to this context, and God revealed regarding their intention to expel him, His Most High saying: “And indeed they almost drove you from the land to expel you from it. And in that case they would not remain behind you except a little.” And this is what Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated from Mujahid, Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, Musa ibn Uqbah, Qatadah, Muqsim, and more than one. To that end, Yunus bin Bakir said on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, waited for God’s command until the Quraysh gathered and plotted against him and intended to do what they intended to do to him, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and ordered him not to spend the night in the place where he used to spend the night. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Ali bin Abi Talib and ordered him to spend the night on his bed and cover himself with his green cloak, so he did. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to the people while they were at his door, and he went out with him with a handful of dirt and began to sprinkle it on their heads, and God took away their sight from His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was reciting, “Ya Seen. By the Wise Qur’an. Indeed, you are of the messengers. On a straight path. A revelation from the Almighty, the Merciful. That you may warn a people whose fathers were not warned, so they are heedless. The word has already come into effect upon most of them, so they do not believe. Indeed, We have placed shackles on their necks, reaching to their chins, so their heads are raised. And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them so that they do not see.” Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: It was narrated on the authority of Ikrimah that which confirms this. Ibn Hibban narrated in his Sahih and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abdullah bin Othman bin Khathim on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Fatima entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she was crying, so he said: What makes you cry, my daughter? She said: O my father, why should I not cry while these leaders of Quraysh are in Al-Hijr, pledging allegiance to Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other. If they saw you, they would rise up to you and kill you, and there is none among them except those who have recognized their share of your blood. He said: O my daughter, bring me water for ablution. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, performed ablution and then went out to the mosque. When they saw him, they said: Here he is. They lowered their heads and their necks fell before them, and they did not raise their eyes. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of dirt and threw it at them and said: May your faces be disfigured. Not a single one of their pebbles struck a man except that he killed an unbeliever on the day of Badr. Then Al-Hakim said: It is authentic according to the conditions of Muslim, but they did not include it, and I do not know of any defect in it. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, Uthman al-Jazari told me, on the authority of Muqsim, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, who told him about his statement: And when he plotted against you verse, he said: Quraysh consulted one night in Mecca. Some of them said: When morning comes, tie him up, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Some of them said: Rather, kill him. Some of them said: Rather, take him out. So God informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of that, so Ali, may God be pleased with him, spent the night on the bed of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out until he reached the cave, and the polytheists spent the night guarding Ali, thinking that he was the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When morning came, they rose up against him, and when they saw Ali, God Almighty repelled their plot, so they said: Where is your companion? He said, I do not know. So they followed his tracks, and when they reached the mountain, they were confused, so they climbed the mountain and passed by the cave. They saw a spider’s web over its entrance, and they said, If he had entered here, the spider’s web would not have been over its entrance. So he stayed in it for three nights. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, regarding his statement, And they plot, and God plots, and God is the best of plotters, meaning, I plotted against them with My mighty plot until I saved you from them.
8:31: God Almighty tells us about the disbelief of the Quraysh, their arrogance, rebellion, stubbornness and false claims when they hear His verses recited to them, that they say, "We have heard. If we wished, we could say something like this." This is a statement from them without action. Otherwise, they have been challenged more than once to bring a surah like it, but they did not find a way to do so. Rather, this statement from them is to deceive themselves and those who follow them in their falsehood. It has been said that the one who said this was Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, may God curse him, as Saeed ibn Jubayr, Al-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj and others have stated. He, may God curse him, had gone to the land of Persia and learned from the report of their kings, Rustam and Isfandiyar. When he returned, he found that God had sent the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he was reciting the Qur’an to the people. So whenever he, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up from a gathering in which Al-Nadr was sitting, he would tell them some of the report of those people and then say, By God, who is better at telling stories, me or Muhammad? And for this reason, when God the Almighty enabled him on the day of Badr and he was taken captive, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered that his neck be struck in front of him, and he did so, praise be to God. And the one who took him prisoner was Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, may God be pleased with him, as Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, killed in the day of Badr, Uqbah bin Abi Mu’ayt, Tu’aymah bin Adi, and Al-Nadr bin Al-Harith. Al-Miqdad had taken Al-Nadr captive, and when he ordered him to be killed, Al-Miqdad said: O Messenger of God, my prisoner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He used to say in the Book of God the Almighty what he said, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered him to be killed. Al-Miqdad said: O Messenger of God, my prisoner. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, enrich Al-Miqdad from Your bounty. Al-Miqdad said: This is what I wanted. He said: And in it this verse was revealed: “And when Our verses are recited to them, they say: We have heard. If we willed, we could say the like of this. This is not but legends of the ancients.” And Hisham narrated it likewise on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja’far bin Abi Dihya narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he said Al-Mut'am bin Adi instead of Ta'ima, and this is a mistake because Al-Mut'am bin Adi was not alive on the day of Badr, and for this reason the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on that day: If Al-Mut'am bin Adi were alive and then asked me about these stinking ones, I would have given them to him, meaning the prisoners, because he had granted protection to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day he returned from Ta'if. The meaning of Legends of the ancients is the plural of legend, meaning he wrote them, so he learns from them and recites them to the people, and this is a pure lie as God informed us about them in the other verse: "And they said, 'Legends of the ancients, which he wrote down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening. Say, 'It was sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.'" That is, for whoever repents to Him and returns to Him, He accepts from him and pardons him. And His statement: And when they said, 'O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment.' This is due to the greatness of their ignorance and the intensity of their denial, stubbornness and insolence, and this is what they were criticized for, and it would have been more appropriate for them. Ibn Abi Hatim said, “My father told us, ‘Abd al-Ghaffar ibn Dawud told us, An-Nadr ibn ‘Arabi told us, Ibn ‘Abbas said, ‘God has placed in this nation two types of security that will remain infallible and protected from the blows of punishment as long as they are among them. There is a security that God has taken to Himself and a security that remains with you. His statement, “And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness.” Abu Salih ‘Abd al-Ghaffar said, Some of our companions told me that An-Nadr ibn ‘Adi told him this hadith on the authority of Mujahid on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas. Ibn Mardawayh narrated something similar to this on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari. It was also narrated on the authority of Qatadah and Abu al-‘Ala’ an-Nahwi al-Muqri. Al-Tirmidhi said: Sufyan ibn Wakee’ told us, Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, on the authority of Ibad ibn Yusuf, on the authority of Abu Burdah ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God sent down to me security for my nation: ‘And God would not punish them while you are among them, nor would God punish them while they seek forgiveness. ’ So when I pass away, I will leave them seeking forgiveness until the Day of Resurrection.” This is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad and Al-Hakim in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Wahb: Amr ibn Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu Al-Haitham, on the authority of Abu Saeed, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The devil said: ‘By Your glory, O Lord, I will not cease to mislead Your servants as long as their souls are in their bodies.’ The Lord said: ‘By My glory and majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek My forgiveness. ’” Then Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it. Imam Ahmad said: Muawiyah bin Amr told us, Rashdin told us, he is Ibn Saad, Muawiyah bin Saad Al-Tujibi told me, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Fadala bin Ubaid, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The servant is safe from the punishment of God as long as he seeks forgiveness from God Almighty.
8:34: The Almighty informs us that they are worthy of being punished, but that was not done to them due to the blessing of the Prophet's position among them. That is why when he left them, God inflicted His wrath upon them on the day of Badr, killing their leaders and taking their noble ones prisoner. The Almighty guided them to seek forgiveness for the sins they were committing, such as polytheism and corruption. Qatada, As-Suddi, and others said: The people did not seek forgiveness, and if they had sought forgiveness, they would not have been punished. Ibn Jarir chose it, for if there were not among them the weak believers who sought forgiveness, the calamity that could not be averted would have befallen them, but it was averted from them because of those, as God Almighty said on the day of Hudaybiyyah: “They are the ones who disbelieved and prevented you from the Sacred Mosque and the offerings were held back from reaching their destination. And had it not been for believing men and believing women whom you did not know, lest you trample them and there should befall you on their part a disgrace without knowledge. That God may admit into His mercy whom He wills. Had they separated themselves, We would have punished those who disbelieved among them with a painful punishment.” Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibn Abza, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca when God revealed, And God would not punish them while you are among them. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Medina, and God revealed, And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. He said: Those remaining Muslims who remained there were weak, meaning in Mecca, seeking forgiveness. So when they went out, God revealed, And why should God not punish them while they prevent [people] from the Sacred Mosque, and they were not its guardians? He said: So God permitted the conquest of Mecca, and it was the punishment that He had promised them. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Abu Malik, Ad-Dahhak and others something similar to this. It has been said that this verse abrogates the words of God Almighty: And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, meaning that what is meant is that they seek forgiveness from themselves. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadeh told us, from Al-Hussein bin Waqid, from Yazid An-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: It was said in al-Anfal 8:And God would not punish them while you are among them, and God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness, so it was abrogated by the verse that follows it: “And what is the matter with them that God should not punish them while they prevent [people] from Al-Masjid Al-Haram, and they were not its guardians? His guardians are only the righteous, but most of them do not know. And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve,” so they were fought in Mecca and hunger and harm afflicted them there. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it likewise from the hadith of Abu Numailah Yahya bin Wadeh. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Hajjaj bin Muhammad told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj and Uthman bin Ata’, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And God would not punish them while they seek forgiveness. Then he made an exception for the polytheists, saying, And why should God not punish them while they prevent [people] from Al-Masjid Al-Haram? Its guardians are only the righteous, but most of them do not know.” That is, how could God not punish them while they prevent people from Al-Masjid Al-Haram? That is, the one in Mecca, preventing the believers who are its people from praying in it and circumambulating it? That is, they are not the people of Al-Masjid Al-Haram, rather its people are the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, as God the Almighty said, “It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of God while they bear witness against themselves of disbelief. Those, their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally. The mosques of God shall be maintained only by those who believe in God and the Last Day and establish prayer and give zakah and do not fear except God.” Perhaps those will be among the guided. God the Almighty said: And averting from the way of God and disbelieving in Him and in al-Masjid al-Haram and expelling his people from it are greater in the sight of God, the verse. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh said in his interpretation of this verse: Sulayman bin Ahmad, who is al-Tabarani, told us, Ja’far bin Ilyas bin Sadaqah al-Masri told us, Na’im bin Hammad told us, Nuh bin Abi Maryam told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Sa’id al-Ansari, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked, Who are your allies? He said, Everyone who is righteous. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, His allies are none but the righteous. Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Abu Bakr al-Shafi’i told us, Ishaq bin al-Hasan told us, Abu Hudhayfah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Khathim, on the authority of Ismail bin Ubayd bin Rafa’ah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered the Quraysh and said: Is there among you anyone other than you? They said: Our nephew is among us, our ally is among us, and our master is among us. He said: “Our ally is among us, our nephew is among us, and our master is among us. Indeed, my allies among you are the righteous.” Then he said: This is correct, and they did not include it. Urwah, al-Suddi, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said regarding the words of God Almighty: His allies are none but the righteous. He said: They are Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, may God be pleased with them. Mujahid said: They are the mujahideen, whoever they were and wherever they were. Then the Almighty mentioned what they used to do at the Sacred Mosque, and how they used to treat it, so He said: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands. Abdullah bin Amr, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Abu Raja’ al-Attardi, Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi, Hajar bin Unbas, Nabit bin Sharit, Qatadah, and Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: It is whistling. Mujahid added: They used to put their fingers in their mouths. Al-Suddi said: The whistling is like a white bird called the muka’ and it is found in the land of the Hijaz. And clapping of hands. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Khallad Sulayman bin Khallad told us, Yunus bin Muhammad al-Mu’addib told us, Ya’qub, meaning Ibn Abdullah al-Ash’ari, told us, Ja’far bin al-Mughira told us on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: And their prayer at the House was nothing but whistling and clapping of hands. He said: The whistling is the whistling and clapping of hands is clapping. Qurra said: And he narrated: We have a gift for Ibn Omar, so Ibn Omar whistled and tilted his cheek and clapped his hands, and from Ibn Omar also that he said: They used to put their cheeks on the ground and clap and whistle. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in his interpretation with his chain of transmission from him. And Ikrimah said: They used to circumambulate the House on the left, Mujahid said: They only did that to confuse the Prophet’s prayer, may God bless him and grant him peace, and Al-Zuhri said: They mock the believers, and from Saeed bin Jubair and Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid and turning away he said people turned them away from the path of God Almighty. 8:36: Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Al-Zuhri, Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Hibban, Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada, and Al-Husayn ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr ibn Sa`id ibn Mu`adh told me that when the Quraysh were defeated on the day of Badr and their camels returned to Mecca, and Abu Sufyan returned with his camel, Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi`ah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and Sufyan ibn Umayyah walked with men from the Quraysh whose fathers, sons, and brothers had been defeated at Badr. They spoke to Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and those who had business with the Quraysh in that caravan, and said: O people of the Quraysh, Muhammad has left you and killed your best, so help us with this money to fight him so that we may take revenge on him for those of us who were defeated. So they did. He said: Regarding them, as mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, God Almighty revealed: “Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of God. So they will spend it; then it will be for them a cause of regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will be gathered to Hell. So God may distinguish the wicked from the good and make the wicked…” And it was also narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Hakam bin Uyaynah, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ibn Abza that it was revealed about Abu Sufyan and his spending of money at Uhud to fight the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ad-Dahhak said: It was revealed about the people of Badr. In any case, it is general, even if the reason for its revelation was specific. God the Almighty has informed us that the disbelievers spend their money to turn people away from following the path of truth. They will do that, then their money will be lost, and then it will be a cause of regret for them, meaning remorse, since it will not find anything, because they wanted to extinguish the light of God and the emergence of their word over the word of truth. God will perfect His light, even if the disbelievers hate it. And He is the supporter of His religion, the proclaimer of His word, and the manifester of His religion over every religion. This is disgrace for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire. Whoever among them lives will see with his eyes and hear with his ears what displeases him, and whoever among them is killed or dies will go to eternal disgrace and everlasting punishment. For this reason, He said: “And they will spend it, then it will be a cause of regret for them, then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieve will go to Hell.” They will be gathered together. And the Almighty’s saying: That God may distinguish the wicked from the good. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: That God may distinguish the wicked from the good, so he distinguishes the people of happiness from the people of misery. Al-Suddi said: He distinguishes the believer from the disbeliever. This may mean that this distinction will be in the Hereafter, like His saying: Then We will say to those who associated partners with God, ‘Where are you and your partners?’ So We will separate them. And the Almighty said: And separate yourselves today, O criminals. Those are the losers," that is, these are the losers in this world and the hereafter.

8:38: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Say to those who have disbelieved, if they desist meaning from their disbelief, opposition, and stubbornness and enter Islam, obedience, and repentance, they will be forgiven for what has passed, meaning their disbelief, sins, and transgressions, as came in the Sahih from the hadith of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever does good in Islam will not be held accountable for what he did in the Jahiliyyah, and whoever does evil in Islam will be held accountable for the first and the last. And in the Sahih also, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Islam wipes out what came before it, and repentance wipes out what came before it. And His statement, But if they return meaning if they continue in what they are doing, Then has already passed the precedent of the former peoples meaning Our precedent has passed with the former peoples, that if they lie and continue in their stubbornness, we will hasten them with punishment and chastisement. Mujahid said regarding His statement, Then has already passed the precedent of the former peoples meaning with the Quraysh on the day of Badr and other nations. Al-Suddi and Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, meaning on the day Badr. And the saying of God the Almighty: And fight them until there is no more persecution and religion is all for God. Al-Bukhari said: Al-Hasan bin Abdul Aziz narrated to us, Abdullah bin Yahya narrated to us, Haywah bin Shuraih narrated to us, from Bakr bin Umar, from Bakir, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar that a man came and said: O Abu Abdul Rahman, will you not do what God mentioned in His Book: And if two parties among the believers should fight (al-Baqarah 2:17). So what prevents you from fighting as God mentioned in His Book? He said: O my nephew, I am criticized for this verse, and I do not like to fight more than to be criticized for the verse in which God the Almighty says: And whoever kills a believer intentionally to the end of the verse. He said: God the Almighty says: And fight them until there is no more persecution (al-Baqarah 2:17). Ibn Umar said: We did that during the time of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) when Islam was few and a man would be tested in his religion, either by killing him or by chaining him until Islam became widespread and there was no more persecution. When he saw that he did not agree with what he wanted, he said: What do you say about Ali and Uthman? Ibn Umar said: As for my statement about Ali and Uthman, as for Uthman, God had forgiven him and you hated that God should forgive him. As for Ali, he is the cousin of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his son-in-law, and he pointed with his hand, and this is his daughter or his daughter, as you can see. Ahmad bin Yunus narrated to us, Zuhair narrated to us, Bayan narrated to us that Ibn Wabra narrated to him, Saeed bin Jubair narrated to me, he said: Ibn Umar may God be pleased with them came out to us and said: What do you think about fighting during the fitnah? He said: Do you know what fitnah is? Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fought the polytheists, and entering upon them was a fitnah, and your fighting is not for the sake of the kingdom. All of this is in the context of Al-Bukhari may God have mercy on him. Ubaydullah narrated from Nafi’ from Ibn Umar that two men came to him during the fitnah of Ibn Az-Zubayr and said: The people have done what you see, and you are the son of Umar bin Al-Khattab and you are the companion of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so what prevents you from coming out? He said: What prevents me is that God has made the blood of my Muslim brother sacred to me. They said: Did God not say: And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is all for God? He said, "We fought until there was no more persecution and the religion was all for God. And you want to fight until there is persecution and the religion is for other than God." Hammad ibn Salamah narrated the same from Ali ibn Zayd from Ayyub ibn Abdullah al-Lakhmi, who said, I was with Abdullah ibn Umar may God be pleased with them when a man came to him and said, 'God says, 'And fight them until there is no more persecution and the religion is all for God.' He said, We fought until there was no more persecution, and you want to fight until there is persecution and the religion is for other than God. Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it the same way. Ibn Umar said, 'I and my companions fought until the religion was all for God, and polytheism was gone and there was no persecution, but you and your companions will fight until there is persecution and the religion is for other than God.'" Both of them were narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Abu Uwanah said, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Taymi, on the authority of his father, who said, "Dhu al-Batin, meaning Usamah ibn Zayd, said, 'I will never fight a man who says, 'There is no god but God,' ever." Sa'd ibn Malik said: By God, I will never fight a man who says, "There is no god but God. A man said, Didn't God say, 'And fight them until there is no more persecution and the religion is all for God'? They said, We fought until there was no more persecution and the religion was all for God." Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "And fight them until there is no more persecution," meaning there is no more polytheism. This is what Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, al-Suddi, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and Zayd ibn Aslam said. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: It was conveyed to me on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and other scholars of ours, that "until there is no more persecution," until no Muslim is tempted to abandon his religion. And His statement, "and the religion is all for God," Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: "Monotheism is to be sincerely devoted to God. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj said, And the religion is all for God, meaning that one says, There is no god but God." Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Monotheism is to be sincerely devoted to God, with no polytheism in it, and all rivals besides Him are to be rejected. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: And the religion will be entirely for God, and there will be no disbelief with your religion. This is supported by what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ When they say it, their blood and wealth are protected from me, except for a right, and their reckoning is with God, the Almighty.” And in them on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights bravely, fights out of pride, and fights to show off, which of these is in the way of God, the Almighty? He said: Whoever fights so that the word of God is supreme is in the way of God, the Almighty. And His statement, But if they desist, meaning by fighting you from what they are doing of disbelief, then desist from it. And if you do not know their inner motives, then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do, like His statement, But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way, the verse. And in the other verse, Then they are your brothers in religion, and He said, “And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is for God. But if they desist, then there shall be no aggression except against the wrongdoers.” And in the Sahih: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Usama, when that man raised his sword and said, There is no god but God, so he struck him and killed him. This was mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to Usama, Did you kill him after he said, ‘There is no god but God?’ And what will you do with ‘There is no god but God’ on the Day of Resurrection? He said, O Messenger of God, he only said it as a means of protection. He said, Why didn’t you split open his heart? And he kept saying and repeating to him, Who will have ‘There is no god but God’ on the Day of Resurrection? Usama said, Until I wished that I had not converted to Islam until that day. And His statement, But if they turn away, then know that God is your Protector; what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper. That is, if they persist in opposing you and fighting you, then know that God is your Protector, your Master and your Helper against your enemies; what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper. Muhammad ibn Jarir said: Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad told me, my father told us, Aban al-Attar told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah, that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to him asking him about some things, so Urwah wrote to him: Peace be upon you, for I praise to you God, there is no god but Him. And after that, you wrote to me asking me about the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, and I will tell you about it, and there is no power or strength except with God. The reason for the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca was that God gave him prophethood, so what a good prophet, what a good master, and what a good clan, so may God reward him with good, and may we know his face in Paradise, and may He make us live upon his religion and cause us to die and resurrect us upon it, and that when he called his people to what God sent him with of guidance and light that He sent down upon him, they did not turn away from him at first when he called them to it, and they listened to him, until he mentioned their tyrants, and some people from Taif from Quraysh who had wealth came, some people denounced that to him and were harsh with him, and they hated what he said and tempted with it those who obeyed them, so the majority of the people turned away from him, and they left him except for those whom God preserved from them, and they were few, and he remained in that for as long as God had decreed that he should remain, then their leaders conspired to tempt those who followed him from the religion of God from their sons, brothers, and tribes, and it was a severe earthquake, so whoever was tempted was tempted and God protected what He wanted them to, so when he did that to the Muslims, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to the land of Abyssinia. There was a righteous king in Abyssinia, called the Negus, who did not wrong anyone in his land, and he was praised for that. The land of Abyssinia was a market for the Quraysh, and it was a place where their merchants would find comfort, security, and good trade. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go there, and most of them went there when they were defeated in Mecca, and they feared sedition for them. He stayed and did not leave, and they remained like that for years, being harsh on those who converted to Islam from among them. Then Islam spread there, and men from their nobles and their fortifications entered it. When they saw that, they relaxed and relaxed about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. The first sedition was the one that drove those of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who left before the land of Abyssinia, fearing it and fleeing from the seditions and earthquakes they were in. So when he relaxed about them and those who entered Islam from among them talked about their relaxation about them, and it reached those who… There were some companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Abyssinia who were relaxed about those of them who were in Mecca, and that they would not be tempted, so they returned to Mecca and were almost safe there, and they began to increase and multiply, and that many people from the Ansar in Medina converted to Islam, and Islam spread in Medina and the people of Medina began to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca. When the Quraysh saw that, they plotted to tempt them and intensify, so they seized them and were keen to tempt them, and they were afflicted with great hardship, and there was the last temptation, and there were two temptations: a temptation that drove those of them who went to the land of Abyssinia when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to do so and gave them permission to go out to it, and a temptation: when they returned and saw those who came to them from the people of Medina, then seventy leaders came from Medina, the heads of those who converted to Islam, and they met him during the Hajj and pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, and gave him their pledges and covenants, that I am from you and you are from us, and that whoever of your companions comes or you come to us, then we will… We prevent you from what we prevent ourselves from. Then the Quraysh became intense against them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to go out to Medina. This was the last tribulation in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions, and he went out himself. It was the one in which God, the Almighty, revealed: And fight them until there is no more persecution and religion is all for God. Then he narrated it on the authority of Yunus bin Abdul-A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abdul-Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad on the authority of his father, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, that he wrote to Al-Walid, meaning Ibn Abdul-Malik bin Marwan, about this, and he mentioned something similar. This is authentic up to Urwah, may God have mercy on him.
