Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fought the polytheists and entering upon them was a fitnah, and your fighting is not for the sake of the kingdom. All of this is the context of Bukhari may God have mercy on him. Ubaydullah said on the authority of Nafi’ on the authority of Ibn Umar that two men came to him during the fitnah of Ibn al-Zubayr and said: The people have done what you see, and you are the son of Umar bin al-Khattab and you are the companion of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so what prevents you from coming out? He said: What prevents me is that God has forbidden me to shed the blood of my Muslim brother. They said: Did God not say: And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is all for God? He said: We fought until there was no more fitnah and the religion was all for God, and you want to fight until there is more fitnah and the religion is for other than God. Hammad bin Salamah narrated the same from Ali bin Zaid from Ayoub bin Abdullah Al-Lakhmi, who said: I was with Abdullah bin Omar may God be pleased with them when a man came to him and said: God says: And fight them until there is no more fitnah and the religion is all for God. He said: We fought until there was no more fitnah, and you want to fight until there is more fitnah and the religion is for other than God. Hammad bin Salamah narrated the same. Ibn Omar said: I and my companions fought until the religion was all for God, and polytheism was gone and there was no fitnah, but you and your companions will fight until there is more fitnah and the religion is for other than God. Both of them narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Abu Awanah said: On the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim At-Taimi, on the authority of his father, who said: Dhu Al-Batin, meaning Usamah bin Zaid, said: I will never fight a man who says there is no god but God. Saad bin Malik said: By God, I will never fight a man who says, There is no god but God. A man said: Didn’t God say, And fight them until there is no more persecution and the religion is all for God? They said: We fought until there was no more persecution and the religion was all for God. Narrated by Ibn Mardawayh. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And fight them until there is no more persecution, meaning there is no more polytheism. This is what Abu Al-Aaliyah, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ bin Anas, As-Suddi, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and Zaid bin Aslam said. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: It was conveyed to me on the authority of Az-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, and other scholars of ours, Until there is no more persecution, until no Muslim is tempted away from his religion. And His statement, And the religion is all for God, Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse, he said, Monotheism is to be sincerely devoted to God. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Ibn Jurayj said, And the religion is all for God means that one says, There is no god but God. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Monotheism is to be sincerely devoted to God, with no polytheism in it, and all rivals besides Him are to be renounced. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: And the religion will be entirely for God, there will be no disbelief with your religion. This is supported by what is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ If they say it, their blood and wealth are protected from me, except for a right, and their reckoning is with God, the Almighty and Majestic.” And in both of them on the authority of Abu Musa al-Ash’ari, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about a man who fights bravely, fights out of pride, and fights to show off, which of them is in the way of God, the Almighty and Majestic? He said: Whoever fights so that the word of God is supreme is in the way of God, the Almighty and Majestic. And His saying, If they desist, meaning by fighting you from what they are doing of disbelief, then desist from it, and if you do not know their inner selves, then indeed, God is Seeing of what they do, like His saying, But if they repent and establish prayer and give zakah, then let them go on their way, the verse, and in the other verse, Then they are your brothers in religion, and He said, “And fight them until there is no more fitnah and religion is for God. But if they desist, then there is no aggression except against the wrongdoers.” And in the Sahih: That the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Usama, when that man raised his sword and said, There is no god but God, so he struck him and killed him, and that was mentioned to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said to Usama, Did you kill him after he said, ‘There is no god but God?’ And how will you deal with ‘There is no god but God’ on the Day of Resurrection? He said, O Messenger of God, he only said it as a means of protection. He said, Why did you not split open his heart? And he kept saying and repeating to him, Who will deal with ‘There is no god but God’ on the Day of Resurrection? Usama said, Until I wished that I had not become Muslim until that day. And His statement, But if they turn away, then know that God is your Protector; what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper, meaning, if they continue to oppose you and fight you, then know that God is your Protector, your Lord and your Helper against your enemies; what an excellent Protector and what an excellent Helper. Muhammad ibn Jarir said, Abd al-Warith ibn Abd al-Samad told me, my father told us, Aban al-Attar told us, Hisham ibn Urwah told us, on the authority of Urwah, that Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan wrote to him asking him about some things, so Urwah wrote to him: Peace be upon you, for I praise to you God, there is no god but Him. And after that, you wrote to me asking me about the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, and I will tell you about it, and there is no power or strength except with God. The reason for the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca was that God gave him prophethood, so what a good prophet, what a good master, and what a good clan, so may God reward him with good, and may we know his face in Paradise, and may He make us live on his religion and cause us to die and be resurrected on it, and that when he called his people to what God sent him with of guidance and light that He sent down upon him, they did not turn away from him at first when he called them to it, and they listened to him, until he mentioned their tyrants, and some people from Taif from Quraysh came with wealth, some people denounced that to him and were harsh with him, and they hated what he said and tempted those who obeyed them with it, so the majority of the people turned away from him, and they left him except for those whom God preserved from them, and they were few, so he remained in that for as long as God had decreed that he should remain, then their leaders conspired to tempt those who followed him from the religion of God from their sons, brothers, and tribes, so it was a severe earthquake, so those who were tempted were tempted and God protected those who He wanted them to, so when he did that to the Muslims, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go to the land of Abyssinia. There was a righteous king in Abyssinia, called the Negus, who did not wrong anyone in his land, and he was praised for that. The land of Abyssinia was a trade for the Quraysh, and it was a residence for their merchants, who found comfort in their livelihood, security, and good trade. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to go there, and most of them went there when they were defeated in Mecca, and they feared the tribulations for them, and he stayed and did not leave, so they remained like that for years, being harsh on those who converted to Islam from among them, then Islam spread there, and men from their nobles and their strength entered it, so when they saw that, they relaxed from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and from his companions, and the first tribulation was the one that drove out those of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who went out before the land of Abyssinia, fearing it, and fleeing from the tribulations and earthquakes they were in. So when he relaxed from them and those who entered Islam from them spoke of their relaxation from them, so it reached those who There were some companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Abyssinia who were relieved of those who were in Mecca and who were not tempted, so they returned to Mecca and were almost safe there, and they began to increase and multiply, and many of the Ansar in Medina converted to Islam, and Islam spread in Medina and the people of Medina began to come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Mecca. When the Quraysh saw that, they conspired to tempt them and to intensify, so they seized them and were keen to tempt them, and they were afflicted with great hardship, so there was the last temptation, and there were two temptations: a temptation that drove those of them who went to the land of Abyssinia when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to do so and gave them permission to go out to it, and a temptation: when they returned and saw those who came to them from the people of Medina, then seventy leaders came from Medina, the leaders of those who converted to Islam, and they met him during the Hajj and pledged allegiance to him at Al-Aqabah, and gave him their covenants and agreements, that I am from you and you are from us, and that whoever of your companions comes or you come to us, then we will We prevent you from what we prevent ourselves from, so the Quraysh became severe upon them, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered his companions to go out to Medina, and it was the last tribulation in which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out with his companions, and he went out, and it was the one in which God Almighty revealed: And fight them until there is no more persecution and religion is all for God, then he narrated it on the authority of Yunus bin Abdul A’la on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Zinad on the authority of his father, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, that he wrote to Al-Walid, meaning Ibn Abdul Malik bin Marwan, about this, so he mentioned something similar, and this is authentic up to Urwah, may God have mercy on him.
8:41: The Almighty explains in detail what He has legislated, specifically for this noble nation, from among all the previous nations, by making spoils permissible. Spoils are the money taken from the infidels, by sending horses and riders, and the spoils of war are what is taken from them in other ways, such as the money that they make peace with or die without having any heirs, and the jizya and kharaj and the like. This is the doctrine of Imam al-Shafi'i and a group of scholars of the early and later generations. Some scholars use the term fay' to mean the same thing as spoils of war, and vice versa. For this reason, Qatada believed that this verse abrogates the verse of al-Hashr 59:Whatever God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns, it belongs to God and to the Messenger and to his near relatives. He said that the verse of al-Anfal was abrogated, and the spoils of war were made four-fifths for the mujahidin, and one-fifth of them for those mentioned. What he said is far-fetched, because this verse was revealed after the Battle of Badr, and that one was revealed about Banu al-Nadir. There is no disagreement among all the scholars of biography and military campaigns that Banu al-Nadir were after Badr, and this is a matter that is not doubted or questioned. Whoever differentiates between the meaning of fay' and spoils of war says that one was revealed about spoils of war, and this one about spoils of war. Whoever makes the matter of spoils of war and fay' go back to the opinion of the Imam says: There is no contradiction between the verse of al-Hashr and the fifth, if the Imam sees it, and God knows best. God Almighty says: And know that whatever you gain, a fifth of it belongs to God confirms the fifth of everything, whether small or large, even thread and needle. God Almighty says: “And whoever steals will bring what he stole on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.” And His statement: A fifth of it belongs to God and to the Messenger the commentators differed here. Some of them said: God has a share of the fifth that is placed in the Kaaba. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi` on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi, who said: The spoils of war would be brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would divide them into five parts, four-fifths for those who witnessed them. Then he would take the fifth and strike it with his hand, and take from it what he had grasped and give it to the Ka`bah, which is God’s share. Then he would divide what remained into five parts, one for the Messenger, one for the relatives, one for the orphans, one for the poor, and one for the wayfarer. Others said: God mentioned here as an opening statement for blessing, and a share for His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent out a detachment and they took a fifth of the spoils, he would multiply that fifth by five, then he would recite, And know that whatever you gain of anything, then a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger, so a fifth of it is for God, the key to the statement, To God belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, so he made God’s share and the Messenger’s share, may God bless him and grant him peace, one. Ibrahim al-Nakha`i said the same. Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Sha’bi, Ata bin Abi Rabah, Abdullah bin Buraidah, Qatadah, Mughirah and more than one, said that the share of God and His Messenger is one. This is supported by what was narrated by Imam Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi, with a sound chain of transmission, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of a man, who said: I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was in Wadi Al-Qura, and he was showing off a horse, so I said: O Messenger of God, what do you say about the spoils of war? He said: A fifth of it belongs to God and four-fifths of it belongs to the army. I said: So who is more deserving of it than anyone else? He said: “No, not even the share that you take from your pocket. You are not more deserving of it than your Muslim brother.” Ibn Jarir said: Imran bin Musa told us, Abdul Warith told us, Aban told us on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Al-Hasan recommended a fifth of his wealth, and said: Shall I not be satisfied with my wealth with what God is satisfied with for Himself? Then the speakers of this statement differed, so Ali bin Abi Talhah narrated, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The spoils of war were divided into five fifths, four of which were for those who fought over it, and one fifth was divided into four fifths, one fourth for God and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. So whatever was for God and the Messenger was for the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not take anything from the fifth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Muammar Al-Manqari told us, Abdul Warith bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Hussein Al-Mu’allim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Buraidah, regarding His statement: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger, he said: What is for God is for his Prophet, and what is for the Messenger is for his wives. Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman said, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, who said: The fifth of God and the Messenger is one, he carries from it and does with it what he wants, meaning the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is more general and comprehensive, which is that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, disposes of the fifth that God made as he wants, and returns it to his nation as he wants. This is supported by what Imam Ahmad narrated, where he said: Ishaq bin Isa told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Abi Maryam, on the authority of Abu Salam al-A’raj, on the authority of al-Miqdam bin Ma’dikarib al-Kindi, that he sat with Ubadah bin al-Samit, Abu al-Darda’ and al-Harith bin Mu’awiyah al-Kindi, may God be pleased with them, and they discussed the hadith of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Abu al-Darda’ said to Ubadah: O Ubadah, the words of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in such-and-such a battle regarding the fifths. Ubadah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed with them in a battle to a camel from the spoils, and when he finished, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood up and took a fur between his two fingertips and said: “This is from “Your spoils, and I have nothing in them except my share with you, the fifth, and the fifth is returned to you, so pay the thread and the needle, and what is greater than that and less, and do not commit fraud, for fraud is a disgrace and a fire for its doers in this world and the hereafter, and strive against people in the cause of God, those near and far, and do not care in the cause of God about the blame of the blamer, and establish the limits of God while traveling and at home, and strive in the cause of God, for jihad is a great door from the gates of Paradise, by which God saves from worry and grief.” This is a great and good hadith, and I did not see it in any of the six books from this source. However, Imam Ahmad also narrated, as did Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i, from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu’ayb, from his father, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Amr, from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar in the story of the fifth and the prohibition of fraud. On the authority of Amr ibn Unbasa, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them in prayer beside a camel from the spoils of war. When he had finished, he took a hair from this camel and then said: It is not permissible for me to take anything like this from your spoils of war except one-fifth, and one-fifth is returned to you. Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Nasa’i. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had something from the spoils that he would choose for himself, a male or female slave, a horse, a sword, or something similar, as Muhammad ibn Sirin and Amir al-Sha’bi stated, and most scholars followed them in this. Imam Ahmad and Al-Tirmidhi narrated, and he authenticated it, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given his sword, Dhu al-Fiqar, on the day of Badr, and it is the one he saw in the vision on the day of Uhud. And on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, she said: Safiyya was from the Safiyya. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan, and he also narrated with his chain of transmission and Al-Nasa’i also narrated it on the authority of Yazid bin Abdullah, who said: We were in Al-Marbad when a man entered with a piece of leather, so we read it and it said: “From Muhammad, the Messenger of God, to Banu Zuhair bin Qais, if you bear witness that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and establish prayer, and pay zakat, and pay the fifth of the spoils, and the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the share of the Safiyya, you are safe with the safety of God and His Messenger.” So we said: Who wrote this? The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) said: These are good hadiths that indicate the confirmation and confirmation of this, and for this reason many have made it one of his special characteristics, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. Others said: The imam should use the fifth in the interest of the Muslims, just as he uses the spoils of war. Our Sheikh, the great scholar Ibn Taymiyyah may God have mercy on him said: This is the opinion of Malik and most of the predecessors, and it is the most correct opinion. If this is proven and known, then there is also disagreement about what the Prophet (peace be upon him) received from the fifth, and what should be done with it after him. Some said: It should be for whoever takes over the matter after him. This was narrated from Abu Bakr, Ali, Qatadah and a group. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace be upon him) was narrated about it. Others said: It should be spent in the interests of the Muslims. Others said: Rather, it should be returned to the rest of the categories, relatives, orphans, the poor and wayfarers. Ibn Jarir chose this. Others said: Rather, the share of the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the share of relatives are returned to the orphans, the poor and wayfarers. Ibn Jarir said: This is the opinion of a group of the people of Iraq, and it was said that all of the fifth is for the relatives, as Ibn Jarir narrated: Al-Harith told us, Abdul Aziz told us, Abdul Ghaffar told us, Al-Munhal bin Amr told us, I asked Abdullah bin Muhammad bin Ali and Ali bin Al-Hussein about the fifth, and they said: It is for us, so I said to Ali: God says: And orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer, and they said: Our orphans and our needy. Sufyan Al-Thawri, Abu Nu’aym, and Abu Usamah said, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, I asked Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, may God have mercy on him, about the words of God Almighty: And know that whatever you obtain of anything, a fifth of it is for God and for the Messenger, and he said: This is the key to the speech, for God belongs this world and the Hereafter. Then the people differed about these two shares, after the death of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so some said: The share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, is in submission to the caliph after him, and others said: For the relatives of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others said: The share of the relatives is for the relatives of the caliph, and their opinion agreed that They used to put these two shares in horses and equipment in the way of God, and they were like that during the caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar, may God be pleased with them. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ibrahim: Abu Bakr and Umar used to put the share of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the forelegs and weapons, so I said to Ibrahim: What did Ali say about it? He said: He was the most severe of them in it, and this is the opinion of a large group of scholars, may God have mercy on them. As for the share of the relatives, it is given to Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, because Banu al-Muttalib supported Banu Hashim in the pre-Islamic era and in the beginning of Islam, and entered with them into the valley out of anger for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to protect him. Their Muslims were obedient to God and His Messenger, and their unbelievers were out of zeal for the clan and pride and obedience to Abu Talib, the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. As for Banu Abd Shams and Banu Nawfal, even though they were their cousins, they did not agree with them on that, rather they fought them and opposed them and filled the bellies of Quraysh to fight the Messenger. For this reason, Abu Talib’s condemnation of them in his poem, Lamiyah, was more severe than others, due to their great closeness. For this reason, he says during his poem: May God punish Abd Shams and Nawfal with an evil punishment, soon and not later. With a just balance that does not deprive a single grain of it, and a witness from himself, not a supporter. You have made foolish the dreams of a people who have replaced the Banu Khalaf with us and the idle ones We are the core of the Hashimites and the Qusay family in the early battles. Jubayr ibn Mut’im ibn ‘Adi ibn Nawfal said: I and ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, meaning the son of Abi al-‘As ibn Umayyah ibn ‘Abd Shams, walked to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we said: O Messenger of God, you gave the Banu al-Muttalib from the fifth of Khaybar and left us, and we and they are of the same status with you. He said: The Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib are one thing. Narrated by Muslim. In some versions of this hadith, it says: They did not leave us in ignorance or Islam. This is the opinion of the majority of scholars, that they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib. Ibn Jarir said, and others said: They are Banu Hashim. Then it was narrated on the authority of Khasif on the authority of Mujahid, who said: God knew that there were poor people among Banu Hashim, so He made for them the fifth instead of charity. In a narration on his authority, he said: They are the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for whom charity is not permissible. Then it was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn something similar to that. Ibn Jarir said, and others said: Rather, they are all Quraysh. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, Abdullah ibn Nafi’ told me, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Sa’id al-Maqburi, who said: Najdah wrote to Abdullah ibn Abbas asking him about the relatives, so Ibn Abbas wrote to him, we used to say: We are them, but our people refused that to us, and they said: All Quraysh are relatives. This hadith is authentic. It was narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sa’id al-Maqburi, on the authority of Yazid ibn Hurmuz, that Najdah wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about the relatives, so he mentioned it up to his saying: But our people refused that to us, and the addition is from the individuals of Abu Ma’shar Najih ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Madani, and there is weakness in it. Ibn Abi Hatim: My father told us, Ibrahim bin Mahdi Al-Masisi told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hanash, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I would prefer you not to wash your hands, because you have from the fifth of the fifth what will suffice you or suffice you. This is a hadith with a good chain of transmission, and this Ibrahim bin Mahdi was authenticated by Abu Hatim, and Yahya bin Ma'in said: He brings strange things, and God knows best. And his saying and the orphans means the orphans of the Muslims, and the scholars differed as to whether it is specific to the poor orphans, or includes the rich and the poor? There are two opinions, and the needy are those in need who do not find what will fill their need and poverty, and the wayfarer is the traveler or the one who wants to travel to a distance where the prayer is shortened, and he does not have what to spend on that journey, and the explanation of that will come in the verse on charity in Surat Bara'ah, God willing, and in Him is the trust and upon Him is reliance. And his saying, If you believe in God and what We have sent down to Our servant, meaning, comply with what We have prescribed for you of the fifth of the spoils, if you believe in God and the Last Day, and what has been sent down to His Messenger. For this reason, it came in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abdullah bin Abbas in the hadith of the delegation of Abd al-Qays, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: “And I command you to do four things, and I forbid you from four things. I command you to believe in God - then he said - Do you know what belief in God means? Testifying that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, establishing prayer, paying zakat, and paying the fifth of the spoils,” the hadith in its entirety, so he made paying the fifth part of faith. Al-Bukhari included a chapter on this in the Book of Faith in his Sahih, and he said: Chapter on paying the fifth part of faith, then he included this hadith of Ibn Abbas, and we have discussed it in detail in the explanation of Al-Bukhari, praise and thanks be to God. Muqatil bin Hayyan said: And what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, meaning in the division, and his saying, The Day of Criterion is the day when the two armies met, and God is over all things. “Something powerful,” the Almighty points out His grace and kindness to His creation, by which He distinguished between truth and falsehood at Badr, and it is called the Criterion, because God elevated the word of faith over the word of falsehood on that day, and made His religion manifest and supported His Prophet and His party. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The Day of Criterion is the Day of Badr, on which God distinguished between truth and falsehood. Narrated by Al-Hakim. Mujahid, Muqsim, Ubayd God bin Abdullah, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Muqatil bin Hayyan, and more than one said the same that it was the Day of Badr. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr regarding His statement the Day of Criterion is the day God distinguished between truth and falsehood, and it is the Day of Badr, and it is the first battle witnessed by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the leader of the polytheists was Utbah bin Rabi’ah, so they met on Friday, the nineteenth or seventeenth of Ramadan, and the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on that day were three hundred and a few men, and the polytheists were between one thousand and nine hundred, so God defeated the polytheists, and killed more than seventy of them, and took a similar number of them captive. Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Al-A’mash from Ibrahim from Al-Aswad from Ibn Mas’ud, who said about the Night of Decree: Seek it on the eleventh remaining, for on its morning is the Day of Badr. And he said according to their conditions. And something similar was narrated from Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr also, from the hadith of Ja’far bin Burqan, from a man from him. And Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Yahya bin Wadh told us, Yahya bin Ya’qub Abu Talib told us, from Ibn Awn from Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi, from Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami, who said: Al-Hasan bin Ali said: The Night of Al-Furqan was the day the two armies met, on the seventeenth of Ramadan. A good, strong chain of transmission. And Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from Abu Abdul Rahman Abdullah bin Habib from Ali, who said: The Night of Al-Furqan was the night the two armies met, on its morning, the night of Friday, on the seventeenth of Ramadan. And this is correct according to the people of the battles and biographies. And Yazid bin Abi Habib, the imam of the people of Egypt in his time, said: The Day of Badr was Monday, and he was not followed in this, and the opinion of the majority is preferred over it, and God knows best.
8:42: God Almighty says, informing us about the Day of Criterion: When you were on the lower slope, meaning when you were descending on the lower slope of the valley, close to Medina, and they, meaning the polytheists, were descending on the farthest slope, meaning far from Medina towards Mecca, and the caravan, meaning the caravan in which Abu Sufyan was with what he had of merchandise, was below you, meaning what was next to the seashore, and if you had made an appointment, meaning you and the polytheists at a place, you would have differed in the appointment, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn ‘Ibad ibn ‘Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr told me, on the authority of his father, regarding this verse, he said: If that had been by appointment from you and them, then you were informed of their great number and your small number, you would not have met them, but that God might accomplish a matter that was to be accomplished, meaning that God might accomplish what He wanted by His power of honoring Islam and its people, and humiliating polytheism and its people, without any of you, so He did what He wanted of that with His kindness. In the hadith of Ka’b ibn Malik said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Muslims went out, intending to take the caravan of Quraysh, until God brought them together with their enemy without an appointment. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told me, on the authority of Ibn Awn, on the authority of Umair ibn Ishaq, who said: Abu Sufyan came with the caravan from Ash-Sham, and Abu Jahl went out to prevent him from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. They met at Badr, and these did not know those, nor those knew those, until the water-carriers met, and the people warned each other. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said in the biography: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued on that path, until when he was close to As-Safra, he sent Basbas ibn Amr and Adi ibn Abi Al-Zaghba Al-Juhani, seeking report about Abu Sufyan. They set out until they reached Badr, and they dismounted their camels at a hill in Al-Batha’, and drew water from a water-skin of theirs. They heard two girls arguing, one of them saying to her companion, Give me my right, and the other saying, The caravan will come tomorrow or the day after. So I will give you your right. So Majdi bin Amr settled the matter between them and said, You have spoken the truth. So, Sabas and Adi heard about that, so they sat on their camels until they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and told him the report. Abu Sufyan approached when they turned away, and he was cautious. He advanced in front of his caravan and said to Majdi bin Amr, Did you sense anyone at this water whom you do not recognize? He said: No, by God, except that I saw two riders who stopped at this hill and drew water from their water skins and then set off. Abu Sufyan came to the place where their camels stopped, took some of their dung and crushed it, and in it were date pits. He said: By God, these are the fodder of Yathrib. Then he quickly returned and struck the face of his camel and set off with it along the coast, until when he saw that he had secured his camel to Quraysh, he said: God has saved your caravan, your wealth and your men, so go back. Abu Jahl said: By God, we will not go back until we come to Badr - and Badr was one of the markets of the Arabs - and we will stay there for three days, and we will eat food there, and slaughter camels there, and drink wine there, and the female singers will play for us, and the Arabs will hear about us and our march, and they will continue to fear us forever after that. Then Al-Akhns bin Shuraiq said: O people of Banu Zuhra, God has saved your wealth and saved your master, so go back. So Banu Zuhra went back, but they did not witness it, nor did Banu Adi. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Yazid bin Ruman told me, on the authority of Urwah bin Al-Zubayr, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, approached Badr, he sent Ali bin Abi Talib, Sa`d bin Abi Waqqas, and Al-Zubayr bin Al-`Awwam with a group of his companions to spy on him for report. They found two Quraysh water carriers, a slave of Banu Sa`id bin Al-`As and a slave of Banu Al-Hajjaj. They brought them to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found him praying. The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, began to ask them: Who do you belong to? They said: We are water carriers for the Quraysh. They sent us to give them water. The people hated their report and hoped that they belonged to Abu Sufyan, so they beat them. When they slipped, they said: We belong to Abu Sufyan. So they left them. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, knelt and prostrated twice, then he said: If they tell the truth, you will beat them, and if they lie, you will leave them. They have told the truth, by God, they belong to the Quraysh. Tell me about the Quraysh. They said: They are behind this sand dune that you see on the far side. The sand dune is Al-Aqanqal. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: How many are the people? They said: Many. He said: What is their number? They said: We do not know. He said: How many do they slaughter every day? They said: Nine one day and ten the next. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people are between nine hundred and a thousand. Then he said to them: Who are the nobles of the Quraysh among them? They said: Utbah ibn Rabi’ah, Shaiba ibn Rabi’ah, Abu al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham, Hakim ibn Hizam, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, al-Harith ibn Amir ibn Nawfal, Tu’aymah ibn ‘Adi ibn Nawfal, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Zam’ah ibn al-Aswad, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, Nabih, Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj, Suhayl ibn ‘Amr, and ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd Wudd. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned to the people and said: This is Mecca, which has thrown to you the most precious parts of its liver. Muhammad ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, said: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr ibn Hazm told me that Sa’d ibn Mu’adh said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: When the people met on the day of Badr, O Messenger of God, should we not build you a hut for you to be in, and we can kneel down to you on your mounts, and we can meet our enemy? If God gives us victory over them and makes us victorious, then that is what we love. But if it is otherwise, then you can sit on your mounts and catch up with those of our people who are behind us, for by God, people have lagged behind you that we do not know.” They love you more than they do. If they knew that you would encounter war, they would not have stayed behind you, and they would support and aid you. So the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) praised him and prayed for him, so a hut was built for him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and Abu Bakr were in it, and no one else was with them. Ibn Ishaq said: Quraysh set out in the morning, and when they returned and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw them descending from Al-Aqanqal, which is the sand dune from which they had come to the valley, he said: “O God, this is Quraysh, they have come with their arrogant and proud, challenging You and denying Your Messenger. O God, defeat them this morning.” And His statement: So that he who is to perish will perish on clear evidence, and he who is to live will live on clear evidence, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: That is, so that he who disbelieves after the proof will disbelieve because of what he saw of the sign and lesson, and he who believes will believe on the basis of the same. This is a good interpretation. And the explanation of that is that the Almighty says: He only gathered you with your enemy in one place, without an appointment, to grant you victory over them and raise the word of truth over falsehood, so that the matter becomes apparent and the argument is conclusive and the evidence is clear, and no argument or doubt remains for anyone. Then whoever perishes will perish, meaning whoever continues in disbelief will continue in it, with insight into his matter, that he has invalidated the proof against him, and whoever lives will live meaning whoever believes will believe with clear evidence meaning argument and insight, and faith is the life of the hearts. God the Almighty said: Or he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people? Aisha said in the story of the slander, he perished among those who perished, meaning he said what he said of slander and falsehood. And His saying: And indeed, God is Hearing meaning of your supplications and your pleas to Him and your calling for help, Knowing meaning of you, and that you deserve victory over your stubborn disbelieving enemies.
8:43: Mujahid said: God showed them to him in his dream a little, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed his companions of that, so it was a confirmation for them. Ibn Ishaq and others said the same, and Ibn Jarir narrated from some of them that he saw them with the eye with which he sleeps. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: My father told us, Yusuf bin Musa told us, Abu Qutaybah told us, on the authority of Sahl al-Sarraj, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding his statement: When God showed them to you in your dream a little, he said with your eye. This statement is strange, and the dream was stated here, so there is no need for interpretation for which there is no evidence. His statement: And if He had shown them to you many, you would have lost heart, meaning you would have been cowardly towards them and differed among yourselves. But God saved you, meaning from that, by showing them a little. He is Knowing of that within the breasts, meaning what the consciences conceal and the entrails conceal. He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal, and his statement: And when He showed them to you when you met in the Your eyes are few. This is also from His kindness to them, as He made them appear few in the sight of the eye, so He made them bold towards them and made them covet them. Abu Ishaq al-Subai’i said: On the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, he said: They appeared few in our eyes on the day of Badr, until I said to a man next to me: Do you think they are seventy? He said: No, they were a hundred, until we took a man from them and asked him, and he said: We were a thousand. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. His statement: And He will make you seem small in their eyes Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Hammad ibn Zayd told us, on the authority of Az-Zubayr ibn Al-Harith, on the authority of Ikrimah, And when He showed them to you when you met the verse, he said: He incited some of them against others, a sound chain of transmission. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Yahya ibn Ibad ibn Abdullah ibn Az-Zubayr told me, on the authority of his father, regarding the statement of God Almighty: That God may accomplish a matter that was to be done meaning that He may cast war between them to exact vengeance on whoever He wanted to exact vengeance on, and to bestow favors on whoever He wanted to complete the favor upon from among the people of His authority. The meaning of this is that God Almighty tempted each of the two parties against the other, and made them seem small in their eyes so that they would covet it, and that was at the time of confrontation. So when the fighting began and God supported the believers with a thousand angels in succession, the party of the unbelievers remained seeing the party of faith as twice as great, as He said. God Almighty said: “There has certainly been for you a sign in the two companies that met - one company fighting in the cause of God and the other disbelieving. They saw them twice as many as they were, with the sight of the eyes. And God supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.” This is the combination of these two verses, for each of them is true and correct, and to God be praise and thanks.

8:45: This is a teaching from God Almighty to His believing servants about the etiquette of meeting and the path of courage when confronting enemies. He said, O you who believe, when you meet a company, stand firm. It is proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Awfa that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, waited during some of the days in which he met the enemy, until the sun declined and he stood among them and said, “O people, do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask God for well-being. When you meet them, be patient and know that Paradise is under the shadows of swords.” Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, stood and said, O God, Revealer of the Book, Driver of the clouds, and Defeater of the parties, defeat them and grant us victory over them. And Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask God for well-being. When you meet them, stand firm and remember God. If they make noise and shout, then you should be silent.” He said, Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani: Ibrahim bin Hashim al-Baghawi told us, Umayyah bin Bastam told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, Thabit bin Zayd told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Zayd bin Arqam, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God loves silence in three situations: when reciting the Qur’an, when marching, and at a funeral.” In another chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, God Almighty says: My servant is the one who remembers Me while he is fighting his enemy, meaning that this state does not distract him from remembering Me, supplicating to Me, and seeking My help. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said: On the authority of Qatada regarding this verse, he said: God has made it obligatory to remember Him when one is most busy, when striking with swords. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abda bin Sulaiman told us, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: It is obligatory to listen and remember God when advancing, then he recited this verse. I said: Should they recite the remembrance aloud? He said: Yes. He also said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la read it to me, Ibn Wahb told us, Abdullah bin Ayyash told me, on the authority of Yazid bin Fudhar, on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar, he said: There is nothing more beloved to God Almighty than reciting the Qur’an and remembering God, and were it not for that, He would not have commanded people to pray and fight. Do you not see that He commanded people to remember God when fighting, saying: O you who have believed, when you meet an army, stand firm and remember God much that you may be successful. The poet said: I remembered you while the steps were moving between us, and the educated dark-skinned woman had drunk from us Antara said: I remembered you while the spears were drinking from me and the swords of India were dripping with my blood. God the Almighty commanded steadfastness when fighting the enemies and patience in their confrontation, so that they do not flee, retreat, or become cowardly, and that they remember God in that situation and do not forget Him, but rather seek His help and trust in Him and ask Him for victory over their enemies, and that they obey God and His Messenger in that situation, so that whatever God the Almighty commanded them to do they obey, and whatever He forbade them they refrain from, and that they do not dispute among themselves and differ and that this would be a cause of their failure and inaction, and your strength will depart meaning your strength and unity, and what you were in of acceptance, and be patient, for God is with the patient. The Companions, may God be pleased with them, had in the matter of courage and obeying what God and His Messenger commanded them to do, and complying with what He guided them to, what no other nation or generation before them had, and will not be for anyone after them, for by the blessing of the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his obedience to what he commanded them, they conquered hearts and regions east and west in a short period, despite their small number in comparison to the armies of the rest of the world. The regions, of the Romans, Persians, Turks, Sicilians, Berbers, Abyssinians, and the various kinds of Sudanese, Copts, and sects of the sons of Adam. They conquered everyone until the word of God was elevated, and His religion prevailed over all other religions, and the Islamic kingdoms extended to the east and west of the earth, in less than thirty years. May God be pleased with them and satisfy them all, and gather us with them, for He is Generous and Giver.

8:47: God Almighty says after commanding the believers to be sincere in fighting in His cause, and to mention Him frequently, forbidding them from imitating the polytheists in leaving their homes, out of arrogance, i.e., to push away the truth, and to show off to people, which is boasting and haughtiness towards them, as Abu Jahl said: When it was said to him: The caravan has escaped, so return, he said: No, by God, we will not return until we return to the water of Badr, and slaughter the camels, and drink wine, and the female singers play for us, and the Arabs will talk about our place there forever. This was reflected upon him all together, because when they returned to the water of Badr, they returned to the baths with it, and they piled up in the valleys of Badr, humiliated and degraded, small and wretched in everlasting torment. For this reason, He said: And God encompasses what they do, i.e., He knows what they brought to Him, and for this reason He rewarded them for it with the worst reward for them. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ad-Dahhak, and As-Suddi said regarding the Almighty’s statement: And do not be like those who left their homes insolently and to be seen by people, they said: They are the polytheists who fought the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr. Muhammad bin Kaab said: When the Quraysh left Mecca for Badr, they went out with singing girls and drums, so God revealed: “And be not like those who went forth from their homes insolently and to be seen by people and to hinder [people] from the way of God. And God encompasses what they do.” And the Almighty’s saying: “And when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, ‘No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your protector. ’” The verse, may God curse him, made what they had come for and what they intended to do seem good to them, and made them hope that no one can overcome them today from among the people, and removed from them the fear of being attacked in their homes by their enemy, Banu Bakr, so he said: I am your protector. That is because he appeared to them in the form of Suraqa bin Malik bin Ju’sham, the chief of Banu Mudlij, the great leader of that region, and all of that was from him as God Almighty said about him: He promises them and arouses false hopes in them, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said about this verse: When the day of Badr came, Satan marched with his banner and soldiers with the polytheists, and he cast into the hearts of the polytheists that no one would He will defeat you, and I am your protector. So when they met and Satan saw the reinforcements of the angels, he turned back on his heels, he said: He turned back, and said: I see what you do not see, the verse. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Satan came on the day of Badr with an army of devils with his banner, in the form of a man from Banu Mudlij, in the form of Suraqah bin Malik bin Ja’sham. Satan said to the polytheists: No one from among the people will defeat you today, and I am your protector. So when the people lined up, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a handful of dirt and threw it in the faces of the polytheists, and they turned back. Gabriel, peace be upon him, approached Satan, and when he saw him, and his hand was in the hand of a man from among the polytheists, he pulled his hand away and turned back, and his followers, so the man said: O Suraqah, do you claim that you are our protector? I said: He means his habit for those who obey him, the Almighty’s saying: “Like Satan when he said to man, ‘Disbelieve.’ But when he disbelieved, he said, ‘Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I fear God, Lord of the worlds.’” And the Almighty’s saying: “And Satan said, when the matter has been decided, ‘Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me but blame yourselves. I cannot be your savior, nor can you be my savior. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated before. Indeed, for the wrongdoers is a painful punishment.’” And Yunus bin Bakir said on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq, Abdullah bin Abi Bakr bin Amr bin Hazm told me, on the authority of some of Banu Sa’idah, he said: I heard Abu Asid Malik bin Rabi’ah after he lost his sight, saying: If I were with you now at Badr and I had my sight, I would have told you about the valley from which I came out. The angels, I do not doubt nor dispute, so when the angels descended and Iblis saw them, and God revealed to them, I am with you, so strengthen those who believe, and their strengthening, that the angels used to come to the man in the form of a man, he knew him and said to him, be of good cheer, for they are nothing and God is with you, think about them, so when Iblis saw the angels, he turned on his heels and said, I am innocent of you, for I see what you do not see, and he was in the form of Suraqa, and Abu Jahl came forward urging his companions, and saying, do not be alarmed by Suraqa’s abandonment of you, for he had an appointment with Muhammad and his companions. Then he said: By Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, we will not return until we tie Muhammad and his companions together in ropes, so do not kill them and seize them. This is from Abu Jahl, may God curse him, like what Pharaoh said to the magicians when they converted to Islam: This is indeed a plot you have plotted in the city to expel its people from it, and like his saying: He is your chief who taught you magic, which is from the category of slander and calumny, and for this reason Abu Jahl was the Pharaoh of this nation. Malik bin Anas said: On the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Ulayyah, on the authority of Talha bin Ubayd God bin Kurayz, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Satan has never seen a day in which he was smaller, more contemptible, more defeated, or more angry than on the Day of Arafah. This is because of what he sees of the descent of mercy and forgiveness of sins, except what he saw on the Day of Badr.” They said: O Messenger of God, and what did he see on the Day of Badr? He said: “He saw Gabriel, peace be upon him, directing the angels.” This is a mursal from this source. And His statement: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, ‘These people have been deceived by their religion,’ Ali bin Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: When the people came close to one another, God made the Muslims appear small in the eyes of the polytheists, and made the polytheists appear small in the eyes of the Muslims. The polytheists said, These people have been deceived by their religion, and they only said that because they were few in number in their eyes, so they thought that they would defeat them, and they had no doubt about that. So God said, And whoever relies upon God - then indeed, God is Exalted in Might and Wise. Qatada said: They saw a group of believers who were steadfast in the cause of God. It was mentioned to us that when Abu Jahl, the enemy of God, looked down upon Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, he said, By God, God will not be worshipped from today on with cruelty and arrogance. Ibn Jurayj said about His statement, When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said, they are a group of hypocrites in Mecca, they said it on the day of Badr. Aamer Al-Sha’bi said: There were some people from Mecca who spoke about Islam, so they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr. When they saw the small number of Muslims, they said: These people have been deceived by their religion. Mujahid said about His statement, the Almighty: “When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease said: These people have been deceived by their religion,” a group of Quraysh said: Qays ibn Al-Walid ibn Al-Mughira, Abu Qays ibn Al-Fakih ibn Al-Mughira, Al-Harith ibn Zama’ah ibn Al-Aswad ibn Al-Muttalib, Ali ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and Al-As ibn Munabbih ibn Al-Hajjaj, they went out with Quraysh from Mecca, and they were in doubt, but their doubt held them back. When they saw the small number of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they said: These people have been deceived by their religion until they came to what they came to despite their small number and the large number of their enemy. Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said the same thing. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding this verse, he said: They are a people who did not witness the fighting on the day of Badr, so they were called hypocrites. Muammar said: Some of them said: They are a people who had acknowledged Islam while they were in Mecca, so they went out with the polytheists on the day of Badr, and when they saw the small number of Muslims, they said that their religion had deceived them. His statement, And whoever relies upon God means, relies on His side, then indeed, God is Exalted in Might means, He will not wrong whoever seeks refuge in Him, for God is Exalted in Might, Invincible in His side, Great in His power, Wise in His actions, He does not place them except in their proper places, so He supports whoever deserves support, and disappoints whoever is worthy of it.
8:50: God the Almighty says: And if you were to witness, O Muhammad, the state in which the angels take the souls of the infidels, you would see a great, terrifying, horrible, and reprehensible matter, when they strike their faces and their backs and say to them, And taste the punishment of the Burning Fire. Ibn Jurayj said: On the authority of Mujahid, Their backs means their buttocks, he said on the day of Badr. Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn Abbas said: When the polytheists face the Muslims, they strike their faces with swords, and when they turn away, the angels catch up with them and strike their backs. Ibn Abi Nujayh said: On the authority of Mujahid, in his statement, When the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved, they strike their faces and their backs, on the day of Badr. Waki’ said: On the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri, on the authority of Abu Hashim Ismail ibn Kathir, on the authority of Mujahid, and on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ya’la ibn Muslim, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, they strike their faces and their backs, he said and their buttocks, but God is called by a nickname, and so said ‘Umar, the freed slave of ‘Ufra. On the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, he said: A man said, O Messenger of God, I saw something like thorns on the back of Abu Jahl. He said, That is the striking of the angels. Narrated by Ibn Jarir, and it is mursal. Although this context was caused by the Battle of Badr, it is general for every disbeliever. That is why God did not specify it to the people of Badr. Rather, God the Almighty said: And if you could but see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieve, they strike their faces and their backs. And in Surat Al-Qital there is a similar statement. And in Surat Al-An’am, God the Almighty said: “And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming pangs of death while the angels are stretching out their hands, saying, ‘Deliver your souls. ’” That is, they are stretching out their hands to strike them by the command of their Lord, when their souls find it difficult and refuse to leave their bodies to leave by force. This is when they are given glad tidings of torment and wrath from God, as in the hadith of Al-Baraa’ that when the Angel of Death comes to the disbeliever at his deathbed in that horrible state, he says: Come out, O wicked soul, to poisonous water and scalding water and a shade of hot water. So it disperses in his body and they extract it from his body, as it extracts… The skewer is made of wet wool, and the veins and nerves come out with it. That is why God Almighty said: The angels say to them, Taste the torment of the fire. And God Almighty said: That is for what your hands have put forth, meaning this is the reward because of the bad deeds you did in your worldly life. God will reward you with this reward. And that God is not unjust to His servants, meaning He does not wrong any of His creation. Rather, He is the just judge who does not wrong, blessed and exalted be He. And sanctified and glorified is the Rich, the Praiseworthy. That is why it came in the authentic hadith, in Muslim, may God have mercy on him, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that God Almighty says, “O My servants, I have forbidden injustice for Myself and have made it forbidden among you, so do not wrong one another. O My servants, it is only your deeds that I count for you. So whoever finds good, let him praise God, and whoever finds otherwise, let him blame no one but himself.” That is why God Almighty said:

8:52: God Almighty says: These polytheists who denied what you were sent with, O Muhammad, did as the nations who denied before them did, so We did to them what is our custom, that is, our habit and our way with their likes from the people of Pharaoh and the nations before them who denied the messengers, the disbelievers in the signs of God. So God seized them for their sins, that is, because of their sins, He destroyed them and seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Powerful. Indeed, God is Powerful and Severe in penalty, that is, no one can overcome Him and no one can escape Him.
8:53: God Almighty tells us about the perfection of His justice and equity in His judgment, that He Almighty does not change a blessing that He has bestowed upon anyone, except because of a sin that he has committed, as God Almighty says: “Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him.” And His statement, Like the way of Pharaoh’s people, meaning like what He did to Pharaoh’s people and their likes, when they denied His signs, He destroyed them because of their sins and took away from them those blessings that He bestowed upon them, of gardens, springs, crops, treasures, and a noble position, and the blessings in which they were enjoying themselves, and God did not wrong them in that, but they were the wrongdoers.
8:54: God Almighty tells us about the perfection of His justice and equity in His judgment, that He Almighty does not change a blessing that He has bestowed upon anyone, except because of a sin that he has committed, as God Almighty says: “Indeed, God will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves. And when God intends evil for a people, there is no repelling it, and they have no protector besides Him.” And His statement, Like the way of Pharaoh’s people, meaning like what He did to Pharaoh’s people and their likes, when they denied His signs, He destroyed them because of their sins and took away from them those blessings that He bestowed upon them, of gardens, springs, crops, treasures, and a noble position, and the blessings in which they were enjoying themselves, and God did not wrong them in that, but they were the wrongdoers.
8:55: God Almighty said: The worst of those who have crawled on the face of the earth are those who disbelieved, for they do not believe, who whenever they make a covenant they break it, and whenever they confirm it with oaths they break it, and they do not fear God meaning they do not fear God in any of the sins they have committed, so if you overtake them in war meaning you defeat them and triumph over them in war, then scatter through them those behind them meaning torment them, as Ibn Abbas, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Al-Dahhak, Al-Suddi, Ata Al-Khurasani, and Ibn Uyaynah said, and its meaning is to make their punishment severe and kill them severely, so that other enemies from Arabs and others will fear, and they will become an example for them, so that they may remember. Al-Suddi said: He says: Perhaps they will beware of breaking their covenant and the same will be done to them.
