8:58: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you fear treachery from a people with whom you have made a covenant then throw back to them that is, their covenant on an equal footing, that is, inform them that you have broken their covenant, so that your knowledge and their knowledge remain that you are at war with them and they are at war with you, and that there is no covenant between you and them on an equal footing, that is, you and they are equal in that. The rajaz poet said: Strike the faces of the enemies with treachery until they respond to you with equality On the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim, he said about the words of God the Almighty: Then throw back to them on equal terms meaning slowly, Indeed, God does not love the treacherous meaning even if it is against the infidels, He does not love it either. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Ja’far told us, Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Fayd, on the authority of Salim bin Amir, who said: Mu’awiyah was traveling in the land of the Romans, and there was a period of time between him and them, so he wanted to get close to them, and when the period expired, he would attack them, and there was an old man on a mount saying: God is Great, God is Great, loyalty, not treachery, for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And whoever has a covenant between him and a people, he should not loosen the knot or tighten it until its period expires, or throw back to them on equal terms. He said: This reached Mu’awiyah, so he returned, and there was the old man, Amr bin Unbasa, may God be pleased with him. This hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi on the authority of Shu’bah, and it was narrated by Abu Dawud, Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa’i and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, through various chains of transmission on the authority of Shu’bah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Zubayri told us, Israel told us, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Abu Al-Bukhtari, on the authority of Salman, meaning Al-Farsi, may God be pleased with him, that he came to a fortress or a city, and said to his companions: Let me call them as I saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, call them. He said: I was only a man from among you, and God Almighty guided me to Islam. If you submit, then you will have what we have and you will be subject to what we are subject to. If you refuse, then pay the jizyah and be humbled. If you refuse, we will fight you equally. God does not love traitors. He did that to them for three days, and on the fourth day, the people went to it and conquered it with the help of God.
8:59: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not think O Muhammad that those who disbelieve have outstripped Us meaning that We have no power over them, but rather they are under the control of Our power and in the grip of Our will, so they cannot defeat Us, as God Almighty says: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is that which they judge. meaning that they think. God Almighty says: "Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape Us on earth. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination." God Almighty says: "Let not the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you. A brief enjoyment. Then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place." Then God Almighty commanded the preparation of war machines to fight them according to one's ability, possibility, and capacity, saying: And prepare against them whatever you are able meaning whatever you are able of power and steeds of war. Imam Ahmad said: Harun bin Maruf told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Abu Ali Thamamah bin Shafi, the brother of Uqbah bin Amir, that Uqbah ibn Amir heard him say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say while he was on the pulpit: Prepare for them whatever you are able of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Narrated by Muslim, on the authority of Harun ibn Maruf, and Abu Dawud, on the authority of Saeed ibn Mansur, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la, all three of them on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb. This hadith has other chains of transmission, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, including what was narrated by al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of a man on his authority. Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shoot and ride, and to shoot is better than to ride. Imam Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Horses are for three things: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden. As for the one who is rewarded, he is a man who ties them up in the way of God and lets them ride long distances in a meadow or garden, and whatever they hit in that meadow or garden is considered good deeds for him. If they cut their tracks and reach a hill or two, their tracks and dung are considered good deeds for him. If they pass by a river and drink from it, and he does not intend to water himself with it, that is considered good deeds for him, so they are a reward for that man. A man ties them up out of self-sufficiency and chastity, and does not forget God’s right over their necks or backs, so they are a cover for him. A man ties them up out of pride, showing off, and pride, so they are a burden for that man.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about donkeys, and he said, “God has not revealed anything to me about them except this comprehensive and unique verse: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. ’” * And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and this is its wording, and Muslim, both of them from the hadith of Malik. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Rakeen bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Hassan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Horses are of three types: a horse for the Most Merciful, a horse for Satan, and a horse for man. As for the horse of the Most Merciful, it is the one that is tied up in the way of God, so its fodder, dung, and urine are used - and he mentioned what God willed - as for the horse of Satan, it is the one that gambles or bets on it. As for the horse of man, it is the horse that a person ties up, seeking its belly, so it is a protection for him from poverty.” Most scholars have said that archery is better than riding a horse, and Imam Malik said that riding is better than archery, and the opinion of the majority is stronger due to the hadith, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Hisham told us: Laith told us: Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Ibn Shamasah, that Muawiyah bin Khadij passed by Abu Dharr while he was standing next to his horse, and asked him: What is wrong with this horse of yours? He said: I think that the prayer of this horse has been answered. He said: What is the prayer of an animal? He said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, there is no horse but that it prays every dawn, saying: O God, You have made me one of Your servants, and You have placed my provision in his hand, so make me more beloved to him than his family, his wealth, and his children. He said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Abi Jaafar, Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Suwaid bin Qais, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Khadij, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Arabian horse but that it is called to prayer at every dawn, and it calls out with two supplications: It says: O God, You have given me authority over whom You have given authority over from among the children of Adam, so make me among the most beloved of his family and wealth to him - or - the most beloved of his family and wealth to him.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas, on the authority of Yahya Al-Qattan, on his authority. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tastari told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, al-Mut’am ibn al-Muqaddam al-San’ani told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, that he said to Ibn al-Hanthaliyyah, meaning Sahl: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection, and their owners are helped by them. Whoever ties a horse in the way of God, the expenses for it will be like someone who extends his hand in charity and does not withdraw it.” There are many hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of tying horses. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Urwah ibn Abi al-Ja`d al-Barqi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Horses have good tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, reward and spoils. And his statement: You terrify with it means you frighten the enemy of God and your enemy meaning the infidels and others besides them. Mujahid said: He means Banu Qurayzah. Al-Suddi said: Knights. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ibn Yaman said: They are the devils in the houses. A similar hadith has been narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi told us, Abu Haywah, meaning Shureih ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, Saeed ibn Sinan told us, on the authority of Ibn Gharib, meaning Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Gharib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say regarding the statement of God Almighty: And others besides them whom you do not know, he said: They are the jinn. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Duhaim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Shuaib, on the authority of Sinan ibn Saeed ibn Sinan, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Gharib, with the same chain of transmission, and he added: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A house in which there is an old horse will not be ruined. This hadith is rejected, and its chain of transmission and text are not authentic. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the hypocrites, and this is the most similar statement, and it is supported by the statement of God Almighty: “And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites and among the people of Madinah are stubborn in hypocrisy. You do not know them. We know them.” And His statement: And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged. That is, no matter what. You spent in jihad, then it will be fully and completely repaid to you. For this reason, it was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: The reward of the dirham in the way of God is multiplied up to seven hundred times, as mentioned previously in the words of God the Almighty: “The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven ears, in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyah told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, my father told us, on the authority of his father, al-Ash’ath ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to command that charity should not be given except to the people of Islam, until the verse And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you was revealed, and then he commanded charity after that, to everyone who asked you from every religion, and this is also strange.
8:60: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not think O Muhammad that those who disbelieve have outstripped Us meaning that We have no power over them, but rather they are under the control of Our power and in the grip of Our will, so they cannot defeat Us, as God Almighty says: Or do those who do evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us? Evil is that which they judge. meaning that they think. God Almighty says: "Do not think that those who disbelieve can escape Us on earth. Their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination." God Almighty says: "Let not the movement of those who disbelieve throughout the land deceive you. A brief enjoyment. Then their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place." Then God Almighty commanded the preparation of war machines to fight them according to one's ability, possibility, and capacity, saying: And prepare against them whatever you are able meaning whatever you are able of power and steeds of war. Imam Ahmad said: Harun bin Maruf told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Abu Ali Thamamah bin Shafi, the brother of Uqbah bin Amir, that Uqbah ibn Amir heard him say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say while he was on the pulpit: Prepare for them whatever you are able of power. Indeed, power is archery. Indeed, power is archery. Narrated by Muslim, on the authority of Harun ibn Maruf, and Abu Dawud, on the authority of Saeed ibn Mansur, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la, all three of them on the authority of Abdullah ibn Wahb. This hadith has other chains of transmission, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Amir, including what was narrated by al-Tirmidhi on the authority of Salih ibn Kaysan, on the authority of a man on his authority. Imam Ahmad and the people of the Sunnah narrated on his authority that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shoot and ride, and to shoot is better than to ride. Imam Malik said on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih al-Samman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Horses are for three things: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden. As for the one who is rewarded, he is a man who ties them up in the way of God and lets them ride long distances in a meadow or garden, and whatever they hit in that meadow or garden is considered good deeds for him. If they cut their tracks and reach a hill or two, their tracks and dung are considered good deeds for him. If they pass by a river and drink from it, and he does not intend to water himself with it, that is considered good deeds for him, so they are a reward for that man. A man ties them up out of self-sufficiency and chastity, and does not forget God’s right over their necks or backs, so they are a cover for him. A man ties them up out of pride, showing off, and pride, so they are a burden for that man.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked about donkeys, and he said, “God has not revealed anything to me about them except this comprehensive and unique verse: ‘So whoever does an atom’s weight of good will see it. ’” * And whoever does an atom’s weight of evil will see it.” Narrated by Al-Bukhari and this is its wording, and Muslim, both of them from the hadith of Malik. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Al-Rakeen bin Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Hassan, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “Horses are of three types: a horse for the Most Merciful, a horse for Satan, and a horse for man. As for the horse of the Most Merciful, it is the one that is tied up in the way of God, so its fodder, dung, and urine are used - and he mentioned what God willed - as for the horse of Satan, it is the one that gambles or bets on it. As for the horse of man, it is the horse that a person ties up, seeking its belly, so it is a protection for him from poverty.” Most scholars have said that archery is better than riding a horse, and Imam Malik said that riding is better than archery, and the opinion of the majority is stronger due to the hadith, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj and Hisham told us: Laith told us: Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Ibn Shamasah, that Muawiyah bin Khadij passed by Abu Dharr while he was standing next to his horse, and asked him: What is wrong with this horse of yours? He said: I think that the prayer of this horse has been answered. He said: What is the prayer of an animal? He said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, there is no horse but that it prays every dawn, saying: O God, You have made me one of Your servants, and You have placed my provision in his hand, so make me more beloved to him than his family, his wealth, and his children. He said: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Abi Jaafar, Yazid bin Abi Habib told me, on the authority of Suwaid bin Qais, on the authority of Muawiyah bin Khadij, on the authority of Abu Dharr, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no Arabian horse but that it is called to prayer at every dawn, and it calls out with two supplications: It says: O God, You have given me authority over whom You have given authority over from among the children of Adam, so make me among the most beloved of his family and wealth to him - or - the most beloved of his family and wealth to him.” Narrated by Al-Nasa’i, on the authority of Amr bin Ali Al-Fallas, on the authority of Yahya Al-Qattan, on his authority. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq al-Tastari told us, Hisham ibn Ammar told us, Yahya ibn Hamza told us, al-Mut’am ibn al-Muqaddam al-San’ani told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan, that he said to Ibn al-Hanthaliyyah, meaning Sahl: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Goodness is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection, and their owners are helped by them. Whoever ties a horse in the way of God, the expenses for it will be like someone who extends his hand in charity and does not withdraw it.” There are many hadiths that have been narrated about the virtue of tying horses. In Sahih al-Bukhari, on the authority of Urwah ibn Abi al-Ja`d al-Barqi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Horses have good tied to their forelocks until the Day of Resurrection, reward and spoils. And his statement: You terrify with it means you frighten the enemy of God and your enemy meaning the infidels and others besides them. Mujahid said: He means Banu Qurayzah. Al-Suddi said: Knights. Sufyan al-Thawri said: Ibn Yaman said: They are the devils in the houses. A similar hadith has been narrated. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Utbah Ahmad ibn al-Faraj al-Himsi told us, Abu Haywah, meaning Shureih ibn Yazid al-Muqri told us, Saeed ibn Sinan told us, on the authority of Ibn Gharib, meaning Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Gharib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say regarding the statement of God Almighty: And others besides them whom you do not know, he said: They are the jinn. Al-Tabarani narrated it on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Duhaim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Shuaib, on the authority of Sinan ibn Saeed ibn Sinan, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abdullah ibn Gharib, with the same chain of transmission, and he added: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A house in which there is an old horse will not be ruined. This hadith is rejected, and its chain of transmission and text are not authentic. Muqatil ibn Hayyan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: They are the hypocrites, and this is the most similar statement, and it is supported by the statement of God Almighty: “And among those around you of the bedouins are hypocrites and among the people of Madinah are stubborn in hypocrisy. You do not know them. We know them.” And His statement: And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged. That is, no matter what. You spent in jihad, then it will be fully and completely repaid to you. For this reason, it was mentioned in the hadith narrated by Abu Dawud: The reward of the dirham in the way of God is multiplied up to seven hundred times, as mentioned previously in the words of God the Almighty: “The parable of those who spend their wealth in the way of God is that of a grain [of corn] which grows seven ears, in each ear is a hundred grains. And God multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And God is All-Encompassing and Knowing.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn al-Qasim ibn Atiyah told us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki told us, my father told us, on the authority of his father, al-Ash’ath ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to command that charity should not be given except to the people of Islam, until the verse And whatever you spend in the way of God will be fully repaid to you was revealed, and then he commanded charity after that, to everyone who asked you from every religion, and this is also strange.
8:61: God Almighty says: If you fear treachery from a people, then throw away their treaty with them on equal terms. If they continue to wage war against you and oppose you, then fight them. But if they incline that is, lean “towards peace” that is, reconciliation, truce and truce, then incline towards it that is, lean towards it and accept that from them. For this reason, when the polytheists asked for peace in the year of Al-Hudaybiyah, and for the war to be stopped between them and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for nine years, he agreed to that along with the other conditions they stipulated. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad bin Abi Bakr Al-Muqaddami told us, Fadil bin Sulayman, meaning Al-Numayri, told us, Muhammad bin Abi Yahya told us, on the authority of Iyas bin Amr Al-Aslami, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There will be a difference or a matter, so if you are able to make peace, then do so.” Mujahid said: It was revealed about Banu Qurayzah, and this is questionable, because the entire context is about the Battle of Badr, and mentioning it encompasses all of this. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Zayd bin Aslam, Ata Al-Khurasani, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: This verse was abrogated by the verse of the sword in Bara’ah: Fight those who do not believe in God or the Last Day, the verse, and this is also questionable, because the verse of Bara’ah contains the command to fight them if that is possible. However, if the enemy is numerous, then it is permissible to make peace with them, as this noble verse indicates, and as the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah. So there is no contradiction, abrogation or specification, and God knows best. And His saying, And put your trust in God, meaning, make peace with them and put your trust in God, for God will suffice you and support you, even if they intended to deceive you by the peace, so that they would strengthen themselves and prepare themselves. Then God is sufficient for you, meaning He alone is sufficient for you. Then He mentioned His favor upon him, through which He supported him from the believers, the Muhajireen and the Ansar, and said, It is He who supported you with His victory and with the believers * and united their hearts, meaning He united them in faith in you, and in obeying you, supporting you and assisting you. If you had spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, meaning because of the enmity and hatred between them, for the Ansar had many wars between them in the pre-Islamic period, between the Aws and the Khazraj, and matters that necessitated a chain of evil, until God cut that off with the light of faith, as God the Most High said, “And remember the favor of God upon you, when you were enemies and He united your hearts so that by His favor you became brothers, and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does God make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.” In the two Sahihs: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, addressed the Ansar regarding the spoils of Hunayn, he said to them: O group of Ansar, did I not find you astray and God guided you through me? And poor and God enriched you through me? And you were divided and God united you through me? Whenever he said something, they said, God and His Messenger are believers. That is why God, the Most High, said: “But God united them. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise.” That is, He is Exalted in Might, so He does not disappoint the hope of those who trust in Him. He is Wise in His actions and judgments. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Ali bin Bishr Al-Sayrafi Al-Qazwini informed us in our house, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qandili Al-Istrabadhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Nu’man Al-Saffar informed us, Maymun bin Al-Hakam informed us, Bakr bin Al-Sharud informed us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta’ifi, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Kinship is severed, and the favor of blessings is denied, and nothing has been seen like the closeness of the womb. Hearts, God Almighty says: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together. This is found in poetry: If a relative of yours makes a mistake and then deceives you and pretends to be self-sufficient, then he is not a relative. But the relative who, if you call him, answers, and throws at the enemy whom you throw He said: And from that is the saying of the one who said: I have accompanied people, then I have explored them and tested the reasons they reached. If kinship does not bring a sever closer, and if affection is the closest of reasons Al-Bayhaqi said: I do not know if this is connected to the words of Ibn Abbas or if it is from the words of someone who is less than him among the narrators. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i said on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, he heard him say: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together verse, he said: They are those who love one another for the sake of God. In another narration it was revealed about those who love one another for the sake of God. Narrated by al-Nasa’i and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, who said: It is authentic. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The ties of kinship are severed, and blessings are denied, and when God brings hearts together, nothing can move them. Then he recited: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together verse, also narrated by al-Hakim. Abu Amr al-Awza’i said: Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah told me on the authority of Mujahid, and I met him and he took my hand and said: When two people who love one another for the sake of God meet, and one of them takes the hand of the other and smiles at him, their sins fall away like the leaves of a tree. Abdah said: I said to him: This is easy. He said: Do not say that, for God says: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together. Abdah said: Then I knew that he was more knowledgeable than me. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Jazari, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Abi Mughith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: If two Muslims meet and shake hands, they will be forgiven. I said to Mujahid: Is it because of a handshake that they will be forgiven? Mujahid said: Didn’t you hear him say: If you spent all that is on earth, you could not bring their hearts together, but God brought them together. Al-Walid said to Mujahid: You know better than me. Talhah ibn Masraf narrated the same from Mujahid. Ibn Awn said from Umair ibn Ishaq, he said: We used to say that the first thing that will be lifted from people is love. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad Al-Tabarani, may God have mercy on him, said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar Al-Qawariri told us, Salim ibn Ghailan told us, I heard Ja’d Abu Uthman, Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi told me, from Salman Al-Farsi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a Muslim meets his Muslim brother and takes him by the hand, their sins fall from them, as leaves fall from a dry tree on a windy day, otherwise their sins will be forgiven even if they were like the foam of the seas.”

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Ali bin Bishr Al-Sayrafi Al-Qazwini informed us in our house, Abu Abdullah Muhammad bin Al-Hussein Al-Qandili Al-Istrabadhi informed us, Abu Ishaq Ibrahim bin Muhammad bin Al-Nu’man Al-Saffar informed us, Maymun bin Al-Hakam informed us, Bakr bin Al-Sharud informed us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Muslim Al-Ta’ifi, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Maysarah, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Kinship is severed, and the favor of blessings is denied, and nothing has been seen like the closeness of the womb. Hearts, God Almighty says: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together. This is found in poetry: If a relative of yours makes a mistake and then deceives you and pretends to be self-sufficient, then he is not a relative. But the relative who, if you call him, answers, and throws at the enemy whom you throw He said: And from that is the saying of the one who said: I have accompanied people, then I have explored them and tested the reasons they reached. If kinship does not bring a sever closer, and if affection is the closest of reasons Al-Bayhaqi said: I do not know if this is connected to the words of Ibn Abbas or if it is from the words of someone who is less than him among the narrators. Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i said on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud may God be pleased with him, he heard him say: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together verse, he said: They are those who love one another for the sake of God. In another narration it was revealed about those who love one another for the sake of God. Narrated by al-Nasa’i and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, who said: It is authentic. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Ibn Tawus on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The ties of kinship are severed, and blessings are denied, and when God brings hearts together, nothing can move them. Then he recited: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together verse, also narrated by al-Hakim. Abu Amr al-Awza’i said: Abdah ibn Abi Lubabah told me on the authority of Mujahid, and I met him and he took my hand and said: When two people who love one another for the sake of God meet, and one of them takes the hand of the other and smiles at him, their sins fall away like the leaves of a tree. Abdah said: I said to him: This is easy. He said: Do not say that, for God says: If you spent all that is in the earth, you could not bring their hearts together. Abdah said: Then I knew that he was more knowledgeable than me. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Jazari, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Abi Mughith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: If two Muslims meet and shake hands, they will be forgiven. I said to Mujahid: Is it because of a handshake that they will be forgiven? Mujahid said: Didn’t you hear him say: If you spent all that is on earth, you could not bring their hearts together, but God brought them together. Al-Walid said to Mujahid: You know better than me. Talhah ibn Masraf narrated the same from Mujahid. Ibn Awn said from Umair ibn Ishaq, he said: We used to say that the first thing that will be lifted from people is love. Al-Hafiz Abu Al-Qasim Sulayman ibn Ahmad Al-Tabarani, may God have mercy on him, said: Al-Husayn ibn Ishaq Al-Tastari told us, Ubayd God ibn Umar Al-Qawariri told us, Salim ibn Ghailan told us, I heard Ja’d Abu Uthman, Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi told me, from Salman Al-Farsi, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When a Muslim meets his Muslim brother and takes him by the hand, their sins fall from them, as leaves fall from a dry tree on a windy day, otherwise their sins will be forgiven even if they were like the foam of the seas.”
8:64: God Almighty urges His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the believers to fight and confront the enemies and duel their peers, and He informs them that He is sufficient for them, that is, He is sufficient for them, their supporter, and their backer against their enemy, even if their numbers are large and their reinforcements are frequent, even if the number of believers is small. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Othman bin Hakim told us, Ubaydullah bin Musa told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement: O Prophet, sufficient for you is God and those who follow you among the believers, he said: God is sufficient for you, and sufficient for those who testify with you. He said: And something similar was narrated on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani and Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid, and for this reason he said: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight, meaning urge them or command them to do so. And for this reason the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would urge people to fight, when they were in line and facing the enemy, as he said to his companions on the day of Badr when the polytheists approached in their number and their number: Stand up for a Paradise whose width is that of the heavens and the earth. Umair bin Al-Hammam said: Its width is that of the heavens and the earth? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes. He said: Good, good. He said: What made you say what you said, good, good? He said: I hope that I will be one of its people. He said: Then you are one of its people. The man came forward, broke the scabbard of his sword, took out some dates and began to eat from them, then threw the rest of them from his hand and said: If I live until I eat them, it will be a long life. Then he came forward and fought until he was killed, may God be pleased with him. It has been narrated on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Saeed bin Jubair that this verse was revealed when Umar bin Al-Khattab converted to Islam and completed forty years with him. There is a view on this, because this verse is Medinan, and Umar converted to Islam in Mecca after the migration to the land of Abyssinia, and before the migration to Medina, and God knows best. Then the Almighty said, giving good tidings to the believers and commanding them: “If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred. And if there are a hundred among you, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve,” each one by ten. Then this command was abrogated, but the good tidings remained. Abdullah bin Mubarak said: Jarir bin Hazim told us, Az-Zubayr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the verse If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, until God made it obligatory for them that not one out of ten should flee. Then the alleviation came, and He said: Now God has lightened your burden until His saying overcome two hundred. He said: God lightened their burden and decreased their patience, according to the amount He had lightened for them. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from the hadith of Ibn Mubarak. Saeed bin Mansour said: Sufyan told us on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, he said: It was written for them that twenty should not flee from two hundred, then God made it easier for them, and said: Now God has made it easier for you and He knows that there is weakness in you. So it is not appropriate for one hundred to flee from two hundred. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Ali bin Abdullah on the authority of Sufyan with something similar to it. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told me, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the Muslims, and they thought it was too much for twenty to fight two hundred, and one hundred thousand, so God made it easier for them and abrogated it with the other verse, and He said: Now God has made it easier for you and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if they were half of their enemy, it was not permissible for them to flee from their enemy, and if they were less than that, it was not obligatory for them to fight them, and it was permissible for them to avoid them. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi narrated something similar to that on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ata’, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Zaid bin Aslam, Ata’ Al-Khurasani, Ad-Dahhak, and others like that. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr bin Mardawayh narrated: From the hadith of Al-Musayyab bin Sharik, from Ibn Awn, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, regarding His statement, If there are twenty among you, patient, they will overcome two hundred, he said, “It was revealed about us, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.” Al-Hakim narrated in his Mustadrak from the hadith of Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’, from Nafi’, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, Now God has lightened your burden and He knows that there is weakness in you, then he raised his head and said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it.

8:67: Imam Ahmad said: Ali bin Hashim narrated to us, on the authority of Humayd, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted the people about the prisoners on the day of Badr, and he said, God has given you power over them. So Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up and said, O Messenger of God, strike off their heads. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and said, O people, God has given you power over them, and they were your brothers yesterday. So Umar stood up and said, O Messenger of God, strike off their heads. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away from him. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned and said, The people have the same. Then Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, stood up and said, O Messenger of God, we think that you should pardon them and accept their ransom. He said, "Then the grief that was in the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went away, and he pardoned them and accepted their ransom." He said, And God Almighty revealed, 'Had it not been for a previous decree from God, a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you took.' And the hadith of Ibn Abbas was mentioned at the beginning of the surah in Sahih Muslim narrated something similar to this. Al-A’mash said: On the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: When the day of Badr came, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you say about these prisoners? Abu Bakr said: “O Messenger of God, they are your people and your family. Let them stay and ask them to repent, perhaps God will accept their repentance.” Umar said: O Messenger of God, they lied to you and expelled you, so bring them forward and strike off their necks. Abdullah ibn Rawahah said: “O Messenger of God, you are in a valley with much firewood. Set the valley on fire and throw them into it.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent and did not answer them at all. Then he got up and entered. Some people said: He will accept the words of Abu Bakr. Some people said: He will accept the words of Umar. Some people said: He will accept the words of Abdullah ibn Rawahah. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them and said: God softens the hearts of men until they are softer than milk, and God hardens the hearts of men in it until they are harder than stones. Your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Abraham, peace be upon him, who said: Whoever follows me is of me, and whoever disobeys me - indeed, You are Forgiving and Merciful. Your example, O Abu Bakr, is like that of Jesus, peace be upon him, who said: If You punish them - indeed, they are Your servants, and if You forgive them - indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise. Your example, O Umar, is like that of Moses, peace be upon him, who said: Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment. Your example, O Umar, is like that of Noah, peace be upon him, who said: My Lord, leave not a single inhabitant of the disbelievers on the earth. You are dependents, and none of them will be freed except by ransom or the beheading of a neck. Ibn Mas`ud said: I said: O Messenger of God, except for Suhayl ibn Bayda, for he mentions Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent. I have never seen myself more afraid of stones falling from the sky than I was on that day, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: And he said: Except for Suhayl ibn Bayda, then God the Almighty revealed: It is not for a Prophet to have captives until the end of the verse. It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Abu Mu’awiyah from al-A’mash, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, and he said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated from Abdullah ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them both, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. In this chapter, from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and Ibn Mardawayh also narrated, and the wording is his, and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak, from the hadith of Ubaydullah ibn Musa, Israel told us from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Mujahid from Ibn Umar, who said: When the captives were taken prisoner on the day of Badr, al-Abbas was taken prisoner among those taken prisoner, a man from the Ansar took him prisoner. He said: The Ansar threatened to kill him, and that reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I did not sleep last night because of my uncle al-Abbas, and the Ansar claimed that they fought him. So Umar said to him: Did you kill them? He said, Yes. So, Umar came to the Ansar and said to them, Send Al-Abbas. They said, No, by God, we will not send him. Umar said to them, "What if the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with him?" They said, "If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is pleased with him, then take him." So Umar took him and when he was in his hand, he said to him, "O Abbas, become Muslim, for by God, your becoming Muslim is dearer to me than Al-Khattab becoming Muslim. This was only because I saw that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was pleased with your becoming Muslim." He said, "The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, consulted Abu Bakr about them, and Abu Bakr said, "They are your clan," so send them. Umar consulted him and said, "Kill them." So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ransomed them, and God revealed, "It is not for a prophet to have captives. Al-Hakim said, Its chain of transmission is authentic, but they did not include it." Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Hisham ibn Hassan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the day of Badr and said: The best of your companions regarding the prisoners, if they wish ransom, or if they wish killing, on the condition that a similar number of them be killed the following year. They said: Ransom and some of us will be killed. Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa’i and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih from the hadith of al-Thawri with it. This is a very strange hadith. Ibn Awn said on the authority of Ubaydah, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said regarding the prisoners on the day of Badr: If you wish, kill them, and if you wish, ransom them, and enjoy the ransom, and a number of you will be martyred. He said: The last of the seventy was Thabit ibn Qays, who was killed on the day of Yamamah, may God be pleased with him. Some of them narrated this hadith on the authority of Ubaydah as a mursal, and God knows best. Muhammad ibn Ishaq said on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It is not for a prophet to have captives, and he recited until he reached the verse: A great punishment. He said: The spoils of Badr before He made them lawful for them, saying: Were it not that I do not punish those who disobey Me until I come to them, you would have been afflicted with a great punishment for what you have taken. And this is what Ibn Abi Nujayh narrated: on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-A’mash said: It was previously narrated from him that he would not punish anyone who witnessed Badr, and something similar was narrated from Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ata’, and Shu’bah said on the authority of Abu Hashim on the authority of Mujahid Had it not been for a previous decree from God meaning for them with forgiveness and something similar, on the authority of Sufyan Al-Thawri, may God have mercy on him, and Ali ibn Abi Talhah said: on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement Had it not been for a previous decree from God meaning in the first Mother of the Book, that the spoils and captives are lawful for you a great punishment would have afflicted you for what you have taken of the captives a great punishment would have afflicted you God Almighty said: So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good Al-Baqarah 2:17. And likewise Al-Awfi narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and something similar was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurairah, Ibn Masoud, Saeed bin Jubair, Ata’, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Qatada and Al-A’mash also, that what is meant is Had it not been for a previous decree from God for this nation to make spoils permissible, and this is the choice of Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him. And he cites as evidence for this statement what they narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was given five things that were not given to any of the prophets before me: I was aided by terror for a distance of a month’s journey, the earth was made a place of prostration and purification for me, spoils of war were made lawful for me while they were not made lawful for anyone before me, and I was given intercession. A prophet would be sent to his own people, but I was sent to all of mankind.” Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Spoils of war were not lawful for black people except us. That is why God Almighty said: So eat of what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good [al-Bukhari and Muslim], and at that time they took ransom from the captives. So I informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of my conversion to Islam and asked him to account for the twenty ounces that had been taken from me, but he refused, so God replaced them with twenty slaves, all of them merchants, and my money was in his hand. We will advise you regarding our people. Then God revealed, If God knows good in your hearts, He will give you better than what He took from you, faith and belief, He will replace for you better than what He took from you, and forgive you, the polytheism you were upon. He said, “Al-Abbas used to say, ‘I do not like this verse not to be revealed about us, even though I have the world. He said, ‘He will give you better than what He took from you,’ so He gave me a hundred times better than what He took from me. He said, ‘and forgive you,’ and I hope that He has forgiven me.” Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, “Al-Abbas was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so he ransomed himself with forty ounces of gold. Al-Abbas said when this verse was recited, ‘God, the Almighty, has given me two qualities, and I do not like to have the world for them: I was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so I ransomed myself with forty ounces, so He gave me forty slaves. I hope for the forgiveness that God, the Almighty, has promised us.’” Qatada said in his interpretation of this verse: It was mentioned to us that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, was presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had performed ablution for the noon prayer, he was not given anything that day. Complaining and not depriving a beggar, and he did not pray that day until he distributed it, so he ordered Al-Abbas to take from it and scoop it up, and Al-Abbas used to say: This is better than what was taken from us, and I hope for forgiveness. And Yaqub bin Sufyan said: Amr bin Asim told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Humaid bin Hilal, who said: Ibn Al-Hadrami sent eighty thousand to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Bahrain. He had never received more money than this, neither before nor after. He said: It was scattered on a mat and the call to prayer was made. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and stood standing over the money, and the people of the mosque came, and on that day there was no number or weight, it was only an abundance, and Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib came and scooped it up in a cloak on him, and he went to stand up but he could not. He said: He raised his head to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, raise it up for me. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, smiled until his laughter or his fangs came out and said to him: Prepare a portion of the money and do what you can. He said: So he did and Al-Abbas kept saying: As for one of the two things that God promised us, we have fulfilled, and we do not know what God will do with the other: O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives (al-Baqarah 2:14) Then he said: This is better than what was taken from us and I do not know what God will do with the other. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to look at that money until not a dirham of it remained and he did not send a dirham to his family. Then he came to the prayer and prayed. Another hadith on this - Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Tayyib Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Saidi informed us, Muhammad bin Issam informed us, Hafs bin Abdullah informed us, Ibrahim bin Tahman informed us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought money from Bahrain, so he said, Sprinkle it in my mosque. He said, “It was the most money that was brought to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he went out to pray and did not pay attention to it, and when he finished praying, he came and sat next to him, and he did not see anyone except that he gave him to him, when Al-Abbas came to him and said, “O Messenger of God, give me, for I have redeemed myself and I have redeemed Aqeel.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him, Take it. So he threw it into his garment, then he tried to carry it, but he could not, so he said, Tell someone to lift it up to me. He said, No. He said, Then lift it up to me. He said, No. So he scattered some of it, then carried it on his shoulder, then left, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept following it with his eyes until it disappeared from him, amazed by his eagerness, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not get up. And then a dirham from it, and Al-Bukhari narrated it in places in his Sahih as a comment with the formula of certainty, saying: And Ibrahim bin Tahman said, and he quotes it and in some contexts it is more complete than this. And His statement, And if they intend to betray you, they have already betrayed God before, meaning, And if they intend to betray you, in what they showed you of words, they have already betrayed God before, meaning before Badr by disbelieving in Him, and He gave them power over them, meaning over the captives on the day of Badr, and God is Knowing and Wise, meaning, He is Knowing of his actions and Wise in them. Qatadah said, It was revealed about Abdullah bin Saad bin Abi Sarh the scribe when he apostatized and joined the polytheists. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ata’ al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: It was revealed about Abbas and his companions when they said, ‘We will advise you against our people.’ Al-Suddi interpreted it in a general sense, which is more comprehensive and clearer, and God knows best.
8:71: Muhammad bin Ishaq said: Al-Abbas bin Abdullah bin Mughaffal told me on the authority of some of his family on the authority of Abdullah bin Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said on the day of Badr: “I have come to know that some people from Banu Hashim and others have been forced out, and they have no need to fight us. So whoever among you meets one of them - meaning from Banu Hashim - do not kill him, and whoever meets Abu al-Bukhtari bin Hisham do not kill him, and whoever meets al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib do not kill him, for he was only forced out.” Abu Hudhayfah bin Utbah said: Should we kill our fathers, sons, brothers, and tribesmen and leave al-Abbas? By God, if I meet him, I will muzzle him with the sword. This reached the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said to Umar bin al-Khattab: O Abu Hafs - Umar said: “By God, this is the first day that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called me Abu Hafs - should the face of the uncle of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, be struck with the sword?” Then Umar said, O Messenger of God, give me permission to strike off his head, for by God he has become a hypocrite. Abu Hudhayfah used to say after that, By God, I do not feel safe from that word that I said, and I am still afraid of it, unless God expiates it for me with martyrdom. So he was killed as a martyr on the day of Yamamah, may God be pleased with him. And on his authority, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the night awake on the day of Badr, and the prisoners were confined in chains, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, spent the first part of the night awake, and his companions said to him, O Messenger of God, why do you not sleep? Al-Abbas had taken a man from the Ansar captive, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I heard the groaning of my uncle Al-Abbas in his chains, so release him. So he remained silent, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: The most ransomed of the prisoners on the day of Badr was Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib, because he was a wealthy man, so he ransomed himself with one hundred ounces of gold. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Musa bin Uqbah, Ibn Shihab said: Anas bin Malik told us that some men from the Ansar said: O Messenger of God, give us permission to leave the ransom of our nephew, Al-Abbas. He said: No, by God, you will not leave a single dirham of it. Yunus bin Bakir said on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq on the authority of Yazid bin Ruman on the authority of Urwah on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of a group whom he named, they said: Quraysh sent to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ransom their prisoners, so each group ransomed its prisoner for whatever they pleased. Al-Abbas said: O Messenger of God, I was a Muslim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God knows best about your Islam. If it is as you say, then God will reward you. As for your outward appearance, it was against us, so ransom yourself, your nephew Nawfal bin Al-Harith bin Abdul Muttalib, and Aqeel bin Abi Talib bin Abdul Muttalib, and your ally Utbah bin Amr, the brother of Banu Al-Harith bin Fihr.” He said: I do not have that, O Messenger of God. He said: Then where is the money that you and Umm Al-Fadl buried? I said to her: If I am found on this journey of mine, then this money that I buried belongs to Banu Al-Fadl, Abdullah, and Qatham. He said: By God, O Messenger of God, I know that you are the Messenger of God. This is something that no one knows except me and Umm Al-Fadl. So calculate for me, O Messenger of God, what I have.” You took from me twenty ounces of money that I had with me, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, No, that is something that God Almighty has given us from you. So he ransomed himself, his two nephews, and his ally, so God Almighty revealed, “O Prophet, say to those in your hands of captives, ‘If God knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what He has taken from you and forgive you. And God is Forgiving and Merciful.’” Al-Abbas said, “So God gave me in place of the twenty ounces in Islam twenty slaves, each of whom had money in his hand to strike with, along with what I hope for from God Almighty’s forgiveness. Ibn Ishaq also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh on the authority of Ata’ on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse in a manner similar to what was mentioned above.” Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Ibn Wakee` told us, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Al-Abbas said: Concerning this verse, It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a great slaughter on the land, was revealed. So I informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, of my conversion to Islam and asked him to account for the twenty ounces that had been taken from me, but he refused, so God replaced them with twenty slaves, all of them merchants, and my money was in his hand. Ibn Ishaq also said: Al-Kalbi told me, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah bin Ribab, who said: Al-Abbas bin Abdul Muttalib used to say, “By God, when I mentioned my conversion to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he mentioned a hadith similar to the one before it.” Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Ata` Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, O Prophet, say to those of the captives who are in your hands, Abbas and his companions said: They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We believe in what you have brought and we bear witness that you are the Messenger of God. We will advise you regarding our people. Then God revealed, If God knows good in your hearts, He will give you better than what He took from you, faith and belief, He will replace for you better than what He took from you, and forgive you, the polytheism you were upon. He said, “Al-Abbas used to say, ‘I do not like this verse not to be revealed about us, even though I have the world. He said, ‘He will give you better than what He took from you,’ so He gave me a hundred times better than what He took from me. He said, ‘and forgive you,’ and I hope that He has forgiven me.” Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse, “Al-Abbas was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so he ransomed himself with forty ounces of gold. Al-Abbas said when this verse was recited, ‘God, the Almighty, has given me two qualities, and I do not like to have the world for them: I was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, so I ransomed myself with forty ounces, so He gave me forty slaves. I hope for the forgiveness that God, the Almighty, has promised us.’” Qatada said in his interpretation of this verse: It was mentioned to us that when the wealth of Bahrain, eighty thousand, was presented to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he had performed ablution for the noon prayer, he was not given anything that day. And Yaqub bin Sufyan said: Amr bin Asim told us, Sulayman bin Al-Mughira told us, on the authority of Humaid bin Hilal, who said: Ibn Al-Hadrami sent eighty thousand to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Bahrain. Another hadith on this - Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz informed us, Abu Al-Tayyib Muhammad bin Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Saidi informed us, Muhammad bin Issam informed us, Hafs bin Abdullah informed us, Ibrahim bin Tahman informed us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Suhaib, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was brought money from Bahrain, so he said, Sprinkle it in my mosque. So he threw it into his garment, then he tried to carry it, but he could not, so he said, Tell someone to lift it up to me. He said, No. He said, Then lift it up to me. He said, No. So he scattered some of it, then carried it on his shoulder, then left, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept following it with his eyes until it disappeared from him, amazed by his eagerness, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not get up. 8:72: God the Almighty mentioned the categories of believers and divided them into Muhajireen who left their homes and wealth and came to support God and His Messenger and establish His religion and spent their wealth and lives in that, and Ansar who were the Muslims from the people of Medina at that time who sheltered their Muhajireen brothers in their homes and helped them in their wealth and supported God and His Messenger by fighting with them. These are friends of one another, meaning each of them has more right to the other than anyone else. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established brotherhood between the Muhajireen and the Ansar, two of them being brothers, so they would inherit from each other by inheritance that took precedence over kinship until God the Almighty abrogated that with inheritances. This was proven in Sahih al-Bukhari on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it was narrated by al-Awfi and Ali ibn Abi Talhah on his authority. Mujahid, Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Qatadah and more than one said: Imam Ahmad said: Waki’ narrated to us on the authority of Sharik on the authority of Asim on the authority of Abu Wa’il on the authority of Jarir, who is Ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Muhajireen and the Ansar are friends of one another. The freed slaves of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqeef are allies of one another until the Day of Resurrection. This was reported by Ahmad alone. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said: Sufyan told us, Ikrimah told us, meaning Ibn Ibrahim al-Azdi, Asim told us, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The Muhajireen and the Ansar, and the freed slaves of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqeef are allies of one another in this world and the hereafter. This is how it was narrated in the Musnad of Abdullah Ibn Mas’ud. God and His Messenger praised the Muhajireen and the Ansar in more than one verse in His Book. He said: “And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them with good conduct - God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him and He has prepared for them gardens beneath which rivers flow” 3:10. He also said: God has forgiven the Prophet and the Muhajireen and the Ansar who followed him during the time of hardship 3:10. He also said: “For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from God and approval and supporting God and His Messenger - those are the truthful. And those who were established in the home and in the faith before them love those who emigrated to them and find not in their hearts any need for what the Muhajireen were given and give them preference over themselves, even though they were in need” 3:10. The best that has been said about His statement: and find not in their hearts any need for what the Muhajireen were given is that they do not envy them for the bounty that God gave them for their migration. The apparent meaning of the verses is to give precedence to the Muhajireen over the Ansar, and this is a matter agreed upon by the scholars and they do not differ on that. For this reason, Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman said: Al-Khaliq Al-Bazzar in his Musnad: Muhammad bin Muammar told us, Muslim bin Ibrahim told us, Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Ali bin Zaid, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave me the choice between migration and support, so I chose migration. Then he said: We do not know it except from this aspect, and the Almighty’s saying: And those who believed and did not emigrate - you have no guardianship over them Hamzah read their guardianship with the kasra, and the rest with the fatha, and they are one like the indication and the indication of anything until they emigrate This is the third category of believers, and they are those who believed but did not emigrate, but rather stayed in their deserts, so these have no share in the spoils, nor in a fifth of them except for what they were present in the fighting. Ahmad said: Waki` narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Alqamah bin Marthad, on the authority of Sulayman bin Buraidah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Yazid bin Al-Khasib Al-Aslami, may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent a commander over a raid or an army, he would advise him in private to fear God and to treat those Muslims with him well, and he would say: “Fight in the name of God in the way of God, fight those who disbelieve in God, if you meet your enemy from the polytheists, then call them to one of three characteristics - or qualities - and whichever of them they respond to, then accept them and refrain from them. Call them to Islam, and if they respond, then accept them and refrain from them. Then call them to move from their home to the home of the immigrants, and inform them that if they do that, they will have what the immigrants have, and that they are subject to what the immigrants are subject to. If they refuse and choose their home, then inform them that they will be like the Bedouin Muslims, and the ruling of God that applies to the believers will apply to them, and they will have no share in the spoils and booty, unless they fight with the Muslims, then They refused, so call them to pay the jizyah. If they respond, then accept it from them and refrain from fighting them. If they refuse, then seek help from God and fight them. This is reported only by Muslim, and he has other additions. His statement, “And if they seek help of you in religion, then you must help them” 1:13. God the Almighty says, “And if these Bedouins, who did not emigrate to fight for religion against an enemy of theirs, seek help from you, then help them, for it is obligatory upon you to help them, because they are your brothers in religion, unless they seek help from you against a people of the disbelievers, between you and them is a treaty, that is, a truce for a period. So do not break your covenant and do not break your oaths with those with whom you have made a treaty.” This was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him.
8:73: When God Almighty mentioned that the believers are allies of one another, He severed allegiance between them and the infidels, as Al-Hakim said in his Mustadrak: Muhammad bin Salih bin Hani’ told us, Abu Saeed Yahya bin Mansour Al-Harawi told us, Muhammad bin Aban told us, Muhammad bin Yazid and Sufyan bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein, on the authority of Amr bin Othman, on the authority of Usamah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “People of two religions do not inherit from each other, and a Muslim does not inherit from an infidel, nor an infidel from a Muslim - then he recited - ‘And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do so, there will be turmoil on earth and great corruption.’” Then Al-Hakim said: Its chain of transmission is authentic, and they did not include it. I said: The hadith is in the two Sahihs on the authority of Usamah bin Zaid, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A Muslim does not inherit from a disbeliever, nor does a disbeliever inherit from a Muslim. And in the Musnad and the Sunan, on the authority of Amr bin Shuaib, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: People of two different religions do not inherit from each other. And Al-Tirmidhi said: It is good and authentic. And Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Muhammad told us, on the authority of Mu`ammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took a man who had entered Islam and said: Establish the prayer, pay the zakat, make the pilgrimage to the House, and fast Ramadan, and you will not see the fire of a polytheist except that you are at war with him. And this is mursal from this source, and it has been narrated connected from another source on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I am innocent of every Muslim among the polytheists, then he said: Their two fires will not be seen. Abu Dawud said at the end of the Book of Jihad: Muhammad ibn Dawud ibn Sufyan told us, Yahya ibn Hassan told us, Sulayman ibn Musa Abu Dawud told us, Ja`far ibn Sa`d ibn Samurah ibn Jundub told us, Khabib ibn Sulayman told me, on the authority of Samurah ibn Jundub: As for what follows, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has intercourse with a polytheist and lives with him is like him. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh mentioned from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma`il, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Hurmuz, on the authority of Muhammad and Sa`id ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Abu Hatim al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If someone comes to you whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him, otherwise there will be great turmoil and corruption on earth. They said: O Messenger of God, even if that is the case? He said: If someone comes to you whose religion and character you are pleased with, then marry him, three times. Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Hatim ibn Isma`il in a similar manner. Then it was narrated from the hadith of Abdul Hamid ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ibn `Ajlan, on the authority of Abu Wathima al-Nadri, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah. May God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If someone comes to you whose character and religion please you, then marry him. If you do not do so, there will be tribulation on earth and widespread corruption.” The meaning of his statement, If you do not do so, there will be tribulation on earth and widespread corruption, is that if you do not avoid the polytheists and befriend the believers, otherwise tribulation will occur among the people, which is confusion and mixing of the believers with the disbelievers, and widespread, widespread corruption will occur among the people.
8:74: When God the Almighty mentioned the ruling of the believers in this world, He followed it with mentioning their wealth in the Hereafter, so He informed about them with the reality of faith as mentioned in the beginning of the Surah and that He the Almighty will reward them with forgiveness and pardon for sins if they exist, and with generous provision which is good, abundant, pure, noble, permanent, and continuous forever, never interrupted or ended, never getting tired or bored because of its goodness and variety. Then He mentioned that those who follow them in this world based on what they were upon of faith and righteous deeds will be with them in the Hereafter, as He said, And the first to foretake al-Anfal 2:17 and He said, And those who came after them al-Anfal 2:17. In the agreed upon hadith, rather the mutawatir hadith from authentic chains of transmission, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said, A person will be with those he loves. In another hadith, Whoever loves a people is one of them. In another narration, He will be gathered with them. Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Jarir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Muhajireen and the Ansar are allies of one another, and the freed slaves of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqeef are allies of one another until the Day of Resurrection. Sharik said: We were told by Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Hilal, on the authority of Jarir, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ahmad was the only one to narrate it from these two sources. As for the Almighty’s saying: And those of kinship are more worthy of one another in the Book of God, that is, in the ruling of God, what is meant by His saying: And those of kinship is not the specificity of what the scholars of inheritance laws apply to relatives who do not have a share and are not agnates, but rather they are related by an heir such as the maternal aunt, paternal uncle, paternal aunt, daughters’ children, sisters’ children, and the like, as some of them may claim and cite the verse as evidence and believe that it is explicit in the issue. Rather, the truth is that the verse is general and includes all relatives, as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and more than one have stated that it abrogates inheritance by oath and brotherhood, by which they used to inherit at first. Based on this, it includes those of kinship by the specific name, and whoever does not inherit from them cites evidence, the strongest of which is the hadith: Indeed, God has given every person with a right his right, so there is no bequest for an heir. They said: If he had a right, he would have had a share named in the Book of God, but since that was not the case, he would not have been an heir, and God knows best. The last interpretation of Surat Al-Anfal. Praise and thanks be to God, and upon Him we rely, and He is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.
8:75: When God the Almighty mentioned the ruling of the believers in this world, He followed it with mentioning their wealth in the Hereafter, so He informed about them with the reality of faith as mentioned in the beginning of the Surah and that He the Almighty will reward them with forgiveness and pardon for sins if they exist, and with generous provision which is good, abundant, pure, noble, permanent, and continuous forever, never interrupted or ended, never getting tired or bored because of its goodness and variety. Then He mentioned that those who follow them in this world based on what they were upon of faith and righteous deeds will be with them in the Hereafter, as He said, And the first to foretake al-Anfal 2:17 and He said, And those who came after them al-Anfal 2:17. In the agreed upon hadith, rather the mutawatir hadith from authentic chains of transmission, on the authority of the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said, A person will be with those he loves. In another hadith, Whoever loves a people is one of them. In another narration, He will be gathered with them. Imam Ahmad said: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Jarir, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Muhajireen and the Ansar are allies of one another, and the freed slaves of Quraysh and the freed slaves of Thaqeef are allies of one another until the Day of Resurrection.
